name: Central Hobart Historic Cottage
description:
This renovated 1885 house has fantastic views & is an easy walk to city centre, or a stroll to the North Hobart cafe/restaurant strip.

It is a vegetarian household, so if you're a carnivore you'll need to engage your inner vego while at home :-)
neighborhood_overview: This part of West Hobart is heritage listed and one of the oldest parts of Hobart. It is very central, being on the edge of the CBD. There are many cafes, bars and restaurants nearby, with the cafe/restaurant strip in Elizabeth Street North Hobart a short walk away, and Salamanca a 20 minute walk. The renowned Hill Street Grocer is a 5 minute walk away if you want to stock up on quality food stuffs (they also sell prepared heat-and-eat meals), and Smolt Kitchen, Pigeon Whole Bakery Cafe & Room for a Pony are all great breakfast places and just a short stroll away.
host_about:
I am an artist/arts educator, and was a Lecturer at the School of Creative Arts & Media, UTAS, from 1999 - 2021. I now run my own little art school in the city.

Having felt like I was running an informal B&B for friends and family, I  decided I may as well offer my home and hospitality to other travelers. I've been an AirBnB host for 13 years, and it has been a wonderful experience!

I am an artist, and animal advocate, and I love vegan cooking.

host_about:
From London originally, now living here in Tasmania.
Love animals, nature, art, music and reading philosophy.  Still working on my second book The CANdida CANcer CONnection. The title of my first book is 'The Irritable Brain Syndrome'.
Love breathing the beautiful fresh air here in Tasmania and listening the the many different birds that visit during the seasons of the year.  My favourites are the swallows that visit every year, building their nests, teaching their young to fly!  And the eagles that cruise around on the winds, high up in the sky. That's awesome to see :)
If you like wallabies, possums, echidnas and rabbits, there is plenty of them around dawn and dusk!  They seem to like my place and also the vegetation! I have to keep an eye on my vegetable patch :)

name: Anderson Suite, The Ark Stanley, Guest House
description:
Including cooked breakfast, private ensuite, free wi-fi & off-street parking.
The Anderson Suite - One of five queen suites at The Ark Stanley B&B, with remote control heating/cooling, tv, cd/dvd, fridge, welcome supplies, toaster, kettle, coffee machine. French-inspired decor, privacy blinds, Sheridan sheets, towels and bathrobes. Ensuite has large shower with luxurious satinjet showerhead, heated floor including heated pebble floor in shower area, heated towel rail and quality amenities.
neighborhood_overview: We are positioned directly opposite Tatlows Beach - our guests are fortunate enough to hear the water lapping at the shore from their rooms.  We are also within walking distance of the majority of the town’s attractions and also positioned at the base of The Nut (the plug of an extinct volcano standing approximately 150 metres high which formation was sighted by Bass & Flinders on their historic circumnavigation of Tasmania in 1798) whereby our guests have a birds-eye view of this most famous attraction.  We are also in close proximity to Highfield House (a favoured location for wedding events), affording the discerning bride the opportunity to select a luxurious location for that special occasion.
host_about: Hi, My name is Rhonda and I recently relocated with my husband from Melbourne to lovely Tasmania where I operate our guest house  - The Ark Stanley and Noah's Luxury B&B.   I love meeting and greeting people, cooking, reading and renovating houses.  While living in Melbourne we worked full time in our own small business, specialising in security.  As such we are both very security conscious and trustworthy.   I was born in Australia, while my husband is Swedish, and we have three grown children.  Neither of us smoke, we drink a little, love all food, and as such we love dining out and travelling so we can experience new tastes and adventures.  We are very tidy people, we enjoy animals and live with our cat Oscar.  We are healthy and enjoy life, and of course our grandchildren!

That said it is uphill and for some (fitness depending) that will still be a slog to walk or ride up, but there is a steep approach directly from town and a more gentle approach around the hill too.

description: Stylish vintage beach house opposite the beach. Free wifi, wood fire heater, spacious, sunny and clean. Enjoy our famous record collection and large deck. Ideally located for swimming, walking, fishing, exploring other towns, or just relaxing …  Stay in one of the last remaining owner-built 'shacks' at Sisters Beach.
neighborhood_overview:
Sisters Beach House is one of the last remaining original beach houses in Sisters Beach, a small beach side community located inside Rocky Cape National Park. The integrity and authenticity of the house, and unfenced garden, conjure up memories of old-school beach holidays (with all the comforts). The beach house is an oasis inside a much larger oasis of National Park walking tracks and kilometres of secluded beaches.

The Aboriginal name for Rocky Cape is Tangdimmaa which was once home to the Raverloihenna people whose caves can still be found here. We invite guests to consider the significance and cultural heritage of Tangdimmaa.

We acknowledge and pay respect to the Tasmanian Aboriginal people as the traditional and original owners of this land and acknowledge their Elders – past, present and emerging.
host_about: I'm a Melburnian who likes to travel and experience living like a local. Occasionally I save stranded whales. I'm a clean and respectful guest when I travel, and welcome the same of guests who stay at Sisters Beach House.

description:

With spectacular views overlooking the wide flowing Tamar River it is the perfect space to enjoy some relaxing days and amazing sunsets. Also some wildlife is bouncing around the Studio at night.

host_about:
Karin: 1987 my family and I moved from Germany to this beautiful spot in the Tamar Valley and lived here ever since. 
I have travelled extensively throughout Europe, USA, Scandinavia, Africa and Australia and experienced a lot of accommodation places throughout. That’ why I know what a traveller is looking for. We opened our studio apartment to meet lovely people from all over the world and share our little paradise with them. 
After 10 years working as an Accounts Officer in the hospitality industry I have now resigned from my job to fully commit myself in our own small business Terra-Preta Developments helping to spread the word about BIOCHAR. I am still working in the accounts and administration, but I also help to produce “Frank’s Char” and promoting it through nurseries and weekend Markets. I believe biochar has got huge potential and will be a growing industry in the future.
In my free time I love spending time with my grandchildren and socializing with family and friends. Also I enjoy gardening, bushwalking, photography, patchwork & quilting, Pilates, dancing, and when time allows I love cooking my own bread & delicious cakes, also preserving our own fruit and vegetables.  

Frank: It is now about 36 years when I first visited Tasmania to explore the Island and  the potential opportunities to become part of the Community.
I was simply stunned by the vista from the Brady's Lookout Reserve now just up the hill from us. 
Little did I know that about 2 and a half years later would we  be able to move into our new home with plenty of land to grow things and provide the lifestyle with pets and farm animals that our then little children would have to look after.
What a life!
We planted fruit trees as soon as the season allowed us to. Now we have a great mix of stone-fruits such as Cherries, Apricots, Peaches, Plumes, Prunes; then the pip-fruits such as various apples and pears.
The Vegetable Garden is providing many good things apart from the greens, asparagus, also soft fruits such as Raspberries and Strawberries during December and Currants in January.
I have also established a Hazelnut Grove since 1989 that now covers nearly one third of the property and the nuts are ready for harvest from about late February. 
No chemical spray is used here and no artificial fertilisers either. 
For the last 14 years I am involved in research, production and use of Biochar,
Bio = Greek for life, means that using char-(coal) to foster life in above & below ground and in water. Effective climate positive carbon action. 
I am very active in establishing the understanding of the potential of Biochar in healthy soil development, horticulture, aquaculture and farming. There are very interesting opportunities to be explored with anyone interested in caring for the land, soil health, carbon sequestration and renewable bio-energy from what is often considered organic 'waste', also called 'unloved biomass'. 
My professional background is in ecological forest management and training of responsible forest management principles.
My passion is in local community action for a better Tasmania, for short, medium and long term, inter-generational benefit. I am linked up with many organisations that care for the environment and the people across the Island, the Country and other continents. 
My love is for Karin, my dear wife of 40 years and the whole family, our children and grandchildren - that keeps me going. Tasmania is home for us. 
Since we have opened the studio apartment I have had the pleasure to meet some fascinating people from around the Country and around the World.

neighborhood_overview: As Tasmania's most important historic town, Richmond is one of the state's most popular destinations, the perfect base for exploring Tasmania's South East. name: Traditional Bed and Breakfast
description: Birdwing in-house bed and breakfast is nestled in our large garden which is surrounded by bush. The lovely room has its private entrance. As the the only guests you can relax here and use us as the base from which to explore the north of Tasmania.
host_about:
We have recently retired and love living here in our home in the country.  Sixteen years ago we chose to live in the beautiful Deloraine area, a vibrant and artistic community. Fritz belongs to a choir and I am involved in the local arts group as well as being a guide in the art gallery in Launceston.
On our 30 acres which includes a large rambling garden and natural bush, we have chooks and some sheep and two loved and fairly well behaved dogs.
Fritz has worked in Papua new Guinea most of his working life, mainly in community development, and I lived and worked with him for a number of years. We loved working in that interesting country. However it is a joy for us to be both here at Birdwing and opening our small bed and breakfast business. This was a dream we have had for many years and now that we are, we are loving meeting people and sharing our place with them.  Annie enjoys cooking so we provide delicious breakfasts using local food. We both love gardening and being outdoors; reading by the fire in winter seems a delightful indulgence!

name: Table House Farm -Luxury villa, secluded beach
description: Table House is a beautiful clifftop villa on Table House Farm on Table Cape just out of Wynyard in North West Tasmania.  With grand spaces inside and out it was designed especially to accommodate couples or families gathering together for special occasions. Enjoy views from every room, four king bedrooms with en-suites, a 360 panorama from the tower and private access to a beautiful beach.  There are other lovely beaches nearby but no real surfing beaches.
neighborhood_overview:
Table House Farm is situated on the iconic Table Cape which features in most coffee table books and tourism brochures on Tasmania. In springtime especially, the spectacular Table Cape Tulip Farm is a mecca for tourists and photographers.

There are lots of places to explore and great day trips to do from Table Cape. Go with a local guide and watch fairy penguins come in from the sea at sunset. Boat Harbour Beach (voted one of the top 10 beaches in Australia by Australian Geographic 2017) is less than 15 minutes away; the long, white, pristine Sisters Beach with a lovely lagoon for children ( 20 minutes); spectacular Dip Falls (40 minutes); Historic Stanley, the charming old fishing village which featured in the film “Light Between Oceans” (45 minutes). From there walk or take the chairlift up on to The Nut and do the awesome 40 minute walk around the top; Wings Wildlife Park with lots of Tasmanian native animals is a favourite for children (1 ¼ hours); Emu Valley
host_about:
Having raised a family of travellers and now retired - Alan from an international construction management company which he co-founded, and Wendy from her job as an ABC television journalist - we moved from Sydney to our farm in Tasmania which we've owned for 35 years.

We have travelled the world, from the Faroe Islands to Antarctica and most places in between. We like to stay in unusual places off the beaten track, much like our place in Tassie.

Vineyard views, cosy nights by the fire, and scenic farmland await you at the Gregan Retreat situated on Lisdillon’s historic sheep farm and vineyard.

neighborhood_overview:
Lisdillon is a 6000-acre working sheep farm and vineyard. The estate includes three secluded beaches as well as the reef off the main beach and a rivulet and estuary. Featuring unrivalled views of The Hazzards, Freycinet National Park, and Maria Island.

Back in the day (1830), the land once housed a small but thriving township. The sheep farm,19th-century cottages and sprawling native land are living reminders of Lisdillon’s rich history. Now home to an award-winning vineyard and boutique accommodation, Lisdillon is the perfect balance of past and present Tasmania.

The cottage is just under 100 square meters with a mezzanine master bedroom and open plan living. It is set among the vines of Charles Reuben Estate in a quiet and secluded area with full kitchen, wood heater and spa.
Charles Reuben Estate is also a vineyard, distillery and lavender farm. Our boutique farm products are readily available for purchase - wine, specialty spirits and various lavender items.
Tours and visits can be arranged.
neighborhood_overview:
There are many things to do in our area. We are very close to two wildlife parks - ZooDo (2 minutes drive) and Bonorong (10 minutes drive).
We are also only 7 minutes away from one of the oldest towns in Australia - Richmond. There are many things to see and do in Richmond, you can visit the - Oldest Bridge, Oldest Gaol, Lolly shop, Bakery, Pub, Paddle boat & bike hire, Art & Craft shops, Antique shops, Maze, or simply enjoy the BBQ facilities. Richmond is situated in the Coal River Valley (which produces some of the best Australian wines) so why not go on a Vineyard tour.

name: Alpine chalet Mt Wellington Hobart
description: 100 yr old character home. Sunny.  On doorstep of rain-forests, waterfalls, alpine walks, mt bike tracks, rock climbing, hiking. 10 minutes to city. Lots of wildlife. On route to sights and tourist ventures of southern Tasmania

I am a teacher of science, art and technology. I have bushwalked extensively in Tasmania and have a good knowledge of much of this beautiful island and am happy to share my knowledge of Tasmania with those interested. I have lived and worked overseas, largely in Kenya. I am active in wildlife conservation and have established a charity which involves rhino conservation. I am creative; I am an artist and also recently patented a product, so I guess I am an inventor as well. I enjoy good food and witty conversation, and enjoy discussing films and books. I currently have a couple from Sri Lanka boarding with me. They are at studying at university.

My style of Airbnb hosting is relaxed and helpful. Guests have the use of a number of rooms in the house; there is a large kitchen and lounge rooms. I provide cereals and tea, coffee and fruit drinks for breakfast. I like to make my house a good base for those who wish to explore Tasmania.

A short drive south is Five Bobs Cafe and

name: The Storekeeper's
description: The Storekeeper's Boutique Accommodation is a beautifully appointed 1840s sandstone cottage with a contemporary edge.  Located next to the original General Store in the village of Buckland, the cottage was the shopkeeper's residence.  The Storekeeper's is operated by Twamley Farm. The farm is just a short drive from The Storekeeper's,  where as a guest you have full access to wander amongst the historic buildings, walk or mountain bike.
neighborhood_overview:
The Storekeeper's is the perfect base to go behind the scenery and discover some of the East Coast's hidden treasures. Visit the magical Maria Island National Park for the day (ferry departs from the Triabunna Marina) a must see for any visitor to our Spring Bay region. Alternatively visit our family's working farm, operating since the 1840s, take one of many local short walks including the Convict Road to the Paradise Probation Station ruins at Orford, discover the intriguing story behind the historic St John the Baptist Church Buckland, explore the local beaches or enjoy a drive up the East Coast Wine Route to visit the many vineyards along the way.

You could just stop a while, wind down, relax, enjoy a beer at the Buckland pub and get to know some of the interesting local characters.
host_about: Our family has lived and farmed in the Buckland area on the East Coast of Tasmania since the 1840s. We are passionate about historic buildings and allowing others to enjoy the pleasure of these buildings with a modern and contemporary edge. We understand the importance of attention to detail, quality and aesthetics in creating an enjoyable and indulgent short break experience. We're also very excited about where our food and wine culture is going in Tasmania and so aim to bring you some of the best of Tasmanian products in your experience. We hope you truly enjoy your stay and discover something a little unique beyond the usual holiday houses and B&B's along our beautiful East Coast of Tasmania.

name: Oakchester Cottage on Bruny Island
description:
English woman Antoinette Pignon Powle built the cottage in the 1860s, making it one of Bruny Island's oldest homes. Originally named Oakchester, it is also known to locals as Mr. Wisby's Cottage - when Antoinette made a pilgrimage to the Holy Land, she asked her neighbor to look after the house. She never returned.

The cottage has been restored, inside and out. It has 1 Bedroom, dining room/kitchen, living room, outdoor entertainment area, bathroom/laundry with walk-in shower and claw foot bath
neighborhood_overview:
The cottage is located in 10 acres natural bushland resounded by country houses, farms and beautiful landscape.

Bruny Island is the perfect destination for those who appreciate outdoor activities amidst the rugged beauty of unspoilt bushland and beaches.

Cliffs and sea surfing (Cloudy Bay is approximately 30 mins drive from cottage. Bruny Island is also a popular destination for fishing (cast a line from the rocks or jetty, or launch your tinny from Alonnah or Adventure Bay boat ramps) and swimming (choose from the many surf and sheltered beaches around the island).
host_about: We live and work in Hobart and enjoy outdoors, food, wine and traveling. Always happy to meet new people and making new friends

description:
Winner of the Gold Medal for Hosted Accommodation in 2019 Australian Tourism Awards!

A traditional country house thoroughly modernised and wheelchair accessible that provides guests a choice of 3 comfortable, well-appointed en-suite rooms with TV/DVD, free WIFI & mini-bar.

neighborhood_overview: Dover is a friendly fishing village situated on the shore of Port Esperance Bay underneath the towering pinnacle of Adamson's Peak. It's an ideal spot for basing yourself to visit Hastings Caves and Thermal Pool, Ida Bay Railway, Cockle Creek and the literal end of the road (the furthest south you can drive in Australia), bushwalking in the South West Wilderness and Hartz National Parks and Tahune Adventures.
host_about:
My uncle once said the definition of a “local” is if your grandparents are buried in the town cemetery. Sadly neither my wife Lorraine nor I can lay claim to being a Dover local, however we have both travelled widely throughout Australia and overseas and we have chosen Dover above all other places visited in which to put down roots.

We’ve been in Dover for 13 years and have spent that time customising our beloved farmhouse into a modern and comfortable bed & breakfast guest house.

It was 30 years ago that Lorraine won enough cash after 4 consecutive nights on the now defunct TV quiz show Sale of the Century that she was able to pursue her childhood dream of travelling on safari in Africa. Little did she know that the expedition leader of her overland safari through Southern Africa would become her husband 9 years later following a proposal atop Africa’s highest mountain – Mt Kilimanjaro.

Years spent living in the west country of the UK and the big smoke of Sydney and working in varied roles within the travel industry as well as extended holidays in South America, Africa, Asia, Europe and the Middle East has provided the impetus to create the type of accommodation that we would feel comfortable and at home in. neighborhood_overview:
This is a peaceful neighbourhood in a bush setting. That's not to say you can't have fun. We just ask that (for respect of our neighbours), that music and loud noise ceases at midnight Fri and Sat, 10pm weeknights.

The bird life is wonderful and includes rosella's, parrots, blue wrens, wattle birds, black and white cockatoo's, kookaburra's and the rare white goshawk. Wallabies and rabbits roam freely on Mount Nelson - best time is dusk and dawn.

There is an extensive network of bush walking tracks on Mount Nelson - some close by and several more are accessible from the Mount Nelson Signal Station lookout (8 mins drive). There is a restaurant/cafe at the Signal Station lookout - the views are stunning. Bicentennial Park is a huge nature reserve and contains remnant native bush land that supports a variety of native plant communities and provides habitat for endangered species such as the swift parrot.

Natural beauty is on your doorstep and only 10 min
host_about:
An active and easygoing person, I lived and worked in Melbourne for 20 years and travelled extensively. I now enjoy life in Hobart and everything it has to offer: Clean air, great food and festivals, wine and local entertainment PLUS loads of natural beauty.

I look forward to making your stay as comfortable as possible. And if you have nothing to do, sit on the balcony and enjoy the river action - ships, yachts and ferries as well as beautiful sunrises, big skies and moons and an abundance of bird life in your bush setting. And if you don't want to venture outside.....you can see all from your Skybed.

Northern View offers a rare chance to experience breathtaking ocean panoramas and prime views of magical Boat Harbour Beach - recently ranked the best beach in Tasmania. Admire the water from nearly every room in this substantial 4 bedroom brick house.

host_about:
My Wife (Kerry) and I arrived in Tasmania in late 1991 with our two young boys as part of a promotion by my employer (as an Accountant), Kerry was a full time Mum (our youngest having a muscular disability) to our two young boys. However due to the recession of the early 90s instead of being offered another position back in Melbourne at the end of the three year stint I was retrenched (with the option of having my return to Melbourne fully paid for). However Kerry and I had fallen in love with Tassie and we stayed. Since then I have been retrenched, sacked, changed professions (last job primary casual relief teacher), lost our youngest son in 2008 from his condition and Kerry is now the main 'breadwinner' with a full-time job as an in house 'carer'. I have retired from teaching and we decided to give hosting guests through Airbnb as our biggest motive to travel is to meet differing people from different places (in 1993/4 we hosted a young Japanese Teacher who we now regard as our friend). In 1983/84 we travelled Parts of Asia (including Bangkok, Hong Kong, Taiwan, Japan and across USSR via the Trans Siberian) and settled in the UK (obtained employment) for most of the time using a motorcycle and the trains to travel Europe including Italy, France, West Germany, Spain, Portugal, U.K.(I had a sister & Kerry had some cousins & an aunt living there), Ireland, Yugoslavia, Greece then flying back via Singapore. In 2012 we travelled to Japan (sightseeing via trains and staying a week at the house of our Japanese Teacher friend and now mother of three boys), then to San Francisco, driving to Seattle (to meet an internet friend) then to New York, Iceland, U.K. (to meet up with Kerry's Cousins again) and back via Kuala Lumpur. Early in 2015 we travelled to Rio De Janerio (Carnival) and then to Las Vegas (meeting up with our son) where we renewed our vows (on our 30th anniversary), checked out the strip and hired a motorhome to see the Hoover Dam, Grand Canyon and Red Rock Canyon. We have also seen a fair bit of Australia as well from the Queensland Coast to our home town (Melbourne), From around Tasmania to the Hills near Adelaide. In 2017 we travelled to Adelaide, caught "The Ghan" train to Darwin, flew to Alice Springs then drove to Melbourne via Uluru (lucky to see the iconic rock in sunshine, overcast and in the rain), Adelaide and Broken Hill. In 2019 since my nephew was marrying a Swedish girl we decided to travel the continent via Athens, Rome, Lake Como, Imst. Austria, Grythyttans Sweden, Copenhagen, Berlin, Paris, Dubai, Bali.
Five things I can't do without are: Kerry (my wife), the internet, My bicycle, Occasional Travel and Occasional Staying Put. 
Guests can join in with our activities or be left alone to their own devices and given advice if that is what they want to enjoy the hidden gems of our island state.
I heard on the radio that there are three elements to happiness. Something to do (host Airbnb guests), something to look forward to (our next travel adventure what ever that be) and someone to love (we definitely have each other and are now closer especially after our unsuccessful fight for our sick son. We are now Grand Parents since 27 April 2020.

host_about:
Hi. We have been married for over 40 years and have a shared passion for travel, which we have passed on to our children. It has also helped that Glenn shares an Austrian heritage, and Gina a Greek heritage through respective fathers. We have travelled extensively to visit family and friends and discover new and wonderful places and can't wait to hear your stories of travel.

We have lived here all our lives and are very excited with the direction Tasmania is heading - especially as we also share a passion for great food and fine wines! We now have some of the finest foods and drinks in the world with an internationally renowned museum, festivals and marvellous natural rugged landscapes.

LEBRENA (South Hobart)
Glenn fell in love with the beautiful grand old Lebrena, a Henry Hunter designed 1876 sandstone mansion. For those of you who choose to stay at Lebrena, we share with you now as an AirBnB experience while we begin the long journey to return it to its former glory. We hope you will stop here a while and enjoy all that there is from our humble beginnings of something that hopefully will turn into a majestic and grand project.

GRANDVIEW (Battery Point)
Those who stay with us at Grandview, it is hard to reconcile the house dated 1885 you now see compared to the dilapidated frame we started with. From the underpinning required to get her standing proud (54 holes approx 1.6 metres deep) to the new renovation, fit out and landscaping, we have done it all ourselves over the last three years. host_about:
I am a friendly, happy go lucky kind of person who thinks a website built on trust is a great thing!
  
I enjoy travelling and meeting people and have stayed at a few Airbnb places and just love the idea and ease with which this system works.

I really hope people will look after and respect my home as I do all the other homes I stay in.

I very much enjoy my friendships gained from all over the world and find the different cultural aspects of people fascinating. People's stories inspire me to believe that all is not lost in this fast-paced, commercial world we live in.

One of my hobbies is photography. Taking lots of photos where ever I go means I have a massive collection of all types of subjects.  I am particularly interested in the minutiae of things in nature and with these new smart phones, blowing pictures up to greater size creates amazing scenes for me.

My favourite travel destinations would be outback Australia and Paris. Quite a difference, but each with their own unique beauty and splendour.  I usually travel with a companion. 

My life motto is - 'Know what you want, Be who you are, Make your heart Sing!'

Please feel free to contact me if you need further information about my little cottage or visiting Tasmania.

Kind regards, Maggie :-)

name: Enjoy Life at Coal Valley Cottage
description:
Offering guests a taste of the wonderful, relaxing Tasmanian life in the beautiful Coal River Valley wine region, we're a very easy 10 mins from the airport, 12 mins from Hobart CBD.

The well-appointed eco cottage was built in 2015, is off-the-grid (solar-powered) on 21 acres with beautiful views of farmland and Coal River estuary, and plenty of wildlife.
Outside the doorstep is many boutique vineyards/wineries.

Your official welcoming committee is Max, a super friendly Smithfield dog.
neighborhood_overview:
The Coal River Valley hamlet is a quaint rural/farming area (reminiscent of Sonoma County in California about 20 years ago), although it's only 12 mins from Hobart CBD, and 10 mins from the airport, 10 minutes from Richmond.
It's dotted with boutique, family-owned vineyards (many with cellar doors), and sheep and cows grazing in the paddocks, and roadside stalls selling cherries and apricots in the summer.

The area has been known for its cool climate wines, but lately, several whiskey distilleries have sprung up.
Sullivans Cove Distillery (5 minutes away) offers daily tasting and tour.
Lark Distillery (7 minutes away) offers tour and tasting.
And there's Last Rites Brewery (5 minutes away) that opens only on Fridays, where the locals go to catch up on the latest news.

If you love seafood, Tasmania is known for its fresh seafood from the pristine waters, and the specialty seafood places are very near us.
The well known Barilla Bay Oyster
host_about:
Having lived in Singapore, USA (NJ, NYC, IN), and Indonesia, the beautiful Tasmania is now home for me.

I live on 21 acres with my Tasmanian-born & raised husband Noel & lots of wallabies (similar to kangaroos).
The lifestyle here is easy, the air clean, the water pure, the food delicious, the wine smooth.
And I'd like to share our slice of paradise with you...

host_about:
Wendy and Mark started with Airbnb in February 2016, and are really loving the experience.  Previously over a number of years, they have had people rent their apartment for long-term stays, usually 6-12 months at a time.  Airbnb is different, Wendy says, “I can set it up really nicely and add my personal touches to make a special place to welcome visitors”.

Wendy is a teacher, working to support students with disability across all grades in the public sector; Mark enjoys working in his Gardening and Landscaping business.  This makes a great combination for being Airbnb hosts.  They both enjoy vegetable gardening as well as time with family and especially their three young grand-daughters.

“Since we opened the apartment to Airbnb, it’s been exciting meeting and interacting with people from all over the world.  It’s been a wonderful experience for us, and we would love to be your hosts.”  Guests are really pleased with our facilities; they have commented particularly how spacious the rooms are, and how much they love the full-sized, well-equipped kitchen facilities.  We have a good quality bed and comfortable easy chairs.  Guests enjoy sitting relaxing on the private deck, enjoying the sunshine and the view.

Mostly we seem to host couples around our own age - those semi-retired or near retirement, touring Tasmania on holiday or visiting family.  Our apartment seems to suit people like ourselves, and I guess that’s been the guiding principle - making our apartment the kind of place that we would like to stay in ourselves.  We keep the quality and standard of cleanliness high (especially with Covid19). The reviews which people have left are testament to happy guests who particularly speak about how well situated and well-appointed our unit is.

host_about:
Hello 
I am Stefan.  I have travelled the world as a scientist studying glaciers and climate change in Antarctica and other cool places. I am currently a science consultant at Glaciology Tasmania.

Over the past 5 years I have settled in beautiful Hobart, Tasmania. I still have dreams one of them is to build a sustainable living place in the centre of Hobart. A proof of concept and a kind of demonstrating that city living can be sustainable, possibly off-grid. I do hope over the next years to complete the first stage - a studio in the back of my property with an aquaponic system doubling as biotope and swimming pool. The second stage then will enlarge the current main house and hopefully includes a large garage underneath the house. The concept is to utilize BIPV - Building Integrated PhotoVoltaic (Solar) to generate my own electricity for battery storage (saltwater batteries) as well as for heat generation/storage for hydronic heating as well as hot water.

Your Stay at Villa Kunterbunt will help make this sustainable living in the centre of Hobart become reality and I look forward to answering any question you may have. I am also always keen to hear about ideas of others.

If I am not designing/building my own house I am a single full-time dad, exploring the great outdoors of Tasmania with my son and friends. I also still do some science work and lots of science outreach activities.

Ben, Vicki, Sasha & Annabel

description:
Honeywoodview is set on 50 acres and provides the perfect rural retreat where you can interact with an abundance of wildlife in their natural habitat.
Come and escape the busy city life and experience the peace and serenity only 27 kilometres from Hobart city.

It’s time to escape the light pollution of major cities and hubs and rediscover the night sky. Marvel at the beauty of twinkling lights at our very own stargazing spots from our back garden.
Whether you’re chasing an Aurora, or you simply have a knack for things that sparkle, make the journey to our place.

name: Beach House at St Helens Private waterfront views.
description: Our family have been enjoying holidays  at the shack for over thirty years. Enjoy spacious  living areas, stylish decor,  water views and  our private, bird-filled native gardens. Relax in the new outdoor bath or explore the bush track winding down  to a secluded bayside beach. Not another shack in sight. Beer Barrel Beach, the Maurouard surf & Peron Dunes await at St Helens Point 8 minutes drive away as are the Mountain Bike tracks. Time to recharge and relax on the Bay of Fires coast.
neighborhood_overview:
Binalong Bay, the gateway to the Bay of Fires, is short drive north of the Beach House and the new St Helens MTB Mountain Bike Trails are right on your doorstep.

Just 5 minutes down St Helens Point Road lie the surfing beaches: Beer Barrel and Maurouard. Grab the boogie boards, towels and some wetsuits (all provided) and jump in the ocean! Or wander over the red lichen covered rocks towards the towering Peron sand-dunes. This untouched part of the coastline is much as the French explorers found it in the 1700s. Thank you François Péron!

If you're looking for a sheltered spot to set up for a day on the sand, head beyond the turn off to the beaches on St Helens Point Road and find the peaceful Burns Bay. There's a collection of secluded bays to explore with beautiful boulders.
host_about: My husband Owen and I have lived and worked in Tasmania since the late 1970's. We discovered this beautiful island on what was meant to be a short stopover. We have travelled widely over the years but we still love the north east coast of Tasmania with its wild untouched beaches and Eucalypt and Myrtle  forested hinterland. We live in Launceston and have two adult daughters and two grand children. We all gather at the Beach House at Christmas and love to meet up there in winter too. Twelve years ago we started the annual Tasmanian Breath of Fresh Air Film Festival (BOFA). The Beach House is very much part of our lives and we hope you enjoy it as much as we do.

neighborhood_overview:
Acton Park is a semi-rural area. There are two very well stocked convenience stores, both with excellent delicatessens, a post office, doctor's surgery, chemist, cafes, take away outlets and tavern all within a few minutes drive from the Studio. There are also several restaurants within a short drive. The area is renowned for its safe swimming and nearby popular surfing beaches. The Tangara trail winds through the Acton corridor and offers some excellent walking opportunities.
The property is also close to the Tasmanian Equestrian Centre, the Tasmanian Police Academy, the Royal Hobart Golf Course and several other popular golf courses. The Coal River wine region is nearby and offers an excellent choice of Tasmanian wines and the finest of dining.
Hobart's CBD is a 20-minute easy drive from the Studio and the Hobart International Airport is a 13-minute drive from the Studio.
host_about:
I’m a passionate lover of wildlife, with a special fondness for Wombats.

Through our Bed and Breakfast suites we meet people from all over the world. Having lived in Grindewald 10 years and travelled throughout Tasmania  we  are able to pass on local knowledge.
We also own and manage up to 8 apartments on the Tamar Ridge Winery Complex, where we  offer the same high standard of accommodation,being only a phone call or text message away with an emphasis on the best value for our guests.

Each season we grow and share food and wine, sourced within the Tamar Valley, supporting other small local businesses.

name: Sunny Hillside Retro Retreat between Gorge & CBD
description:
Soak up the sun & the lovely views in this private 1 bedroom retro styled apartment. Located between the pristine iconic Cataract Gorge and the City. The apartment is positioned on a beautiful hillside overlooking the city and mountains beyond. Free off street parking, a quick 10-20 min walk or 5 min drive to the Launceston CBD, restaurants, museums, trendy cafes, shops and the Gorge.
Only a 10 min drive to the Launceston airport and 1 hours drive from The Spirit Of Tasmania in Devonport.
neighborhood_overview:
We might be bias but we believe our neighbourhood is the best you can get in Launceston. It has amazing city views, lush greenery, with beautiful housing, our local IGA supermarket is just 3 minutes walk up the road with fresh Tasmanian produce, the CBD, restaurants, bars, cafes and shops are all at your fingertips AND we are one of the closest areas to the incredible Cataract Gorge, which is practically in the backyard! It is just a nice 10 minute walk or 3 minute drive, where you'll find walking and hiking trails, the world's longest single span chairlift, swimming pool, restaurant, kiosk, cafe, peacocks and wildlife, beautiful gardens, suspension bridge, inclinator for easy access, Interpretation Centre and panoramic lookouts with spectacular views.

name: Eco self contained  cottage in a garden.
description:
This mini 1 bedroom house was our trial run in building our main home using passive house principles. We are approx 1 km from the centre of Westbury in a rural location. (You may be lucky enough to sight some of our local wildlife during your stay! )
The cottage is suitable for a couple, however the extra single bed does enable some flexibility for guests.(i.e. if you wish to use both beds, please book for 3 people.) We provide a library of information about sustainability for guest perusal.
neighborhood_overview:
The quaint little village of Westbury, centrally located in the Northern Tasmania, is the perfect base from which to explore Launceston, Devonport, the Tamar wineries, Cradle Mountain, the Mole Creek Caves, the Northwest, and, of course our local attractions.
•Nestled under the Great Western Tiers, Westbury is a classic Georgian village, surrounded by hedgerows and bursting with old English charm. It was established in the 1820's as a garrison town, and many of these buildings are still in evidence. Today Westbury is a classified historic town with plenty of attractions and charm.
These include:
•The stately Fitzpatrick’s Inn with its quaint little bar.
•The picturesque English style Village Green.
•The Westbury Maze and Cafe, a traditional hedge maze with over 1 km of pathways.
• Pearn's Steam World, a collection of over 200 examples of historic agricultural machinery. Houses one of the largest collections of working steam engines in the world.

host_about: Ian and I are retired teachers and this property is our retirement "project"! We were looking for 1 acre, north facing, gentle slope, close to amenities etc (and I had "bicycle ride to a cappachino" on my list as well. ) Long story, but the block of 12 acres found us! We built in stages: shed, workshop, garage, somewhere to live while we built the main house, landscaping, tree planting, walled garden, summer house, labyrinth and have started my "she cave" recently. The main house is nearly finished , however the whole project is still a work in progress. We are still teaching and sharing information with others who want to reduce their heating costs, grow their own food and leave a smaller footprint on our planet. Life is pretty full and we feel blessed to have this opportunity to share our lifestyle with others.

description:
Perfect for couples or families, Opossum Bay Beach House is your ideal location to enjoy all that absolute beachfront living has to offer. Stroll directly from the large deck down to the beach to swim, play, walk and relax the days away.

Opossum Bay is one of Tasmania's family holiday hot spots that features a safe, sheltered beach, stunning uninterrupted views of Mount Wellington and the River Derwent, and is only a 40 minute drive from Hobart city.

Welcome to our little slice of paradise!

description: Our one bedroom, fully furnished, self-contained unit shares our residential block, sitting above stunning Georges Bay on the East Coast of Tasmania and provides a comfortable base to explore all our region has to offer.
neighborhood_overview:
Akaroa is a coastal hamlet nestled on a small promontory over-looking Georges Bay between the bay and ocean beaches, surrounded by St Helens Point Conservation Area.
Situated 8km from St Helens, a 10min drive gives access to ample shops, supermarkets, hospital, hotels, restaurants, cafes, school and recreational facilities.

name: The Studio
description:
The Studio has an open-plan configuration with en-suite shower room and kitchenette and is located in the centre of Dover town, within easy walking distance to restaurants, cafes, supermarket and the beach.

neighborhood_overview: Dover is home to friendly locals; we know this from first hand experience having moved here from the mainland 13 years ago and the community has welcomed us with open arms and supported our hospitality business ambitions.  The Studio is 20 to 500 metres from the town's shopping area with IGA Supermarket, Cellarbrations liquor store, The Bottom Shop Deli and Larder, Top Shop Takeaway, Dover Pharmacy, Bendigo Bank & ATM, laundromat, post office, BP petrol station, hardware store, Ratznest Hair Salon, Post Office 6985 Restaurant and Dover RSL & Lawn Bowling Club. The beach on Esperance Bay is a 1km walk away and has a children's playground,  public barbecue area and public toilets and showers.
host_about:
My uncle once said the definition of a “local” is if your grandparents are buried in the town cemetery. Sadly neither my wife Lorraine nor I can lay claim to being a Dover local, however we have both travelled widely throughout Australia and overseas and we have chosen Dover above all other places visited in which to put down roots.

We’ve been in Dover for 13 years and have spent that time customising our beloved farmhouse into a modern and comfortable bed & breakfast guest house.

It was 30 years ago that Lorraine won enough cash after 4 consecutive nights on the now defunct TV quiz show Sale of the Century that she was able to pursue her childhood dream of travelling on safari in Africa. Little did she know that the expedition leader of her overland safari through Southern Africa would become her husband 9 years later following a proposal atop Africa’s highest mountain – Mt Kilimanjaro.

Years spent living in the west country of the UK and the big smoke of Sydney and working in varied roles within the travel industry as well as extended holidays in South America, Africa, Asia, Europe and the Middle East has provided the impetus to create the type of accommodation that we would feel comfortable and at home in. Having spent 9 months living in a tent as we circumnavigated Australia, we feel we have a great understanding of what is required for the weary traveller at the end of a long day on the road or a full day of sightseeing and we hope we have created a space that is worth leaving home for.

description: Villa Kunterbunt is an old cottage recently renovated and located within walking distance to the CBD. Interactions with guests - one may share a meal of enjoy a glass of wine and good conversations.
neighborhood_overview:
Villa Kunterbunt is located between the Hobart CBD and West Hobart in close proximity to most places in town.
A few favourite places are Pigeon Hole Cafe, a block and half away at the corner of Goulburn and Molle Street. They have the best bread in town serve great cafe, yummy breakfast and lunch. Two block further down on Molle is the Hamlet Cafe - a not-for-profit social enterprise with an interest in sustainability and social welfare - food is delicious and they do have a great selection of vegetarian meals.
From Hamlet cafe you can head up the rivulet walking and bike track to South Hobart, the Cascade brewery or if you on the move all the way up to Mt Wellington.
The Knoblofty Reserve with its walking tracks can be reached by either walking all the way to the end of Bathurst Street or up Forest Road from the Pigeon Hole Cafe.

In the other direction, at the end of Bathurst street is located the Queens Domain with walking tracks, the Aquatic Centre and the
host_about:
Hello 
I am Stefan.  I have travelled the world as a scientist studying glaciers and climate change in Antarctica and other cool places. I am currently a science consultant at Glaciology Tasmania.

Over the past 5 years I have settled in beautiful Hobart, Tasmania. I still have dreams one of them is to build a sustainable living place in the centre of Hobart. A proof of concept and a kind of demonstrating that city living can be sustainable, possibly off-grid. I do hope over the next years to complete the first stage - a studio in the back of my property with an aquaponic system doubling as biotope and swimming pool. The second stage then will enlarge the current main house and hopefully includes a large garage underneath the house. The concept is to utilize BIPV - Building Integrated PhotoVoltaic (Solar) to generate my own electricity for battery storage (saltwater batteries) as well as for heat generation/storage for hydronic heating as well as hot water.

Your Stay at Villa Kunterbunt will help make this sustainable living in the centre of Hobart become reality and I look forward to answering any question you may have. I am also always keen to hear about ideas of others.

If I am not designing/building my own house I am a single full-time dad, exploring the great outdoors of Tasmania with my son and friends. I also still do some science work and lots of science outreach activities.

name: The Stone House - Rose Room - Heritage Tasmania
description: The Stone House is 10 minutes from the Launceston Airport and 15 minutes from downtown Launceston.
neighborhood_overview: The Storehouse is one of the oldest houses in Australia (the original part of the house is circa 1835) and has been maintained in an immaculate condition. It was recently expanded with the addition of a lovely airy Conservatory overlooking the back Garden and Swimming Pool. The garden includes many magnificent examples of an old English Garden, with Rose Beds and heritage listed trees, including one of the oldest Magnolia Trees in Tasmania
host_about:
We bought our home in 2004 on a whim - once seen, we couldn't resist the temptation.  We renovated in 2006 and added the conservatory onto the back of the old stone house and the two bedrooms upstairs, including creating the stairwell.

The Rose Room is very much original, left almost as it would have been when first built.  The French windows add glamour to the room, allowing you to open up onto the Front Verandah, and has full view of the South Esk River and the magnificent  Magnolia tree that takes up much of the front garden - said to be the oldest in Tasmania!

The garden has been painstakingly upgraded over the years, as have other rooms in the rest of the house.  

This is the perfect getaway for friends to surround themselves in luxury, unwind in style and enjoy peace and tranquility in a very relaxed setting with historical Georgian architecture and fixtures.

name: Salt Box Hideaway
description:
Designed with comfort and ultimate rest and relaxation in mind, Salt Box Hideaway features soothing rich naval tones and a grand Tasmanian Blue Gum custom-made built-in bed. Sit by the cedar window and watch the rolling mist cover the hills as night falls, or rise early and embrace the tranquillity on the water's edge. We love to spoil our guests with complimentary port for you to sip under the stars.
This is a rustic part of the world and an important part of Tasmania's history.
neighborhood_overview:
Lettes Bay evolved into the perfect hideaway location in the early 1920s. Over the decades the cabins were passed down through family connections or sold on to others who were keen to preserve this water side sanctuary.

Your neighbours are others like you, seeking peace and quiet while enjoying the simplicity that the Historical Village of Lettes Bay offers.

The serenity and close-knit community of neighbouring, historic miner shacks is what makes Lettes Bay so special. Some are occupied permanently and others used as weekenders by owners living elsewhere in Tasmania or as ours is, enjoyed by vacationers wanting to experience a little slice of Tasmania for a short stay.

You will be charmed by the constantly changing weather and enormous skies. The bay is more alive during the summer months but the winter is also very special. Rug up and get out for long walks, take a steam train ride or explore Macquarie Harbour and take a Gordon River Cruise.
host_about:
Many visitors to the wild West Coasters aren't aware of Lettes Bay's quaint surroundings and heritage-listed shacks; the ones built in the early 1900s by hard-working employees from the Mt Lyell Railway and Queenstown Mine.  They positioned them right by the water's edge for their families to enjoy on days of rest. 

We understand the importance of taking time out to rejuvenate.

Our hideaway is a reward for all that hard work, and a place to spend quality time with each other, away from the hustle and bustle of everyday life.  

We think it's one of the most magical places in Tasmania and hope it casts its magic spell on you too.

Michelle

name: Derby Base @ Derby
description:
Derby Base is an ideal cottage for a MTB escape. Set in a quiet location off the main road yet just a short walk (or pedal) to the trailhead, pub, cafes and restaurants.

This original miners cottage has been tastefully renovated to include the modern conveniences you’d expect while retaining its original charm and with 3 private bedrooms it’s perfect for a family or group of riders.

The home is set on a large corner block with plenty of parking along with onsite bike storage facilities.
neighborhood_overview:
Derby is most well-known these days for the Blue Derby MTB trails. You can find plenty of information and maps of the trails on the ridebluederby or ridetassie websites.
There are 3 companies in Derby currently running shuttle services - Premium MTB Transfers, Mad MTB and Vertigo MTB. For more details on their services, check out their websites.
Other than world class mountain bike trails, the walking trails around Derby are simply stunning - check out Environment Tasmania for more info.
Or you can always put in your kayak or canoe (you’ll need to BYO) down at the Derby picnic ground and enjoy the view from the Ringarooma River (even throw in a line – the river is well-known for flyfishing).
Be sure to check out Blue Lake – also ideal for canoeing, fishing and boating. Keep an eye out for some smokey quartz or topaz.

name: Leighton Stud Cottage - Historic Evandale
description: Leighton Stud Cottage is set on a stunning property in Evandale, 2 minutes from Launceston airport and a short distance from, the Tamar Valley Wine Region, Ben Lomond and Launceston. The idyllic cottage set in a bustling farm environment is newly renovated and beautifully decorated with Tasmanian antiques and artwork. The property is yours to discover, take a walk to the South Esk River and visit our cows on the way. Or learn to ride at the Pegasus riding school. NEW wifi connection via the NBN.
neighborhood_overview:
Historic Evandale is one of the most picturesque towns in Northern Tasmania, the bustling community has the best flea and produce market you will find anywhere in Australia bursting with treasures and wonderful things to eat.
There are two historic pubs in Evandale, the Prince of Wales offers basic pub fare and you can enjoy a family meal with the locals. The Clarendon Arms has received a stunning makeover and offers gastro pub featuring the best local producers in Tasmania.
The Evandale Bakery offers the best local produce and a number of other antique stores and gift shops add to the location. There is also an IGA for basic supermarket needs. There is a local swimming hole on the South Esk River that is perfect for summer months and picnic areas to enjoy. There are also a number of important monuments in the town include the historic Evandale Uniting Church and water tower. Evandale will take you back in time, while being perfectly located to star Tasmanian attractions...<

An oval and playground are also 5 minutes walk away, which the kids will love to run around or kick a ball.

We are also on the MONA side of town - 15-20 minute drive north or head south into the city to catch the ferry to MONA instead.

name: The Racecourse Inn - Upstairs Queen Suite.
description: The Racecourse Inn was purpose built as a coaching inn in 1860 by ticket-of-leave convict William Dean, and is now a heritage B&B. The Queen Suite is a Queen sized bedroom with separate sitting room (with a sofa bed), with an interconnecting bathroom in between.  The bathroom has a shower, and separate toilet, with doors from both sides (bedroom and sitting room).  All linen and towels are provided, and bathroom amenities.  The tariff includes a full cooked and continental breakfast for two.
neighborhood_overview: Longford is a quiet agricultural town, established in 1814, only 20 minutes from Launceston and 15 minutes from Launceston airport.  We are 5 minutes from UNESCO World Heritage listed Woolmers and Brickendon Estates, and close to some of the best fly fishing in Australia, in the Macquarie and South Esk Rivers, Brumby's Creek and the highland lakes.
host_about:
We love Tasmania's northern midlands and the wonderful rural landscape around Longford, and enjoy making our guests feel welcome in this wonderful heritage listed Georgian house. 

I am passionate about cooking our beautiful Tasmanian fresh produce (especially desserts), gardening, good wine, antiques, and painting botanic watercolours and birds.  

We also love our animals, and are slaves to one very small cat, a young Smithfield Collie (a Tasmanian sheepdog breed), and custodians of two gorgeous black sheep and eight chooks.

When not at the Racecourse Inn we love to get out and explore around Tasmania's northern midlands and the Great Western Tiers.

description:

neighborhood_overview: The best thing close by my place is the beach! Only 4 min walk, cross the toad and you’re there. There are some little shops there too.
host_about:
Hello, I'm Anna. 

What can I say? I love my new home in Hobart and busting to get back into hosting. 

I'm one of Australia's 'original' hosts. It's been such a pleasure to host over 400 people from all over the world in my apartment in Sydney. It all started when a workmate told me about AirBnB, I thought, why not? Sounds like a great idea and totally my thing. Having travelled a whole bunch of places around the world, the places I remember as the best are those that are comfortable (a good bed with nice sheets), a bit homely (warm lights and space to lounge in) and easy (central location and not too many stairs to lug suitcases up- I have creaky knees!). Well- I have all those things and I love the idea of my home being someone else’s ideal find. 

I have spent over 10 years working in community development both overseas and in Australia, which has lead me into the world of Service Design. I guess what that means is that I’ve got a pretty broad appreciation of the life experiences of others, and I’m down with enough management jargon to take on any consultant with buzz words ;)

If you can overlook that my little obsession of collecting textiles from the Orient   everything will be fine. I’m super easy going, so feel free to just be yourself and enjoy your travels!

Cheers,

Anna

Stained glass windows, corniced ceilings and original period features are complimented by the ease of dual living areas, two bathrooms, a fully-equipped kitchen and a private courtyard set for alfresco dining. Stroll five minutes to peruse the creative stalls of Salamanca Market, with plenty of restaurants and cafes nearby to explore.
neighborhood_overview:
Set in prestigious Battery Point, Salamanca Markets beckons with its vibrant array of local crafts, foods, and the unique atmosphere that can only be found in this historic setting. Culinary adventures await at The Drunken Admiral and Jackman & McRoss bakery, where local flavours meet world-class hospitality.

You’ll be within walking distance of not only the bustling wharf precinct but also the departure points for the MONA Ferry, making it effortless to explore the renowned Museum of Old and New Art. St Davids Park offers a tranquil escape amidst the city's hustle and bustle, perfect for leisurely strolls or picnics under the Tasmanian sky.
host_about: Hometime curates collections of holiday homes for every occasion. We handpick our homes and offer guests on-the-ground support from teams who live, work and support tourism in their community. In Tasmania, we manage Hosting Hobart, which has been welcoming holidaymakers since 2016, led by Matt and Jo, who deliver the best service. There’s a stay for everyone, everything from water views to city stays. We know you’ll love it there all year round!

name: Well-appointed, architecturally designed home
description:
Mixing old world charm with timeless, modern simplicity, this well appointed architecturally designed home is located in the heart of Hobart.

description:
With a spectacular 180-degree views of Hobart and the Derwent river, this house is a wonderful holiday home. You even can see yacht races, especially the result, from the two lounges, dining room and even bedrooms. Also come to Hobart to the see the aurora, sometimes you can even see it from the house.

neighborhood_overview:
This house is located in Sandy Bay, Tasmania, Australia.
Sandy Bay is one of Hobart's premier suburbs. It follows the Derwent river, from the outskirts of Hobart city, South, as far South as Taroona (made famous by Princess Mary of Denmark). Sandy Bay is the home of the University of Tasmania and Wrest Point Casino and is only a few minutes drive from Hobart CBD. Properties in this area often have magnificent views of the Derwent river.

The suburb has its own shopping village where you will find a Coles and Woolworths as well as a selection of smaller shops, including a great butcher and bakery. All the major banks have branches in the village and there is also a post office. There are a selection of excellent cafes, bars and restaurants to choose from. These are all an easy drive from the house. Sandy Bay also has a lovely beach and one of the best seafood restaurants in Tasmania!
host_about:
We are locals who came from New Zealand initially, after coming to Hobart, we fall in love to it. The things we love most about Hobart are the beautiful scenery, water/mountain view everywhere, the fabulous food and the world class markets and world class festivals. We like the easy pace of life here which is really like New Zealand and enjoy camping, fishing (especially the dad), bush walking and eating out at the many great restaurants and markets. We also like to travel, both abroad and within Australia. 
 
 We run women fashion retail business, named Merric at Centre Point Shopping Centre. If you come to the shops and mentioning Airbnb guests, we could give you 10% off everything storewide.

I'm from England originally, half French too, and now Australian. Dave my husband and I live  in Tasmania, where we love the wilderness, the laid back lifestyle...arts and music, cinema, great gourmet food and good coffee! 

We used to live part of each year in England, in Paxton's beautiful Princes Park, Liverpool, in our heritage listed apartment there. 

We love Europe too especially France and Paris where my family are from.  We love the vibrant arts and culture, food and music. Community, family  and friends always call us back.

For now Covid has halted our travels.

We like to welcome others to our home as a home-from-home, sharing the special places we know and love. Live the wonder of the moment - it's sacred; we practice meditation and we care about the environment and people.

description:
Green Valley Homestead is a stylish holiday house in a quiet rural setting on Flinders Island.

The cottage is situated on a productive sheep and cattle property, five minutes’ drive to the township of Whitemark.

Green Valley is on the doorstep of some of the most spectacular beaches and walking tracks on Flinders including Trousers Point and Fotheringate Bay.

Whitemark Beach is a good spot for a beach stroll and you can also walk the 30 minute coastal track to The Bluff.

Mt Strzelecki is a 10 minutes down the road and further along you will find our two favourite beaches - Trousers Point and Fotheringate Bay. Water too cold? Then pull on your runners and do the one hour coastal track between the two beaches along the headland and granite rocks.

There is also the Mountain Seas restaurant at Trousers Point and the Furneaux Tavern at Lady Barron at the southern end of the island.

To the north Bellerive is bordered by the small foothills of Waverley Flora Park.

neighborhood_overview: North East Tasmania has a rich tin mining, agricultural and natural history. Mountains, lakes, beaches, waterfalls and unique refugia rain forest are all a short drive from Tin Dragon Cottages (Settlers Hut). host_about:
Graham and Christine are passionate about living sustainably in Tasmania.

Falling in love with this lush green valley and its clear-flowing river we purchased a 36 Ac farm in 2001 and set about building the five brick and stone cottages which now sit looking out over the Ringarooma River. The former degraded cow paddock has been transformed to give each cottage its own private native garden with outdoor bar-be-que setting.

We are keen to learn about sustainable living, and very happy to share our experiences with our guests. More often than not our gardening efforts benefit the possums more than the human inhabitants; but we persist!

Rain is harvested to supply clean chemical-free water and a micro-hydro powers the cottages. Waste water is recycled back onto the farm. Guests are encouraged to collect eggs, pick vegetables and fruit from our organic garden and catch trout for the BBQ. In summer the river is ideal for a refreshing swim!

Binalong Bay is a great destination for couples. With pristine beaches at its’ door step and surrounded by natural bush, the area offers something for everybody. The region is a bushwalkers paradise, with many tracks beginning almost at the doorstep of "The Loft". Book a boat trip with Bay of Fires Eco Tours and see the whole of the Bay of Fires from the water. Or launch your own boat from the unique Binalong Gulch to enjoy Tasmania's premier game fishing areas or explore the endless white sand and crystal clear waters of the numerous beaches. Book the local tennis court for a hit of tennis down on the waterfront, or have a BBQ down on the green. Walk down and dine at "Meresta EATERY" which is open most days offering delicious food and great coffee. Binalong Bay beach was voted by a well-known travel magazine as the second best beach in the world.

Jump in the car and take a short 10 minute drive into St Helens where you can visit the galleries, the collectibles store, and
host_about:
My husband and I have lived at Binalong Bay for 27 years but recently went away to NSW to trial living there. During this time, we holiday let our home very successfully and had many happy guests who just loved “Seascape” and still wish to holiday here. We returned to our home which is nestled between Humbug National Park and the Bay of Fires conservation area, overlooking Skeleton Bay, realising that Binalong Bay is the best place to live in the world with its beautiful white beaches and crystal-clear sea.

We also knew that previous guests wished to stay here again so we built “The Loft” alongside our home which is now available for bookings, providing an opportunity for others to enjoy everything that this part of the world offers. Peace and tranquillity with opportunity for bush walking, fishing, cycling, dining, whale watching to name a few activities that can be undertaken in the area.

name: The Bungalow - Partridge Farm - Flinders Island
description:
The Bungalow overlooks the animal paddock on Partridge Farm and has a Queen bed and large spa with BBQ facilities.

Our guests can also experience Lorraine’s meals for dinner, which are delivered to your room. All units have an extensive wine and beer selection.
host_about:
Rob & Lorraine Holloway moved to the 30 acre property in 1980.  They cleared the block, grassed and fenced the paddocks & turned what was once ‘an ecological desert’ into a perma-cultural paradise.

In 1996, they named the property ‘Partridge Farm’ after the free range partridges and started holiday accommodation.  First was  The Bungalow which is bed and breakfast accommodation.  The Bungalow overlooks deer and sheep paddocks and has good views of Franklin Sound and outer Islands.  The Bungalow has a double bed and spa.

The Bungalow was very busy so they decided to build The Tophouse which is self contained and has 3 bedrooms.  The Tophouse  has views of Franklin Sound and is close to the Eucalypt forest.

After a few months they built The Retreat.  It is a self contained studio unit with a king size bed and also overlooks Franklin Sound and is close to the large eucalyptus forest. They have a large vegetable garden, many different varieties of fruit trees  and an olive grove.

They also cater for house guests on request and food is sourced mainly from Partridge Farm, cooked by Lorraine with meals delivered to the houses.  Partridge Farm has a liquor licence and in each house is an extensive wine and beer supply,  featuring local wine from Unavale Vineyard & a large selection of tasmanian wine.  There is an enclosed  bbq area with a wonderful brick pizza/bread oven.

Partridge Farm has a Rav 4 available for hire, so you can see the island at your leisure.

name: Saltworks Beach House - fun with family & friends
description: Relax and have fun with family and friends while enjoying sensational sea views and a stunning landscape from this historic beach house; the perfect spot for a special holiday, a romantic getaway or as a base to explore the East Coast. The Saltworks Beach House is a waterfront cottage with short walks to secluded beaches for swimming and longer coastal walks. Close to an all weather boat ramp, it’s an ideal location for every season. It has a special 'wow' factor you will always remember.
neighborhood_overview:
The Saltworks Beach House takes its name from the historic Lisdillon Salt Works that operated in the 1830's and is now a small sleepy settlement consisting of around 25 large blocks, predominately weekenders with a few permanent residents. The properties are well spaced for privacy. As there is no through road, the Saltworks remains one of the east coast's best kept secrets, known predominatley by local fishermen in search of bream, crayfish, flathead, salmon, calamari, scollops and abalone.
Getting there: The Saltworks Beach House is accessed via Saltworks Road which joins the Tasman Highway between Boomer Creek (to the South) and Lisdillon Rivulet (to the North). It sits almost exactly halfway between Triabunna (28 kms South - 22 mins) and Swansea (24 kms North - 19 mins).
host_about: I co-host The Saltworks Beach House with my sister Mercia, a wonderful collaboration we both enjoy.  I also work as a mediator supporting people in dispute resolution. I have a background in education and facilitate workplace training for leadership and teams. I enjoy walking, reading, music, time on the beach and in the wilderness. I cherish relaxing and sharing food and conversation with family and friends, I especially like hanging out with my sister (co-host) and family at our Beach House. I have a keen interest in current affairs and issues which impact social justice and the environment. I am committed to making a positive contribution to our world.

description:
Nature lovers delight - immerse yourself in the tranquility of a secluded valley, 95 acres of mature native forest - Mountain Ash, Stringybark, Blackwood, giant tree ferns, beautiful and endangered birds and animals, creeks, ponds, a river with cascades and swimming holes, and trillions of stars in the night sky.

name: The Bunker - Place of the stars
description:
Rural retreat in Murdunna,
the best kept secret on the Forrester Peninsula.

A comfortable and charming open planned upcycled tiny home. Surrounded by a native garden and glimpses of water views across the bay.

A short 2min walk to the water's edge.

The use of Tasmanian timbers and re purposed materials makes the Bunker experience unique & memorable.

The name Murdunna is believed to come from a local indigenous word meaning "place of the stars"

Fur kids welcome 😻 we are fully fenced.
neighborhood_overview:
Murdunna is a quite seaside community. Local residents and people visiting on weekends make up the small community.

The Bunker is located in a quite street with a mix of neighbouring local residents and occasional visitors.

Please be mindful that Murdunna is a quite community. It's a place to come and relax and to get away from our busy lives. We ask guests to keep noise to a minimum after 10pm :)

There is a general store and petrol station.

Stop in Sorell on your way to the Bunker for supplies, where you will find Coles and Woolworths supermarkets.
host_about:
Danita grew up on the Tasman Peninsula and has always felt connected to this beautiful place.

When the opportunity came up to purchase a little piece of land, my hubby and I jumped at the chance.  

We wanted to create a space where there would be little to no impact on the environment, a space to be shared with others, to enjoy, relax and to experience the magical seaside community.

We decided to build the Bunker and source materials that could be repurposed, restored and/or reused.  We tracked down materials from around Tasmania that had history or could potentially end up in land fill. 

We used Tasmanian Oak, pallet wood, pre loved roofing and search for interesting home wares that tell a story.
 
The Bunker Build
We started by thinking what we could do with the 5m x 5m colour bond shed that was on the property. A tree had fallen and damaged the shed roof, the whole property was overgrown with tall dry grass, half burnt trees that was caused by the Dunalley fires several years previously.  No fencing,  just an exposed burnt-out space.  

At the time all we could see was just how amazing it would be to transform this little piece of paradise and for the past four years that’s what we did, we built the Bunker.

Every part of the Bunker tells a story; the ceiling are made from the use of pallets by removing every piece of wood, de-nailed, sanded and white washed. 

The kitchenette is made using pre-loved Tasmanian Oak. The kitchen bench cabinet belonged to my great grandmother, this too has been lovingly restored and incorporated into the kitchenette.  

The Constantine door that divides the living and bedroom space was rescued from a Lindisfarne tear down.  The bed is made from pallets. 

The front fencing is made using the roof from a house in Primrose Sands that was heading for landfill. The art deco walling in the toilet came from a bungalow in Bellerive. 

The cool glass blocks in the shower were purchased from a Devonport business who were re-decorating their retro office space. 

Wherever we could upcycle we did. 

The end result is a cozy, unique and special place to get away from it all.

We look forward to welcoming you to the Bunker!

neighborhood_overview:
Waratah is a picturesque town midway between Burnie and Cradle Mountain. The town features a number of historical buildings including Philospher Smith's Hut and The Bischoff Hotel and is well worth exploring. With the main street only 300m away it is an easy walk past the lake.
The Roadhouse is prominent on Smith Street as you drive in or out of town. It is open 7am - 6pm 7 days per week and can supply all your basic needs, including take away food and petrol.
Further along this road you will find the Waratah Museum, The Athaneum, the Post Office, the Stamper Mill and also the top of the waterfall. If you continue along past the old post office you will find the perfect location to view the waterfall across from the Bischoff Hotel.
While you are there stop in at The Bischoff Hotel for a drink or stay for dinner - they do a Monster Chicken Schnitzel that my son LOVES!
Wander around the lake - it's a nice easy stroll and keep an eye out for Platypus - they do exis

I live on the NSW central coast at beautiful Lake Macquarie with my little man Christopher and fur baby Luna the Bulldog.

It was my love for photography and travel that first led to exploring Cradle Mountain and eventually resulted in searching for our own little holiday home nearby.  That is how we first came across "The Burrow" at Waratah - It truly was a labour of love turning it into something we are proud to call our own and happy to share with others.

We are pleased to be able to share this with you and  we hope you enjoy your travels in  wonderful Waratah as much as we do.

Hi there
my name is Anne. I live in beautiful Stanley, a small village in north 
west Tasmania, in Australia. I am a retired art teacher and a practising artist. I live with my partner Jon, who is a sculptor. When we leave this area we love visiting Melbourne's galleries and museums, as well as travelling further afield to explore the world.

neighborhood_overview:
Derby is a quaint village in a picturesque valley in North East Tasmania. Once a sleepy country town it has been revitalised by the creation of the Blue Derby Trails and the enthusiasm of the local community. In the main street are the post office, The Hub for great beer and pizza, The Dorset Hotel for a fantastic pub meal and friendly service, and two great cafes. There is even a Floating Sauna on the lake! Vertigo MTB and MadMTB run shuttles to the trail heads every day.

Derby is situated on the Ringarooma River which is popular for fishing and kayaking. Some people spend their time fossicking for gemstones on the banks of the local creeks and rivers.

Just on the edge of town is the Blue Derby trail head and shuttle buses are available to reach the trail heads further out of town. All trails lead back into Derby and also connect with the Blue Tier Trails to the east. Just opened is a family friendly bike trail around the local lake and a pump track just over

Make the most of the expansive lands by walking, swimming, fishing or bringing your kayaks and exploring the river and coastline.

name: The Old Wesleyan Chapel
description:
The Old Wesleyan Chapel (1836) is a charming Heritage Building (National Trust) that offers studio accommodation with character and history.
We are situated in the heart of one of Australia's finest colonial villages, Evandale.
The Chapel has been stylishly decorated and features a double bed and a sofa bed, fully equipped kitchen, large screen TV, washing machine & easy car parking outside.
Best of all, you are only 15 minutes from Launceston and 5 minutes from the airport!
neighborhood_overview:
What makes Evandale special is its one of the prettiest and best preserved historic towns in Australia. Its Late Georgian and early Victorian buildings house shops and Pubs and it's relatively untouched streetscape offer a unique glimpse into Australia's past, with some buildings dating back to 1809.
The Wesleyan Chapel is situated in Russell St, which is the main historic street and is less than 100 metres from the popular Evandale
Market with over 100 stalls. Every year Evandale holds the World Penny Farthing Championships, which is something to see! The historic towns around Evandale are also delightful and are full of Historic homesteads and if you are looking to visit the popular Ben Lomond area, Evandale is a great jumping off point.
host_about:
I lived with my partner Mark in Evandale a few years ago, we loved it so much, when we saw the Wesleyan Chapel for sale..we just had to buy it!
My passion is ART, family & travelling, my partner has a tour business to the Port Arthur historic site. 
We also have 2 children and a cat!
We hope to retire and live in the Chapel, but for the near future, we would love to share the building with you.
