name: Adrift Studio at Flotsam Dunalley
description: Flotsam has two fabulous fully self-contained studios, right at the doorway to the Tasman Peninsula.  Each has their own private surroundings and fantastic sea views. We are about 30 mins due east of Hobart Airport.  It's ideal for one-night stays, but, if time permitting, treat yourself to a few days so you can explore this incredible area which is all within easy reach. The Studios are well-designed and modern, and have lovely touches which will make your stay very comfortable and special.
neighborhood_overview:
Dunalley was once a centre for fishing and canning, and had a busy little harbour. There are signs of it still. But now it has numerous oyster farms, sheep farms, an abolone farm, and lots of orchards. It is rural yet attached to the sea. We have a canal and a bridge that opens allowing the fishing and sailing boats through from Blackman Bay into Frederick Henry Bay - a much safer, and shorter way into Hobart. Tho' historically there have been many a shipwrecked vessel at the Narrows, that's the outlet of Blackman's Bay to the Pacific Ocean. Sometimes the swell is so high boats can't risk coming through.
We had a catastrophic fire in 2013 which destroyed in total 161 homes. It destroyed the community and the lives of many people. However, if you look closely you will see the amazing survival spirit of the locals - the new school, new community hall and terrific new infrastructure, not to mention the great new homes which have been rebuilt, and the strength that has emerged

neighborhood_overview:
Alonnah has an amazing beach for those keen on beach-combing, swimming, snorkelling, kayaking, and boating, with a ramp close by. You can also drop a fishing line from the pontoon and regularly spot seals and dolphins. This track and the beach are just a short 350-meter walk from Blue Cottage.

The natural scenery around Alonnah is breathtaking, with the Dray Track starting at the Pontoon going north, the easy foreshore walking track opens up a world of wildflowers and stunning viewpoints. The Pontoon is also an excellent spot for birdwatching, or if you're lucky, to gaze at the majestic Aurora Australis.

A short 10-minute walk south down the beach brings you to the Hotel Bruny Restaurant. Make sure to book Hotel Bruny Restaurant in advance, as it gets quite busy!

For the wine and gourmet food enthusiasts, the Bruny Island Premium Wines and Tastings provide the perfect lunch spot with stunning views.

name: "Elsmere" - Heritage Gardens & Accom
description: Your accommodation is on the ground floor of this 3 storey house which was originally the servant's quarters of this magnificent Arts & Crafts period home built in 1905. neighborhood_overview: Quiet, private street with just 4 houses and no thru traffic. This street is named after the house. The home faces East so you get the morning sun and no hot afternoon sun. The large deciduous trees in the garden put on a show throughout the seasons, and dozens of different roses and magnificent 100+ year old magnolia grandiflora locked in a battle with an equally old mauve wisteria provide that special old world feel you just don't get from a new garden. Fragrant lilliums, colourful hydrangeas and fruit trees round out the spectacle. There is a terraced outdoor area where you can sit to take it all in just listen to the birds singing and it's hard to imagine you are so close to the city centre with your own private parkland.

name: Mary Monica. Queen bed in Victorian Cottage.
description:

neighborhood_overview: Friendly.
host_about: I am an almost retired teacher with a very simple yet enjoyable life. I have been blessed with 4 (adult) children, a most adorable granddaughter, and an equally adorable grand baby boy. They take my breath away! I am blessed to be a grandma. Such a gift! I love to cook and would happily do so for my bnb guests. It would involve freshly plucked herbs and healthy fare.  Amongst other things, I make pretty aprons, bags and slippers for little ones. A girl can never have too many shoes, right? I thrive in my garden space and very much enjoy the surprises she brings. I write but I don’t share it. Not yet. I love antique furnishings and belong in the last century. Travelling gives me much joy  and I love to meet other adventurers and the resultant conversation. I welcome visitors. I can hide away too. One cannot live without flowers, good coffee, and anything Italian. I value greatly the embrace of a blue sky, both in terms of sunshine and as a metaphor for life. My favourite travel destination thus far would have to be Venice. Actually, if I woke up anywhere in Italy I would be pretty pleased with myself. Finding a companion to play Scrabble with is now sorted with any enthusiastic guest who is willing to take on the challenge. I would be thrilled! I am fascinated with Poland and it’s history, love learning about the lives of British royalty and have a weakness for weird and wonderful vintage wall pockets. A passion for female jazz vocalists gives me much joy. Stacey Kent would be my eternal favourite. She sings and I potter! There are so many musicians who are somewhat enticing for me. Nina Simone for her heartbreaking story, her prowess with classical training as a pianist and her very important spiritual messages. Leonard Cohen, pure poetry in song! name: Adventure Bay Beach House for 2, Bruny Island.
description: New and perfectly set up for one couple, this house is a relaxing getaway overlooking Adventure Bay beach. You can't help but relax in this beautiful contemporary home's style and tranquility.  Enjoy a spacious light-filled house with full kitchen, outdoor BBQ, sauna, luxe king bedroom and ensuite.  Stroll to the beach or jetty,  just a few steps from the gate. Located on 6 private Land for Wildlife acres, the artist and musician owners have added their personal touches for your enjoyment.
neighborhood_overview: Bruny Island is the best of Tasmania compressed into one island!  From rainforests to beaches, a dramatic coastline of plunging cliffs to stretches of sandy beaches, olive groves, vineyards, oysters and cheese tastings, this is a place which will embrace you into its relaxed and gentle pace of life.  Adventure Bay, the loveliest stretch of beach on the island, is known for being unspoiled, uncrowded and is the place where Captains Cook and Bligh and other explorers like Bruni d'Entrecasteaux, after whom the island is named,  dropped anchor and rested.   It is is home to the unique White Wallaby as well as being surrounded by forests with any number of beautiful and sometimes rare birds.   Bruny is still mainly a rural island of sheep farms, forests and renowned gourmet food producers.  And world class artists, including jewellery makers.  Its waters are full of fish and lobsters.....enjoy local produce from markets (if on) or the local shop during your stay.
host_about: Sailing, islands, wildlife, exploring and adventuring  have been such a big part of our lives, we feel unbelievably lucky to live where we do and to be able to share our homes .  After 10 years running charter yachts in the Caribbean (way back in the '70's!) before settling permanently in Queensland's Whitsunday Islands, we discovered Tasmania and Bruny Island on our travels.   Hospitality has been our life, so today we enjoy sharing our new beach house in TASMANIA and the +100 year old Heritage Cottage in the Whitsundays.  Between hosting guests with an authentic Australian experience, we enjoy home life,  riding our horses, travel and sailing around the world with friends.  In the past years we've sailed New Zealand, Alaska, Central America, Galapagos, Patagonia and all the way to Antarctica.  We hope to share some of  your adventures too!

name: Farmstay by the ocean-The Pear Shed Pickers Hut #1
description: Our restored pickers accommodation Hut #1 is part of a twin cabin with a shared bathroom and toilet amenities. It is situated in a private corner of the pear orchard with a view to the pear and lemon trees first thing you step out of the door. There is a variety of birdlife in the bush next to the huts and in a Parsons Bay, one minute walking distance, where you can also find a farmgate stall with fresh fruit and veggies and an orchard cafe. White beach 5 mins walking distance away.
neighborhood_overview:
Our Huts are situated in a sheltered corner of the pear orchard. It is close to a beautiful white sandy beach (White Beach) perfect for walking, kayaking, swimming, fishing. There are some nice snorkelling spots nearby and a Beautiful Roaring Beach- the famous surfing spot about 30 min drive.
There is a fresh fruit and veg stall at the premises where you can get all the essentials of cooking your dinner.
Our friends have set up The Pear Shed Cafe in front of the Veg Stall which is open from Wed-Sun 7.30am-14.30pm and makes beautiful coffee and pastries.
Nubeena township has got 2 shops, a bakery, hardware store, Bendigo bank with an ATM, a chemist, and a Community Health Centre. The Port Arthur Historic Sites is just a 10 min drive and Port Arthur Lavender Farm 15 min drive. Love living in such a beautiful corner of Tasmania!
host_about:
We are living in a beautiful southern corner of Tasmania- the island state of Australia or as historically named An Apple Isle. Our property is a 4th generation pear orchard and is situated in a renowned crayfishing village, Nubeena about 10 mins drive from Port Arthur Historic Sites. Life in this corner of the world, in a rural settlement can be rugged and challenging but definitely inspiring and colourful. You find beauty everywhere you look. Scott is a born and bred pear orchardist and this is his family farm. 
The huts have a long history of guests enjoying their  summer holidays since they were established in the 70s. And thats not a surprise- situated in the sunny corner of the orchard with a short walk through the property you could get to the beautiful White Beach! 
The pear farm with its beautiful location and character has developed to be a hub for local artists -The Pear Shed Gallery where you can find works of the local artists and craftspeople from the Tasman Peninsula is located at the farm gate- a big packing Shed as you arrive to the farm. 
There is a beautiful small café next to the gallery called The Picker’s Pantry where you can enjoy locally roasted coffee and local treats in a beautiful orchard.

description: Swim, surf and explore by day and star gaze by night on Tasmania’s rugged and beautiful East Coast in this 3 bedroom home with expansive views of Spring Beach and Maria Island. Maydena is also a great stop on the way to Lake Pedder, and Mount Field National Park is only a 10 minute drive away. Mount Field is the home to one of Australia's most beautiful waterfalls Russell Falls a tiered cascade waterfall and there is a lovely tall trees walk . Also near Maydena you can walk through some of the tallest trees in Australia at the Styx Big Tree Reserve. Nearby there are numerous rainforest walks with towering swamp gums and one of the best trout fishing rivers the Tyenna river. Near the bridge at Maydena you can often spot platypus. Mount Field with its mountain scapes and trees also encompasses a cave system, glacial lakes and ancient turns and heath groves. The Junee caves and springs are in Maydena and well worth a visit as are Marriot falls just down the road towards Mount Field.

Ben, Vicki, Sasha & Annabel

name: BICHENO BEACH BUNGALOW: Beautiful Waterfront Pad!
description:
This gorgeous, peaceful Bicheno beach bungalow has spectacular views of the coastline in charming Bicheno. Walk outside our back gate and within seconds you’ll be at secluded Rice Pebble Beach, a wonderful place to laze and have a dip.
Features all mod cons including BBQ. With open plan living area and great views, it has 3 bedrooms, each with comfy bed (2 Queens, 3 King Singles) and quality linen. You'll love the stunning views.
neighborhood_overview: Bicheno is a tiny, historic  seaside hamlet with a permanent population of just 800! It has cafes, restaurants, a Sunday market, art gallery, boutique, newsagent, medical centre, hardware store and supermarket. It also has a terrific fish and chip shop - The Gulch - a  7 minute stroll from our bungalow! Originally a whaling town, Bicheno still sports historic lookouts from the headlands, with amazing views of the region, where whalers once looked out to sea to find whales. These days, of course, the whales are protected, but you can still spot them out at sea in winter and late spring. Bicheno is also famous for its penguin colonies . (You can sometimes hear their cries from our bungalow as they come ashore in the evening!) This is why it's important we have no pets on the property as dogs or cats could frighten these gentle little creatures. Aside from the special secluded beach below the bungalow, Bicheno also has a large popular beach with white sand and clear waters at nearby Waub'

host_about:
Hello 
I am Stefan.  I have travelled the world as a scientist studying glaciers and climate change in Antarctica and other cool places. I am currently a science consultant at Glaciology Tasmania.

Over the past 5 years I have settled in beautiful Hobart, Tasmania. I still have dreams one of them is to build a sustainable living place in the centre of Hobart. A proof of concept and a kind of demonstrating that city living can be sustainable, possibly off-grid. I do hope over the next years to complete the first stage - a studio in the back of my property with an aquaponic system doubling as biotope and swimming pool. The second stage then will enlarge the current main house and hopefully includes a large garage underneath the house. The concept is to utilize BIPV - Building Integrated PhotoVoltaic (Solar) to generate my own electricity for battery storage (saltwater batteries) as well as for heat generation/storage for hydronic heating as well as hot water.

Your Stay at Villa Kunterbunt will help make this sustainable living in the centre of Hobart become reality and I look forward to answering any question you may have. I am also always keen to hear about ideas of others.

If I am not designing/building my own house I am a single full-time dad, exploring the great outdoors of Tasmania with my son and friends. I also still do some science work and lots of science outreach activities.

name: Low Head Lagoon Beach One
description: This gorgeous, peaceful, heritage listed cottage is right opposite Lagoon Beach on a large block in the heart of historic Low Head. It is a quintessential 'Tassie shack' with loads of character and is immaculate inside and out. The house has 5 bedrooms and sleeps 10 people; outside is a huge deck and space for many cars or even a game of cricket!  Lagoon Beach is 20m from the gate and is perfect for young children; or if you prefer a surf beach, 'East' is a 5 minute stroll from the back gate.
neighborhood_overview: Low Head boasts a beautiful lighthouse and historic pilot station with a cafe and museum; it has three unique beaches: Lagoon Beach, Pilot Beach and East Beach. Lagoon and Pilot's are picturesque and sheltered and thus perfect for young children. East Beach is a beautiful surf beach from which you can take a long walk to Bell Buoy Beach if you're looking for exercise.  There is an active fairy penguin colony at the light house with nightly tours. There are multiple supermarkets, butchers, restaurants and amenities at George Town (a 5min drive). Low Head is perfectly situated to enjoy the Northern Tamar wineries such as Clover Hill, Pipers Brook, Bay of Fires, Jansz, Delamere, Dalrymple and Sinapius, most of which are within 30 mins drive.  The world renowned Barnbougle Golf Links consisting of The Dunes (#2 course in Australia and #11 in the world) and Lost Farm (#2 public course in Australia and #23 in the world) are both approx 45mins drive away.

This holiday shack oozes charm and retro style. Built in the 1950s the house remains relatively unchanged and enjoys beautiful views across Spring Bay and Triabunna.

neighborhood_overview:
Triabunna is the departure point to World Heritage listed Maria Island National Park. On Maria Island, there are an array of walking and mountain biking trails. Maria has stunning beaches, mountain peaks and is teaming with wildlife. The ferry departs several times a day from Triabunna, docking at historic Darlington, a former convict settlement.

Orford which is 4km away has many beautiful beaches for swimming/ exploring, including Raspins, Shelley, Spring and Stapelton. There is a 2km coastal walk between Shelley and Spring Beach which is worthwhile, although not a circuit. The Three Thumbs track is another local bushwalk which is 4km (2 hour) loop trip with fantastic views of Orford, Spring Bay and Maria Island.

Barton Avenue is incredibly quiet day / night, and we're lucky to be surrounded by some fantastic neighbours.

name: Mary Monica. A touch of yesteryear. Double room.
description: Mary Monica is a delightful little hidden gem: a double story Victorian cottage, a 20 minute walk to the city centre, a little further and you will find Salamanca Place. It is a mirror of times gone by. Vintage fabrics and soft furnishings, rose scents, antiques and candlelight to warm the night. neighborhood_overview: A five minute walk to the popular North Hobart restaurant strip and State Movie Theatre. It is a happy neighbourhood with forged friendships. If you are lucky, you may get to have a laugh with my fabulous and inimitable  friends up the street :))
host_about: I am an almost retired teacher with a very simple yet enjoyable life. I have been blessed with 4 (adult) children, a most adorable granddaughter, and an equally adorable grand baby boy. They take my breath away! I am blessed to be a grandma. Such a gift! I love to cook and would happily do so for my bnb guests. It would involve freshly plucked herbs and healthy fare.  Amongst other things, I make pretty aprons, bags and slippers for little ones. A girl can never have too many shoes, right? I thrive in my garden space and very much enjoy the surprises she brings. I write but I don’t share it. Not yet. I love antique furnishings and belong in the last century. Travelling gives me much joy  and I love to meet other adventurers and the resultant conversation. I welcome visitors. I can hide away too. One cannot live without flowers, good coffee, and anything Italian. I value greatly the embrace of a blue sky, both in terms of sunshine and as a metaphor for life. My favourite travel destination thus far would have to be Venice. Actually, if I woke up anywhere in Italy I would be pretty pleased with myself. Finding a companion to play Scrabble with is now sorted with any enthusiastic guest who is willing to take on the challenge. I would be thrilled! I am fascinated with Poland and it’s history, love learning about the lives of British royalty and have a weakness for weird and wonderful vintage wall pockets. A passion for female jazz vocalists gives me much joy. Stacey Kent would be my eternal favourite. She sings and I potter! There are so many musicians who are somewhat enticing for me. Nina Simone for her heartbreaking story, her prowess with classical training as a pianist and her very important spiritual messages. Leonard Cohen, pure poetry in song! I suspect that if you visited and stayed, you would like to return. I firmly believe that one can learn something from everyone in this life. My motto is “kind words, loving gestures.”However, a spade remains a spade and I am certainly not backward in coming forward! Have a happy day and may Lady Luck travel with you.

neighborhood_overview:
Pirates bay is at your doorstep! This vast beautiful and wild beach stretches out along Eaglehawk Neck - perfect for beach walks, fishing, surfing and paddle boarding!

Eaglehawk Neck is a small town and natural gateway to the many attractions of the Tasman Peninsula, including the Port Arthur Historic Site.

The thin strip of land known as the Neck connects the Tasman Peninsula to the Forestier Peninsula. It's about 400 metres long and less than 30 metres wide at one point. The Neck is also a natural geological wonder with striking rock formations like the Tessellated Pavement, and nearby Tasman's Arch, Blowhole and Devil's Kitchen.

There's also an eco-cruise that takes visitors past massive sea cliffs and the local seals, dolphins and penguins.

The area attracts bushwalkers, rock climbers, kayakers, divers and surfers and is a popular summer holiday destination for locals and visitors alike with a range of places to stay.

name: Adventure Bay Beach House, Bruny Island
description: New and perfectly positioned at Adventure Bay for a relaxing getaway . The retreat-style feeling of this thoughtfully designed beach house on 6 private acres of Land for Wildlife forest is quite unique.   Enjoy personal touches and attention to detail in the full kitchen, outdoors BBQ, sauna, 2 luxe spacious bedrooms with king size beds and en-suite facilities.  Watch the wallabies hop past to graze in the natural landscapes.  Enjoy peace and privacy with sea views from every room.
neighborhood_overview:
Bruny Island is the best of Tasmania compressed into one island! From rainforests to beaches, a dramatic coastline of plunging cliffs to stretches of sandy beaches, olive groves, vineyards, oysters and cheese tastings, this is a place which will embrace you into its relaxed and gentle pace of life. Adventure Bay, the loveliest stretch of beach on the island, is known for being unspoiled, uncrowded and is the place where Captains Cook and Bligh and other explorers like Bruni d'Entrecasteaux, after whom the island is named, dropped anchor and rested. It is is home to the unique White Wallaby as well as being surrounded by forests with any number of beautiful and sometimes rare birds. Bruny is still mainly a rural island of sheep farms, forests and renowned gourmet food producers. And world class artists, including jewellery makers. Its waters are full of fish and lobsters.....enjoy local produce from markets (if on) or the local shop during your stay.

description: Fantastic spacious 5 bedroom beach house overlooking the ocean and is located on Main Road at Binalong Bay in the Bay of Fires. You can walk, fish, swim, climb, sit, read, cook & play.

It is a peaceful and relaxing place for a family or group holiday.

Light & bright 3 bedroom, sandstone home conveniently located in the heart of idyllic Oatlands, nestled in the peaceful southern midlands of Tasmania, you will arrive at Raffah House via Tasmania's Heritage Highway - the majestic gateway from the North to the South.

Follow us on socials @raffahhouse for frequent updates on the space.

Oatlands is a peaceful, historical, sandstone village. There’s a supermarket, bottleshop, news agency, post office, pub, wine bar and a number of coffee shops only a short walk from Raffah House. The locals are very friendly and always happy to chat or help with any questions you may have around the area, so don't be shy to say hi!

name: Forth River Cottage-Bed and Breakfast by the river
description:
“Rivers know this: there is no hurry. We will get there someday” AA Milne

Five Star accommodation, with full complimentary breakfast, on the banks of the Forth River in NW Tasmania. Ideal for one or two adults, Forth River Cottage is located 10 minutes drive from Devonport and 1 hr from Cradle Mountain. Private, peaceful and designed for the most discerning traveller. Leave your worries behind as you take in the flowing river, the sunsets and green pastures. You won’t want to leave!
neighborhood_overview: Forth definitely ranks as one of the most scenic, as well as one of the oldest towns in Tasmania. Nestled on the banks of River Forth, it is only a 13 kilometre drive from the city of Devonport. The population of just 350 people makes it the kind of town where everyone knows everybody and you will be made to feel extremely welcome. Many of the original buildings have been replaced since settlement, but there is still a strong sense of history about this old town. At the hub of this history is the Historic Bridge Hotel, which is one of the town's oldest buildings and still stands in almost its original form. It was first licensed and opened in 1872, and has managed to retain the old world charm and atmosphere of those times of the past. The building is in fact heritage listed and regarded as a national treasure. It is also regarded as one of Tasmania's leading live music venues. I love traveling around Tasmania.  My favourite places to stay in Tassie other than Strahan are Corinna, Cradle Mountain, Anson's Bay, Binnalong Bay and North Motton.

I also love fresh fish and salads and blueberries which we grow in our garden.

name: Winkle Shack - waterfront, wood fire, outdoor bath
description: In Tasmania, a shack can be anything from a corrugated iron lean-to, to an architect designed home.  Our place falls somewhere in between, but we reckon it’s one of the best shacks in Tassie.   In a sheltered, waterfront spot,  it’s a classic little vertical board place built by a family in the 1960s as a get away from Hobart that we've kept improving over the years.  This is our family get away, the place that our kids have grown up and memories built.
neighborhood_overview: Winkle has water frontage to Eaglehawk Bay and nothing but eucalypts behind it.  It’s only a ten minute walk to the surf beach, Pirates Bay. You can easily walk along the beach to the Lufra Hotel (another 20 min) and get a newspaper in the morning or walk there for dinner in the evening.  The blowhole, the Pirates Bay Jetty, Doolishus Fish and Chips / Icecream Van and the walks around Tasman Arch / Devils Kitchen are 10 minute drive away.   Port Arthur is a 20 minute drive. There are great walks all over the place here - cliff top walks, lookouts, beaches, and headlands. There is a book of Tasman Peninsula walks in the bookshelf. Lastly, keep an eye on the bay in front of the house. There’s often dolphins or seals about. If the water is glassy, watch for the telltale narrow V of an octopus swimming close to the surface.
host_about:

host_about:
Hello 
I am Stefan.  I have travelled the world as a scientist studying glaciers and climate change in Antarctica and other cool places. I am currently a science consultant at Glaciology Tasmania.

Over the past 5 years I have settled in beautiful Hobart, Tasmania. I still have dreams one of them is to build a sustainable living place in the centre of Hobart. A proof of concept and a kind of demonstrating that city living can be sustainable, possibly off-grid. I do hope over the next years to complete the first stage - a studio in the back of my property with an aquaponic system doubling as biotope and swimming pool. The second stage then will enlarge the current main house and hopefully includes a large garage underneath the house. The concept is to utilize BIPV - Building Integrated PhotoVoltaic (Solar) to generate my own electricity for battery storage (saltwater batteries) as well as for heat generation/storage for hydronic heating as well as hot water.

Your Stay at Villa Kunterbunt will help make this sustainable living in the centre of Hobart become reality and I look forward to answering any question you may have. I am also always keen to hear about ideas of others.

If I am not designing/building my own house I am a single full-time dad, exploring the great outdoors of Tasmania with my son and friends. I also still do some science work and lots of science outreach activities.

Cockle Creek really is a bush walkers haven and a fisherman's dream with it being the perfect spot for Cray Fish and flathead fishing.

name: Exclusive Boutique Coastal Cottage
description:
At Beaupre enjoy the wonders and exquisite beauty of exclusive secluded access to over 300 meters of sandy beach in a private bay.

Our 40 acre working farm has billabongs, coastal tracks, native forest, abundant wildlife and exquisite 270º vistas over the Huon River, Cygnet Bay and across to Bruny Island.

Call into Franklin and visit the Wooden Boat Centre on the way. Visit the crayfish, abalone and salmon fishing village of Dover and take a swim at the nearby Hastings Caves and Thermal Springs. Also, in the vicinity is Southport’s Ida Bay historic railway and Cockle Creek, gateway to Southwest Wilderness and the farthest point south one can drive in Australia. With Hobart a northerly 50 mins scenic drive

name: The Loft at SoHo: Architecture & Views
description: REST, EAT and WANDER. With Hobart at your doorstep, The Loft at SoHo is the perfect base for all explorers. neighborhood_overview:
The Loft at SoHo is located on the doorstep of the thriving South Hobart café strip. Start your day with breakfast and some of the best coffee in Hobart (Bear With Me, Ginger Brown) sample world-famous produce at the local shops (Salad Bowl, Salamanca Fresh and Maquarie Supermarket), visit the new South Bar & Bistro and meet the local platypus at the serene Rivulet, all just a few minutes’ walk away.

The Loft is also walking distance to antique and gift shops, as well as the lovely historical houses of South Hobart and tourist attractions such as The Female Factory and the Cascade Brewery.

Although close to public transport and all of the above, it's really quiet here.
host_about:
Marcelo and I discovered Tassie about 7 years ago and fell in love with it, especially Hobart.  We bought this little place and started our Airbnb in January 2019, and finally managed to move here in July 2021 after a 2 year stint working in Singapore.  We love hosting and helping to share the Hobart love/experience that we're obsessed with. 
Marcelo is originally from Uruguay and is a sculptor/artist by trade.  You can see his work throughout The Loft.  He also has experience in the hospitality industry.
I'm the organiser, having worked in events and customer service.  I'm passionate about people, music, home design and creating atmospheric and comfortable spaces.
Between the two of us, we love classic cars and scooters, cooking (especially South American barbeques), shopping for antiques/rare finds and travelling.  Throughout our travels, we've stayed at quite a few Airbnb homes, enough to know what we like and don't like. description:
A cosy waterfront cabin on The Great Lake, Miena - Coldwater Cabin is the perfect place for a secluded wilderness escape.

Relax on the deck with a glass of wine and watch the light dance across the lake, or curl up inside with a cup of tea and take in the views through the north-facing windows.

If what you crave is the connection to wilderness only Tasmania can offer, then Coldwater Cabin is the place for you.

Follow our stays @coldwatercabin
neighborhood_overview:
Miena is one of the coldest towns in Australia. It snows more than 60 days each year, including in during January, so you should prepare for any type of weather.

Miena is in the bush and also full of wildlife. Wallabies, possums and deer roam the property, a wombat often pops up from underneath the cabin, and an echnida lives in the wood tanks next door. If you're really lucky, you might even spot a Tassie devil nearby. All this fauna makes it really important that you keep your rubbish in the allocated bins during your visit.

For this reason also we have a strict no pets policy to promote wildlife in the area.

If you’re into trout fishing, you’ve definitely come to the right place. There are plenty of world-renowned fly fishing lakes in the area. If you’re a walker, Liffey Falls is a 30-minute drive away and Lake St Clair, an hour. There are also a series of shorter walks close by, and plenty of local lakes to explore.

neighborhood_overview:
The small riverside village of Maydena is the gateway to Tasmania's World Heritage wilderness and an ideal stop for those on their way to remote Lake Peddar.

Maydena sits by the Tyenna River, south west of New Norfolk between Mount Field National Park and Lake Pedder. The village has a rich forestry heritage but is now better known for its close proximity to some of Tasmania's most beautiful natural places including Mt Field National Park and Southwest National Park.

Mt Field National Park, before Maydena, is home to one of Tasmania's most beautiful waterfalls - Russell Falls, a tiered–cascade waterfall just a short walk from the park's visitor centre and one of several waterfalls in the vicinity.

At Maydena, experiences include a walk though some of the tallest trees on earth at the Styx Big Tree Reserve and the Railtrack Riders - a unique pedal-powered experience on an historic stretch of railway track.

Bellerive is a busy little suburb of Hobart on the eastern shores of the Derwent River. Bellerive stretches from Kangaroo Bay where it borders Rosny Park, around the curved shoreline of Bellerive Esplanade to Kangaroo Bluff, then down to Bellerive Beach and east to Second Bluff, where Bellerive borders Howrah. To the north Bellerive is bordered by the small foothills of Waverley Flora Park.
Bellerive is best known as the home of international cricket ground Bellerive Oval – more recently known as Blundstone Arena. Is it also a popular sailing area, home to Bellerive Yacht Club (1926) and has a marina located at Bellerive Quay.
Bellerive was first settled in the 1820s, and at that time known as “Kangaroo Point”, for the large numbers Kangaroos that would be seen on the shore. Even before this time a ferryman regularly crossed the Derwent, coming ashore in the Bellerive area.

description:
Whale Song is an escape on the edge of the ocean where pacific gulls call and the roar of the ocean fills the air.
Our beach shack is a sanctuary of peace and calm, perfectly suited for 2 - 4 guests.
Located in the sleepy hamlet of Falmouth, a stunning, secluded part of the East Coast of Tasmania.

neighborhood_overview:
Falmouth is a very special, secluded hamlet. Many of the shacks and properties play a unique part in the rich history of the close knit and creative Falmouth community.
Wander down the quiet streets or access the headland path at the eastern end of the garden, explore as you are make your way to the favoured swimming hole of Henderson Lagoon. Once your in Falmouth you won't need your car to explore our sweet town, your feet will find their way.
In summer, there is always a private place for you to enjoy the beach from, drift wood forts to explore and draw. Surfers come and go as the swell turns it on. In winter, there is a beautiful stillness, with the delicious bonus of the generous sun that shines to make the days feel warm. Every season is beautiful, and are equal in their magic, we love them all!

Groceries and Supplies
There are no shops in Falmouth so please stock up on all your food before you arrive. There is an IGA in St Mary's, Scamander and St Hele
host_about:
Hi there, We love the beach, nature and the peace and tranquility of the bush. I am an artist, and Clif is a graphic designer. I love to paint and am inspired by the world of travel, from a bustling city full of culture to a sleepy hamlet where time stands still. 
Our family love the beach, we all surf and all find inspiration in being outside amongst nature.

name: Ashdowns of Dover Bed & Breakfast King / Twin Room
description:
Winner of the Gold Medal for Hosted Accommodation in 2019 Australian Tourism Awards!

An award winning traditional country house thoroughly modernised and wheelchair accessible that provides guests a choice of 3 comfortable, well-appointed en-suite rooms with TV/DVD, free WIFI & mini-bar.

A 70 minute scenic drive south of Hobart in the Huon Valley in the centre of Dover.

Experience warm hospitality and locally sourced delicious hot breakfasts cooked to order.
neighborhood_overview: Dover is a friendly fishing village situated on the shore of Port Esperance Bay underneath the towering pinnacle of Adamson's Peak. It's an ideal spot for basing yourself to visit Hastings Caves and Thermal Pool, Ida Bay Railway, Cockle Creek and the literal end of the road (the furthest south you can drive in Australia), bushwalking in the South West Wilderness and Hartz National Parks and Tahune Adventures.
host_about:
My uncle once said the definition of a “local” is if your grandparents are buried in the town cemetery. Sadly neither my wife Lorraine nor I can lay claim to being a Dover local, however we have both travelled widely throughout Australia and overseas and we have chosen Dover above all other places visited in which to put down roots.

We’ve been in Dover for 13 years and have spent that time customising our beloved farmhouse into a modern and comfortable bed & breakfast guest house.

It was 30 years ago that Lorraine won enough cash after 4 consecutive nights on the now defunct TV quiz show Sale of the Century that she was able to pursue her childhood dream of travelling on safari in Africa. Little did she know that the expedition leader of her overland safari through Southern Africa would become her husband 9 years later following a proposal atop Africa’s highest mountain – Mt Kilimanjaro.

Years spent living in the west country of the UK and the big smoke of Sydney and working in varied roles within the travel industry as well as extended holidays in South America, Africa, Asia, Europe and the Middle East has provided the impetus to create the type of accommodation that we would feel comfortable and at home in. Having spent 9 months living in a tent as we circumnavigated Australia, we feel we have a great understanding of what is required for the weary traveller at the end of a long day on the road or a full day of sightseeing and we hope we have created a space that is worth leaving home for.

Years spent living in the west country of the UK and the big smoke of Sydney and working in varied roles within the travel industry as well as extended holidays in South America, Africa, Asia, Europe and the Middle East has provided the impetus to create the type of accommodation that we would feel comfortable and at home in. Having spent 9 months living in a tent as we circumnavigated Australia, we feel we have a great understanding of what is required for the weary traveller at the end of a long day on the road or a full day of sightseeing and we hope we have created a space that is worth leaving home for.

name: Tamar House, Rosevears
description: Tamar House, self-catering accommodation, is set in a quiet rural location, on the Tamar Valley Wine Route, and on the Tamar River.  15 minutes from Launceston; set in 1 hectare of gardens, overlooking the Tamar River. Tamar House offers guests serenity and beauty. Stroll in the gardens, sit and relax with a good book, or enjoy local food & wine with friends. Tamar House is a great choice for small groups of up to 8 adults.
neighborhood_overview: Rosevears is a quiet, tranquil hamlet on the banks of the Tamar River Estuary in Northern Tasmania.
host_about:
A Baby Boomer, animal lover, gardener and rudimentary water colour artist, I fell in love with the Tamar Valley on a trip to Tasmania in 2016. We bought Tamar House in April 2017 and, with my husband, have enjoyed commencing the process of rejuvenating a large established, pre-loved garden. In 2018 we began a total renovation of the guest accommodation and now have a beautiful space which our guests can enjoy. 

The guest accommodation building is separate from our private residence, so guests can have as much or as little interaction as they would like with us. 

Both my husband and I have travelled overseas to Europe, USA and Asia.  We both love books, our family, and being out in the garden or farm shed, pottering. When you come, you will probably find us in our jeans and a T-shirt, up to our elbows in our latest project - be it digging in the garden, or renovating an old piece of furniture in the shed.

Charlie, our slightly overweight (Ok..., very overweight!) Labrador, lives on the property with us, and loves welcoming our guests. 

We offer a relaxed and informal type of stay in a quiet rural hamlet - the accommodation is modern and comfortable and guests are left to relax, unwind and feel at ease, and at home. 

Guests are welcome to stroll in the gardens at Tamar House; or sit on one of our park benches and read a book; or take a stroll along the quiet rural road that runs alongside the river. Alternatively, they can snuggle up in front of the wood fire, eat breakfast on the deck, or chat with friends at the large kitchen table.

We are located on the Tamar Valley Wine Trail, so we are a great base for those looking for a day out visiting the cellar doors. Just an hour’s drive away is the world class Barnbougle golf course. 

We are very fortunate to look out on to the magnificent Tamar River every day, and its beauty never ceases to amaze us.  During the day a myriad of birds fly overhead, rest on the jetty or walk through the gardens. At night, wallabies, possums and bandicoots come out to feed. 

We want to live in a place of beauty and enjoy a quieter life, away from the noise and bustle and the harried city life. We want to eat simply and live simply and hope you will come and share in a piece of the paradise we have found in Rosevears. We look forward to welcoming you to Tamar House.

description: The Nest is a delightful one bedroom house in picturesque Eaglehawk Neck. neighborhood_overview:
Eaglehawk Neck has an abundance of historic natural features including the Tessellated Pavement, The Blow Hole, Tasman Arch and the Devil's Kitchen. There are amazing picturesque walks of varying degrees of difficulty but all taking in the wonderful coastal scenery. The white, sandy beaches are ideal for swimming, surfing, fishing and a variety of other water activities.
Port Arthur Historic site is a 25 minutes drive away and this convict penal colony is Australia’s leading tourist attraction. The Remarkable cave is a further 3kms from Port Arthur and has breathtaking views of the coastline to Cape Raoul. The Three Capes walk is also located in this iconic wilderness area as well as the award winning Pennicott Tasman Island Cruise, a must see do in my eyes !
For keen surfers, Ship Stern bluff and Roaring beach are both within a 40 min drive.
Let's not forget the mountain bikers. There are a myriad of tracks and roads for you to explore in this mostly untamed wilderness

Nubeena is a sleepy, scenic village near the Port Arthur Historic Site on the Tasman Peninsula. It's a popular holiday spot among tourists and Tasmanians and offers excellent Beaches, fishing and waterside views, with World Heritage-listed convict sites nearby.

Surrounded by a network of inlets around Parsons Bay, Nubeena has a long maritime history. The village was originally an outstation of Port Arthur and for many years was an important convict farming community.

Coal was once mined in the north-west of the peninsula and the ruins of the soldiers' barracks and convict quarters can be found at the World Heritage listed Coal Mines Historic Site nearby Saltwater River.

Walks and water fun can be had on the shores of nearby White Beach, while surfers hit the challenging waves at Roaring Beach.

name: Peaceful cosy home with mountain views
description:
Peaceful home with great mountain views nestled in a native garden. Queen double bedroom with en suite, smaller second bedroom, full bathroom, kitchen, living room, deck. Sunny garden terrace among fruit trees. Bush walks (steep road). City 10 mins away by car or bus, or 45 min walk by historic pretty Hobart Rivulet. Easy street parking, one spot on site. Great base to explore Tasmania.

No TV, but you can watch the clouds and stars from the deck!

There's an Airbnb also at lower ground level.
neighborhood_overview:
The Mountain is always in view with its changing weather patterns and light. Low light pollution means lots of stars.
Wallabies and possums come out at night too! South Hobart is friendly with great local cafes and restaurants. 10 mins to Sandy Bay beaches and the cultural city centre, or if you like the walk, 40 minute walk along the historic and scenic Hobart Rivulet. Platypus have been seen there, a rare treat though, as is an Aurora Australis. Cascade Brewery in its dramatic setting is nearby as is the World Heritage convict site, the Female Factory, both have special histories. Mt. Wellington allows views right across the Island, you can drive to the top (15km). Or walk from our home (4 hours) or 2hrs from the Springs half way up, where there are many delightful walks, short or longer.
host_about:
I'm from England originally, half French too, and now Australian. Dave my husband and I live  in Tasmania, where we love the wilderness, the laid back lifestyle...arts and music, cinema, great gourmet food and good coffee! 

We used to live part of each year in England, in Paxton's beautiful Princes Park, Liverpool, in our heritage listed apartment there. 

We love Europe too especially France and Paris where my family are from.  We love the vibrant arts and culture, food and music. Community, family  and friends always call us back.

For now Covid has halted our travels.

Dave keeps a rich fruit and veggie garden which guests can taste for breakfast when in season. We will share with you our favourite local secrets - cafes, arts venues, quirky surprises and natural wonders.

 We enjoy bush walks, gardening and growing food, the beach and the Mount Wellington in Tasmania and sharing time with friends. In Liverpool we have been very involved as friends of Princes Park, planting trees, joining the Saturday morning fun run and occasional special events.

We've also enjoyed being AirBnB guests, staying somewhere homely and finding out what the locals like to do. 

We like to welcome others to our home as a home-from-home, sharing the special places we know and love. Live the wonder of the moment - it's sacred; we practice meditation and we care about the environment and people.

name: The Wayfarer ~ Stunning water views
description:
A piece of paradise overlooking stunning Pirates Bay at Eaglehawk Neck, the gateway to the treasures of the Tasman Peninsula.

Step into a charming, original beach shack, lovingly restored. A peaceful, romantic space to pause, breathe and listen to the lullaby of the waves and soak in the surroundings.

An ideal base to explore Port Arthur, Three Capes walk, scenic cruises and pristine beaches.

With incredible views, this heavenly little wonderland promises to create some cherished memories
neighborhood_overview:
Eaglehawk Neck is a small town found in southeast Tasmania. It is the perfect spot to explore the Tasman Peninsula including the renowned convict ruins at Port Arthur.

Eaglehawk Neck is built around a narrow bar of land, less than 30 meters wide, connecting the Tasman Peninsula to the Forester Peninsula approximately an hour's southeast of Hobart. The isthmus is bordered by Pirates Bay on the east and Norfolk Bay on the west.

Easy to get to via the winding but gentle Arthur Highway you’ll be mesmerized by the amazing vistas and beautiful waters of Pirates Bay and the many activities in the area. You certainly won’t be bored if you’re taking a trip to Eaglehawk Neck. There is easy access to the challenging Three Capes track, famous geological features such as Tessellated Pavements, the Blowhole, Tasman Arch & Devil’s Kitchen, the Tasmanian Devil Conservation Park at Taranna, the award-winning Pennicott Tasman Island cruise, Remarkable Cave and famous surfing beach
host_about:
Melbourne born and based in Hobart. It was our dream to have a shack on the Tasman Peninsula which has now become a reality. It means the world we get to share it with others!! 

Interests: Travelling far and wide as well as close by, good food and wine with family and friends, running and walking, reading and taking time out to enjoy life.

Hi! This house is my home, nestled in the hills of South Hobart - close to the city - on the edge of Sandy Bay.

Filled with plants, books, records, and all the cooking equipment you need to whip up a feast for a cozy night in (fresh pasta?), the space is lighting -filled, warm and relaxing. It's the place I miss the most when I'm away.

Blessed with a central location, it's a great base for exploring southern Tassie, and the perfect pad for staying in Hobart with a few friends.
neighborhood_overview:
Walking distance to Salamanca markets (25 mins) and the picturesque streets of Battery Point, it's a beautiful neighbourhood to explore on foot. In good weather, the Fitzroy Gardens (my favourite picnic spot) are just a block away, and if you feel up to facing our hill (it's a steep one!) the Hobart Rivulet track is a beautiful walk close to home also. All the Sandy Bay shops (supermarkets, pharmacies, bottle shops) are super close (10 min walk / 2 min drive), with good coffee and food options close by, and all the cult favourites just a stone's throw away (in the city).

In summer, you can get to any of the good swimming beaches (Nutgrove Beach, Long Beach, the glorious Hinsby Beach) in 10-15 mins by car, which may be relevant to your interests if you're training for the winter solstice swim?

name: Saltair Cabin-Waterfront getaway with beach access
description:
This lovingly built cabin is the perfect location for a family or couple's getaway.
With private direct access to one of the island's most peaceful beaches, an outdoor fire pit, wonderful deck for those outdoor dinners, and a wood heater to gather around - this retreat was created with togetherness in mind. This cabin was designed to be both cozy and spacious.
neighborhood_overview: The Island is a foodies and nature enthusiasts paradise. With Cider, cheese, oysters, berries, fudge, wine and beer all made or grown at your back door, it is easy to book an extra nights stay. You will find with most beautiful beaches, you will have them all to yourself. 50% of the island is national parks, so there are walks for novice walkers to experienced hikers.
host_about:
We operate a dynamic family business 365 days/year, and we love hospitality! 

We are pleased to manage a number of vacation homes and shacks for Tasmanian families, and take great pride in connecting individuals and families with amazing places to explore. We love our beautiful island state, and we love helping others to share in enjoying it! 

When we aren't being AirBnB hosts, we're running meals and pouring drinks at Hotel Bruny, pruning the orchard for Bruny Island Cider, having fun with photography, paddle-boarding in the d'Entrecasteaux channel, skiing, kayaking, washing dishes, flying planes, composting a few tonnes of scraps/year, chopping wood, painting pictures, learning languages, designing stuff, raising chickens, and most importantly - raising a family. 

We like craft beer, sparkling water, slow food and a vibrant life. 

We love being here. Ask us anything - we would love to help.

description: Wanderers Cottage - A Slice of Paradise in Woodbridge Tasmania
neighborhood_overview:
Tasmania, our ancient little island on the edge of the world showcases the best in fresh food, fabulous wine and spectacular scenery and Woodbridge – our unspoiled, quaint little village that is one of Australia’s oldest country towns - is the star of the show. Reached by winding country roads that snake past the Channel, this lovely town is lost in time. And here, on our olive grove, surrounded by stunning wildlife – a rare parrot, wallabies, wombats, geese and ducks and greeted by our sweet-natured, wag-tail Border Collie, Sam – you will be lost in time, too.
On a full moon, which bathes the Channel in a soft, candescent glow, even the brightest lights of a brash big city dim in comparison. Host to bewitching rainbows of iridescent hues, Woodbridge is one of the last places on the planet where the bush and sky kiss and where the countryside holds you in a warm embrace.

description:
"The Cave" is a stylish and unique self-contained apartment under my centrally located 1885 West Hobart home. It is a 15 minute walk to the city centre and a short walk to the Elizabeth Street North Hobart cafe strip.

With the stairs to the entry and the bed in a raised platform "nook", "The Cave" may not be for everyone, but if you're looking for well located lodgings that ooze atmosphere I think you'll love it!
neighborhood_overview:
This part of West Hobart is heritage listed and one of the oldest parts of Hobart. It is very central, being on the edge of the CBD.

There are many cafes, bars and restaurants nearby, with the cafe/restaurant strip in Elizabeth Street North Hobart a short walk away, and Salamanca a 20 minute walk. The renowned Hill Street Grocer is a 5 - 7 minute walk away if you want to stock up on quality food stuffs (they also sell prepared heat-and-eat meals), and Smolt Kitchen, Pigeon hole Bakery/Cafe, & Room for a Pony are all great breakfast places and just a short stroll away.

If you feel like a bush walk, Knocklofty Reserve is also close by and there are numerous walking trails there (it's a very short drive or about a 20 minute walk to the bush).

name: Bluff Hill Point
description:
Huddled together in the midst of incredible wilderness, 12 shacks look out over the Indian Ocean.

The weather dictates life here, and every day is a good day. Fine days for adventuring. Wild days for sitting around the fire, gazing out at the ocean as it breaks with ferocity against the jagged rocks which surround Tasmania’s unsung Westernmost point.

We feel so fortunate to cherish, share and gradually improve this simple shelter on the Tarkine Coast.

More photos @Bluffhillpoint
neighborhood_overview:
Bluff Hill Point is Tasmania's unsung Westernmost Point. Frequently pounded by the intense weather of the Roaring 40s, the coastal flora is dense and unique. You may find cowrie shells on the beach, see wombats, echidnas and devils in the yard and the occasional human surfing the Bluff Break.

This little shack (okay, maybe a bit more of a house!) is one in a community of 12 shacks and houses at the Edge of the World. There is a feeling of community here, and although our nearest neighbour prefers to keep to himself, our neighbours at the other end of the Bluff may invite you to a barbecue or happy hour. If you have children, they will almost certainly be thrilled with Max and Christel's carefully engineered waterfront playground - with confounding puzzles for kids and adults alike.

If you want to keep to yourselves, your wish will be respected, but if you want to experience the fullness of Tasmanian shack life, you can find it here. Nature, comfort, community.
host_about:
We operate a dynamic family business 365 days/year, and we love hospitality! 

We are pleased to manage a number of vacation homes and shacks for Tasmanian families, and take great pride in connecting individuals and families with amazing places to explore. We love our beautiful island state, and we love helping others to share in enjoying it! 

When we aren't being AirBnB hosts, we're running meals and pouring drinks at Hotel Bruny, pruning the orchard for Bruny Island Cider, having fun with photography, paddle-boarding in the d'Entrecasteaux channel, skiing, kayaking, washing dishes, flying planes, composting a few tonnes of scraps/year, chopping wood, painting pictures, learning languages, designing stuff, raising chickens, and most importantly - raising a family. 

We like craft beer, sparkling water, slow food and a vibrant life. 

We love being here. Ask us anything - we would love to help.

name: Modern executive studio, sparkling, river view
description:
Modern, quiet, spacious, sparkling clean!
Ideally placed in mid-Sandy Bay. Easy access to shops, bus and University; 7 minutes to city.
Enjoy the huge covered terrace with 2 tables, BBQ and breathtaking views.
Two booking options:
1. Self-contained studio – perfect for two;
2. Studio PLUS optional second bedroom – see next heading.
Triple-glazed windows and hydronic heating for comfort all year round.
Liz and Philip are experienced AirBnB hosts (and guests). We will make your stay delightful.
neighborhood_overview:
Sandy Bay is an attractive, safe and sought after area, offering spectacular views over the Derwent River. Drivers are courteous and the people friendly.
We are a quick drive from the city, either along Sandy Bay Road or via the alternative route, Churchill Avenue, which runs parallel.
Explore historic Battery Point, one of the premier tourist attractions in Hobart.
Visit Salamanca Place and on Saturdays experience the famous Salamanca Markets.
Or tour the Hobart wharf area where you can book tours or enjoy restaurants and other attractions too numerous to list.
The local shopping centre is on Sandy Bay Road between us and the city. This has two supermarkets, three chemists, numerous coffee shops, pubs and restaurants, and a variety of other retail businesses offering physiotherapy, massage, medical and dental services, etc.
There is a local gourmet provedore, Hill Street Grocer, on Churchill Avenue, next to the University. We recommend it.
For

Philip and I have a keen interest in  travel, listening and learning about new cultures, sustainable practices and sharing and connecting our lives with people.

Step back in time and enjoy the historic sites and Georgian architecture which include The Historic Richmond Bridge (The Armoury Cottage overlooks the Bridge) The Convict Gaol, Museum, The Miniature Village of Hobart Town, The Oldest Catholic Church in Australia.

Cafes and Restaurants, craft shops, Antique Shops, Bakery etc. are there to enjoy.

A short drive will find many wineries to visit and enjoy a meal.

If a Golf enthusiast a Golf Course is nearby

My favourite pass-time is a walk across the Bridge, feeding the ducks and a wander along the riverside - then back to the Village to enjoy a coffee and cake (many Cafe's to choose from)

Saturdays are enjoyable at the Richmond Market with local produce and products to enjoy.

neighborhood_overview:
The location of South Arm is rural. It is 35 to 40 mins drive to Hobart.

It is a stunning area to the south east of Hobart. It is on the edge of Storm Bay with huge skies, dancing light and some 14 beaches and winding coastal trails.

In Winter it is well known as a top destination to view the Southern Lights, the Aurora Australis.

With an early history of whaling, South Arm lies on the main route for ships and yachts entering the city of Hobart. The annual Sydney to Hobart Yacht race goes past this house.

Australia's second oldest lighthouse, the Iron Pot Lighthouse, is located here.

The area is rural with a strong community. There are two hamlets on the Peninsula, South Arm and Opossum Bay.

name: The Wombat Burrow - Waratah (for Cradle Mountain)
description:
Get back to nature in our lovely, comfortable and private 2 bedroom villa, decorated in an industrial wilderness decor and with all the comforts of home so you can make the most of your stay.
Perfectly located only 50m to the lake and playground and within easy walking distance to everything Waratah has to offer, including museum, pub, cafe and service station.
A scenic 40 minute drive to Cradle Mountain and 45 minutes to Burnie and the main shopping district.
neighborhood_overview:
Waratah is a picturesque town midway between Burnie and Cradle Mountain. The town features a number of historical buildings including Philospher Smith's Hut and The Bischoff Hotel and is well worth exploring. With the main street only 300m away it is an easy walk past the lake.
The Roadhouse is prominent on Smith Street as you drive in or out of town. It is open 7am - 5pm 7 days per week and can supply all your basic grocery needs, as well as take away food and petrol.
Further along this road you will find the Waratah Museum, The Athaneum, the Post Office, the Stamper Mill and also the top of the waterfall. If you continue along past the old post office you will find the perfect location to view the waterfall across from the Bischoff Hotel.
While you are there stop in at The Bischoff Hotel for a drink or stay for dinner - they do a Monster Chicken Schnitzel that my son LOVES!
Wander around the lake - it's a nice easy stroll and keep an eye out for Platypus - they do
host_about:
I live on the NSW central coast at beautiful Lake Macquarie with my little man Christopher and fur baby Luna the Bulldog.

It was my love for photography and travel that first led to exploring Cradle Mountain and eventually resulted in searching for our own little holiday home nearby.  That is how we first came across "The Burrow" at Waratah - It truly was a labour of love turning it into something we are proud to call our own and happy to share with others. 

So nice we did it twice......

When presented with the opportunity to buy the adjoining unit we couldn't  resist.  Again it was time to roll up the sleeves and do some work  and so "The Wombat Burrow " was born.  

This was our chance to create a holiday home that offered us the flexibilty to do solo travels, family trips or  share our adventures with our extended family and friends . 

We are pleased to be able to share this with you and  we hope you enjoy your travels in  wonderful Waratah as much as we do.

name: Towering Gums Two
description:
You are tucked in a sheltered forest, surrounded by towering gum trees and ferns, on the slopes above a fertile valley, with the River Leven meandering through the plain. Beef and dairy cattle, pigs, goats and potatoes are farmed. A few minutes walk takes you to two sets of falls cascading down Preston Creek. Your accommodation is newly built as a guesthouse and your upper storey apartment gives lovely views of the bush. Cradle Mountain is a 75 minute drive.
We request quiet after 9 pm please.
neighborhood_overview:
Delaney and Preston Falls are 500 metres up our road.
Gunns Plains Caves and Wings Wildlife Park are 5 km away.
Our farm is nearby and if you are comfortable walking across paddocks and negotiating gates and electric fences then you are welcome to walk along the River Leven and watch for platypuses in our farm dam. In summer if it is hot you may like a swim. Further upstream our river flows through a spectacular canyon which can be viewed from above after a 20 km drive. Short and long walks can take you to the top or bottom of the canyon.
Ulverstone is our nearest town and has lovely beaches and a surf-lifesaving club if you would like to swim between the flags. The coastal drive from Ulverstone to Penguin is very pretty.

In an easy 15 minutes, you can walk from central Launceston along the banks of the Tamar River into the Gorge. From there, follow a pathway originally built in the 1890s along the cliff face looking down onto the South Esk River.

host_about:
Richard (Rick) and Suzanne (Suzi) are a married couple of twenty one years. They bought the property in 2002 and have spent the last nineteen years extensively renovating this huge WWI brick terrace house to its former glory while raising five children. Our home and our family are our passion. Since the fruits of this renovation have consumed our lives we’d love to share those fruits with others in the hopes that they feel a sense of connection with local history attached to the property and the historic beauty of the surrounding neighborhood. 
Salvator Suite sits at the front of the property facing the ocean and hills of West Hobart on level one of this 2 1/2 to 3 level house. The residential part of the house is situated above and behind the suite. The suite and structure above include a second storey deck which was part of a massive reconstruction process starting in 2010 and completed in 2011. The kitchenette/kitchen was built into the suite in October, 2019. The home is a 1915, double brick, Australian Craftsman Federation terrace house. One of the largest houses built by Mrs. Regina Cleary in the area. 
Many visitors over the years have marveled at the size and scope of the renovation that is not immediately apparent from street view. Although the property, according to many, has a certain unique charm and is a talking point among locals who walk past with their dogs and children. 
The Airbnb  ‘plan’ was to create something bold and eclectic but to also provide a calm, homey, artistic, quirky space for quiet, reflective getaways. 
Rick is a print journalist/sub-editor with 30+ years experience and has resided in Tasmania for the last twenty years, where he worked as a high level editor at The Mercury Newspaper for over twenty years. He was born and educated in Sharon,Massachusetts, USA and was active in many school athletics-(track and gridiron) and spent a lot of his free time with friends playing pick up basketball and field baseball throughout his childhood. His father was a WWII Veteran and an electrical engineer and his mother was Valedictorian of Norwood High School, Norwood, Massachusetts who went on to teach Special Education at high school, completed multiple masters degrees in Special Ed. and became the head of Special Education in her region. His mother was a devout Catholic and worked extensively in her church and with various historical societies over many many years. Rick is one of six siblings, all his other siblings still reside in the north eastern United States. 
Rick was elected Editor of the College newspaper at UMASS Amherst, Amherst, Massachusetts. He worked as a copy editor at newspapers in Connecticut, Victorville, California, San Bernardino, California and as a copy editor on the National Desk of the prestigious LA Times. Rick and Suzi met in 1998 and married in Los Angeles in 1999. Rick then emigrated to Tasmania in 1999. 
Suzi was born in Portsmouth, Hampshire, UK and emigrated to Tasmania in 1975, ten days after the Tasman Bridge disaster. She is a former Royal Navy brat who spent two years deployed in Singapore with her family, where she started her schooling at the Royal Naval school, HMS Terror, Sembawang in 1969. Her family and one other hired a camper Combi van and drove from Chong Pang to Penang, Malaysia, which was a very long drive with the accomodation having three songs on the jukebox- Glen Campbell, Neil Diamond & The Beatles! How Partridge Family is that?! Suzi has fond memories of traveling to different Naval homes throughout her childhood and especially H.M.S Ganges Cadet Training School in Ipswich, Suffolk. Suzi matriculated from Hobart Matriculation College. She was a hospital trained registered nurse at the Royal Hobart Hospital. She became an Australian citizen in 1981. She began her undergraduate degree in Classics, Latin, History and Ancient Greek in 2008, now currently on leave of absence.
Suzi is a self-confessed nerd & bibliophile, Doctor Who fan, music and arts fan. She is a great amateur cook, self-taught in many things including gardening and horticulture, classically trained in voice & flute, has a bad habit of reversing names, staring into the distance for ages while people are calling her name, (usually ‘muuuum’) loves natural history, ornithology, totally random facts & trivia. She also has a brother whom she doesn’t actually like very much, but he was a successful principal opera singer in Australia, who starred in Baz Lurhman’s epic production of La Boheme.  So, yeah, he has to be useful for advertising, something. 
Rick, being a journalist, has a wealth of socio-political knowledge at the Tasmanian, Australian & International level. He also kicks butt at Rock n Roll & general trivia. He’s a map guy, a geography guru, an amazing planner and math whiz. He likes his privacy and his hound dogs. He’s also incredibly generous, talented and smart. Suzi is the one who has obsessed over the ‘look’ and the ‘feel’ of your decor, layout, books, CDs, Knick knacks, linens and arranges small customized adjustments to the colour, style and arrangement of bedding and supplies for each stay that just doesn’t show up on the lists photos, but they are there. 
We are an introspective, educated, quiet family who love to connect over the silly little things that make us laugh. Our home is an expression of our love of art, history, music, learning & love of Tasmania’s environment-Flora & fauna. Also, living through a major renovation project, revamping this century-old home, has given us a great perspective on work and life. 
You will see that this behemoth of a building still needs some slight cosmetic work, because some prior owner of the property was a 70s concrete enthusiast. But, rest assured, all major renovations are complete and NO renovations of any kind will interrupt your stay. We have three adult daughters who lived the renovations with us and have their own homes now. They can attest to how disruptive and difficult it has been over the last 17 years. However, the results have been worth the hardship, and we hope you agree. Also, we are a well-travelled family having consistently visited the US over the last 14 years- Massachusetts, Maine, Vermont, New Hampshire, Connecticut, Rhode Island, Cape Cod, Los Angeles, Pasadena- California, San Diego, Ca.- Old Town and La Jolla, Hawaii- Waikiki Beach, New York City 3 times & a family getaway in Melbourne. Individually, Suzi has visited Sydney, Melbourne, Fiji-Coral Coast & Beachcomber Island, Japan- Yokosuka, Yokohama, Kyoto & Tokyo, England-London, York, Holy Island of Lindisfarne, Northumberland, Durham City, Sunderland-Durham, Middlesbrough-Teesside, The Yorkshire Moors, Newcastle & Scotland-Musselburgh & Edinburgh. We have driven around much of Tasmania as a family, camped on Maria Island and Bruny Island, stayed at Freycinet Lodge and camped at Freycinet National Park, stayed at Cradle Mountain Lodge and enjoyed the Dove Lake bushwalk. We have stayed at several old Tasmanian towns along the east & north west coasts of Tasmania and at the unique town of Strahan on the wild west coast, close to the World Heritage South West Wilderness. We have been to Hastings Caves & Thermal springs- large, Dolomite show caves unique to Tasmania. And many other escapades. Finally, we are generous, honest and loyal people who hope to share our stories, our love of Tasmania and our dear home with you.

name: GYPSY- Partridge Farm - Flinders Island
description: Gypsy is a unique new accommodation for Partridge Farm.  Gypsy has been purpose built using beautiful Tasmanian timbers.  From this tiny house you can experience spectacular sea views overlooking olive trees and orchard whilst backed on the  gum forest.  This 4.5 star building is fully self contained.
neighborhood_overview: Spectacular views with hobby farm experience
host_about:
Rob & Lorraine Holloway moved to the 30 acre property in 1980.  They cleared the block, grassed and fenced the paddocks & turned what was once ‘an ecological desert’ into a perma-cultural paradise.

In 1996, they named the property ‘Partridge Farm’ after the free range partridges and started holiday accommodation.  First was  The Bungalow which is bed and breakfast accommodation.  The Bungalow overlooks deer and sheep paddocks and has good views of Franklin Sound and outer Islands.  The Bungalow has a double bed and spa.

The Bungalow was very busy so they decided to build The Tophouse which is self contained and has 3 bedrooms.  The Tophouse  has views of Franklin Sound and is close to the Eucalypt forest.

After a few months they built The Retreat.  It is a self contained studio unit with a king size bed and also overlooks Franklin Sound and is close to the large eucalyptus forest. They have a large vegetable garden, many different varieties of fruit trees  and an olive grove.

They also cater for house guests on request and food is sourced mainly from Partridge Farm, cooked by Lorraine with meals delivered to the houses.  Partridge Farm has a liquor licence and in each house is an extensive wine and beer supply,  featuring local wine from Unavale Vineyard & a large selection of tasmanian wine.  There is an enclosed  bbq area with a wonderful brick pizza/bread oven.

Partridge Farm has a Rav 4 available for hire, so you can see the island at your leisure.

name: Seaside haven with breathtaking Maria Island views
description:
A dreamy seascape welcomes you to a colonial style, timber home on a 1.5acre bush block.
Maria Island stands proud between the Mercury passage and the Tasman Sea, with breathtaking views to Schouten Island and Freycinet beyond.
An ideal place for couples or friends to spend quality time together amongst local wildlife, flowers and gums. A home for complete relaxation and memory-making.
neighborhood_overview:
The Orford/Spring Bay Area has an abundance of walking and bike riding tracks as well as beautiful white sandy beaches with clear blue waters. The ferry leaves from neighbouring Triabunna for Maria Island daily.
There are three local hotels which serve great pub food and good restaurants serving local seafood, as well as a highly recommended Fish Van.
The area also boasts Spring Bay Distillery producing good quality whisky and gin. Darlington Vineyard situated in Orford is a must see.
Both Piermont and Devil's Corner offer some of Tasmanias' finest wine and are both under an hours drive.
A wellworth day trip 1 hour 40 mins from Merryway is Freycinet National Park. Here you can see some of Tasmania's most pristine and spectacular landscape.

name: Towering Gums Retreat
description:
Towering Gums Retreat
You are tucked in a sheltered forest, surrounded by towering gum trees and ferns, on the slopes above a fertile valley, with the River Leven meandering through the plain. Beef and dairy cattle, pigs, goats and potatoes are farmed in this valley. A few minutes walk takes you to two sets of falls cascading down Preston Creek. Your accommodation is newly built as a guesthouse and your lower storey apartment overlooks lovely views of the bush.
neighborhood_overview:
Delaney and Preston Falls are 500 metres up our road.
Gunns Plains Caves and Wings Wildlife Park are 5 km away.
Our farm is nearby and if you are comfortable walking across paddocks and negotiating gates and electric fences then you are welcome to walk along the River Leven and watch for platypuses in our farm dam. In summer if it is hot you may like a swim. Further upstream our river flows through a spectacular canyon which can be viewed from above after a 20 km drive. Short and long walks can take you to the top or bottom of the canyon.
Ulverstone is our nearest town and has lovely beaches and a surf-lifesaving club if you would like to swim between the flags. The coastal drive from Ulverstone to Penguin is very pretty.

neighborhood_overview:

When you stay at The Apartment, you are within easy walking distance to Hobart CBD (1.2km) , Salamanca and historic Battery Point. A short stroll(literally 2 minutes or 250m) around the corner, is our local: Hamlet community café; where the popular Rivulet track begins; busy with locals commuting to and from work and bike riders on weekends. The track is a lovely gentle walk providing accessible enjoyment of nature and fresh open space; you might even glimpse the resident platypus! Take an easy walk (10 minutes)along the Rivulet to theSouth Hobart (or SoHo in local slang) Village where you will find everything you need : the Salad Bowl a well-stocked local Providore offering a fine selection of local wines ,breads, cheese, fresh produce, and a deli section. Three good quality cafes, a post-office,
host_about:
Laura and Adam  found the building @245   in derelict condition in late 2014 and  were immediately  hooked on the challenge of bringing the building back to life and revealing its many possibilities; as a home, a working creative space and one to share with others . Originally from Argentina, Laura has loved travelling, especially for meeting new people and experiencing diverse cultures. After living in Sydney and travelling,  Twenty years ago  i moved to Tasmania.
30years ago,  Born and bred in Sydney, Adam came to Tassie on a 1960's BMW motorcycle and decided to stay. 
Both love old buildings and the stories they hold.  Unfortunately, since buying the building, i have survived a severe stroke;  so am not as mobile as i used to be. In spite of everything, Adam  carried on over these past years to restore and create a beautiful space of which we are both proud of. Adam is a designer maker, with his studio on the street level of @245 He also lives here part-time in the basement apartment and working in the ground floor studio. 
Our intended roles changed , and i am now taking care of the behind the scenes and communication with you, whilst Adam takes care of the apartment.
We have our family home out of town, down the beautiful Channel area. so we are lucky and privileged to have the best of both worlds. Looking forward to hosting you.:)

name: Eaglehawk Cottage- a nest for two
description:
Location, Location, Location! Eaglehawk Neck is the gateway to the Tasman Pensinsula, and this cottage is the perfect base to explore Port Arthur and Tasman National Park.
When we purchased this property in February 2020, the real estate described it as being "cute as a button"! Downstairs there is an open-plan kitchen, dining, living area and bathroom, and a sun-drenched covered courtyard. Upstairs there is a large bedroom complete with a Juliet balcony with glimpses of Eaglehawk Bay.
neighborhood_overview:
With so much to see and do you will not be disappointed with a trip to this majestic part of Tasmania. Come and see for yourself! Port Arthur Historic site is a 15 minutes drive away and this convict penal colony is Australia’s leading tourist attraction. The Remarkable cave is a further 3kms from Port Arthur and has breathtaking views of the coastline to Cape Raoul. The Three Capes walk is also located in this iconic wilderness area as well as the award winning Pennicott Tasman Island Cruise, a must see do in my eyes !
For keen surfers, Pirates Bay beach is only a 10 minutes walk away, and Ship Stern bluff and Roaring beach are both within a 30 min drive.
The location of our cottage is so quiet and peaceful and there's an abundance of wildlife right in the backyard!

neighborhood_overview:
Southport is known as Australia's southernmost settlement. It is now little more than a quiet holiday retreat and, looking at the shacks and small shops, it is hard to imagine that in the early 1800's it was Tasmania's second largest town and it was proposed as the capital of the colony. It was a bustling and dynamic convict station, whaling station, timber town and international port exporting timber to Europe. The modern appeal of the town lies in its away-from-it-all sleepiness. It is known for its excellent recreational fishing and the journey to Roaring Beach and Lady Bay rewards the traveller with beautiful white sand beaches and bull kelp near the rocky headlands.

Heading south towards Australia's southernmost point and the end of the road at Cockle Creek, is Lune River (the post office is recognised as the southernmost in Australia).
