Hi  
In 2013 I became a Super Host. I pride myself in providing amazing accomodation! 

I am world traveller, so my places are designed for absolute comfort with discerning travellers like myself in mind!

In February 2020 I completed a 10 week trip of Europe and I was desperate to find accommodation which encompassed all the things I like to offer to my guests.  

As a long standing Australian Super host, I strive to offer fabulous, unique, sparkling clean accommodation in 3 great Aussie destinations.

Firstly, the vibrant Sydney suburb of Newtown just 3km from the CBD, walk to Sydney Uni and RPA Hospital.  

In 2020 I added my unique Studio in Invermay, Launceston, Tasmania.

Next was the unique seaside, Hamlet of Penguin on Tasmania spectacular North, West Coast 

I have been offering accommodation for 23 years well before Air BnB Existed.

My point of difference is I have a ABN and my business is run to a professional standard with correct insurances etc. There are no common shared spaces. You are not squeezing into someone else home! My places are your home away from home.

Having returned in 2020 from travelling to Europe , 5 times to Santa Barbara (USA) in 2018, and in 2017  (kayaking in Antarctica and exploring Chile) and having worked in Geneva and NYC, I strive to offer guests what I need myself, a very comfortable bed, quality linen, quiet but interesting environment and a place to eat and work (a real table and chairs!), a couch, outdoor space and Wifi.

Here's my hosting story:

In 2000 I purpose built Studio Q as a stand alone Studio in my garden in O'Connor, Canberra a sought after leafy inner suburb .This property has been sold but Simon is now hosting Studio Q.

In Newton (Sydney) I have 2 fantastic apartments in the same complex with a roof top garden.  3 mins to the train and on "the strip" of restaurants, cafes, bookshops, movie and live theatres.  Please read more under Newtown Mews listings.  In 2020 I relocated to Launceston Tasmania and have a fabulous self contained apartment in the vibrant suburb of Inveraray and in November 2021 I added a upstairs and downstairs property in the jewel of the north west coast a little hamlet town of Penguin.

You will find my favourite local tips in each unit (i.e. best local cafes, great walks and the best the area has to offer).  I am a non intrusive host, and available by phone or email between 9-7pm,  I do not offer a 24 hr Concerige service but reviews conclude I am helpful and available in reasonable hours.

description:
Relax and enjoy stunning views in one of two architecturally designed cabins, nestled in the rolling hills, just outside the town of Sheffield and on the main road to Cradle Mountain.

You will be staying on our working farm that is home to platypus in the dams, a small herd of Speckle Park beef cattle and some fat and friendly goats. The farm is proudly centered eco-friendly, regenerative principles, promoting a healthy environment for birds, insects and other life to flourish.

Tracks to the summit offer a very different perspective. The return walk takes approximately 6 hours (depending on your level of fitness) as you travel through tall eucalypt forest, ancient Antarctic Beech, alpine vegetation and boulders to the summit (From where it’s possible to see the farm)

Mole creek is located on the other side of the Gogg Range- 25km and roughly 25 minutes’ drive from the farm. It’s possible to spend a full day exploring what this area has to offer. Attractions include the spectacular Mole Creek Caves, the Mole Creek Hotel and Trowunna Wildlife Park where you can meet Tasmanian Devils up close.

host_about: I am an almost retired teacher with a very simple yet enjoyable life. I have been blessed with 4 (adult) children, a most adorable granddaughter, and an equally adorable grand baby boy. I write but I don’t share it. Not yet. I love antique furnishings and belong in the last century. Travelling gives me much joy  and I love to meet other adventurers and the resultant conversation. I welcome visitors. I can hide away too. One cannot live without flowers, good coffee, and anything Italian. I value greatly the embrace of a blue sky, both in terms of sunshine and as a metaphor for life. My favourite travel destination thus far would have to be Venice. Actually, if I woke up anywhere in Italy I would be pretty pleased with myself. Finding a companion to play Scrabble with is now sorted with any enthusiastic guest who is willing to take on the challenge. I would be thrilled! I am fascinated with Poland and it’s history, love learning about the lives of British royalty and have a weakness for weird and wonderful vintage wall pockets. A passion for female jazz vocalists gives me much joy. Stacey Kent would be my eternal favourite. She sings and I potter! There are so many musicians who are somewhat enticing for me. Nina Simone for her heartbreaking story, her prowess with classical training as a pianist and her very important spiritual messages. Leonard Cohen, pure poetry in song! I suspect that if you visited and stayed, you would like to return. I firmly believe that one can learn something from everyone in this life. My motto is “kind words, loving gestures.”However, a spade remains a spade and I am certainly not backward in coming forward! Have a happy day and may Lady Luck travel with you.

host_about: My husband, Jeremy, & I moved to Stanley from Qld in 2019. The old cottage needed more work then we originally anticipated so we pulled it down, apart from one fireplace and chimney, and a team local expert builders re-built it to its near original design and added a modern rear extension. We now have a warm and cosy cottage where we can invite family, friends and guests to stay and enjoy the lovely village of Stanley & it’s surrounds. We have travelled extensively overseas and within Australia and love meeting new people and sharing stories. What better way to do this than host travelers in our own home! So we decided to offer bed & breakfast in the original cottage area. We hope people who stay with us enjoy our cottage and little village as much as we do.

Once the stomping ground for sailors, whalers and workmen, Salamanca Place in Hobart is now home to a vibrant cultural scene. Pop into warehouse art galleries, theaters, cafes and bars, and pick up boutique jewellery and one-off fashion pieces. name: Goodland’s Stable - Unique Accommodation
description: Goodland’s Stable, a heritage-listed building that now stands as unique luxury accommodation, centrally located in the classified historic village of Longford in Northern Tasmania. Experience the original 1830’s building, superbly furnished with William Morris fabrics to create a unique and unforgettable experience. The Stable has a queen size bed finished with luxurious linens, perfect for a couple seeking a romantic and tranquil escape.
neighborhood_overview: Close by is World Heritage listed Woolmers Estate Est. 1817, a unique and fascinating reflection of colonial life in Tasmania. It is preserved, and maintained in an original and authentic setting.  Brickendon Est. 1824 Colonial Farm Village, also World Heritage listed, is one of Tasmania’s oldest farming properties. The two estates are regarded as the most significant rural Estates in Australia having the second largest number of convict workers and still retaining a living history from early European settlement to the present day.
host_about:
Hi I'm Julie, 
I live in the village of Longford and my husband and I have recently restored the 1835 old Stable into unique accomodation. The building was derelict when we first found it. The ceiling beams in the Stable were fixed by the mortise and tenon joints and the whole structure of the roof sat on the convict brick walls with nothing anchoring it down, just sitting on top for all those years.  Amazingly the old stable has sat on foundations of simple bluestone with lime mortar for 160 years. It has been such fun restoring it and a joy working with and recycling the old original timbers, turning them into something special.
My love of gardening keeps me busy and I am a member of our local Garden Club.  Many plants and cuttings were given to me from dear friends, neighbours and people whose gardens I have visited. This is such a lovely part of gardening and it’s where many friendships have been made over many years.
We both enjoy listening to music, the outdoors, camping and travelling when we are able to.

description: Bright Water Lodge is a heritage cottage lovingly restored into a warm and inviting home situated in the pristine Upper Esk Valley along the banks of the South Esk River, tucked between Ben Lomond National Park and Mt Saddleback. neighborhood_overview:
Bright Water Lodge Farm Stay is a heritage Cottage, once the local community and dance hall during the Mathinna Golden Gate Mine and gold rush between 1888 and 1932. Now lovingly restored into a warm and comfortable haven for travellers.
Local attractions include the Ben Lomond mountain range & national Park with seasonal ski fields. Hiking trails abound. Evercreech national reserve is a local favourite, with some of the most magnificent and ancient trees in the world. The South Esk river, home to platypus which meanders it's way around the farm, is a stunning feature of this stay. Along its banks, you will discover wonderful fishing spots, swimming opportunities, bonfire & picnic spots and abundant native bird & wildlife. Perfect for photographers, artists and those simply wishing to soak up the incredible natural beauty and tranquility in this, one of Tasmania's best kept secrets.

We enjoy welcoming other people to share these experiences.

name: Villa Rochford - 1 Night Stay
description:
A unique place to rest and relax amongst Australia’s award-winning olive grove, Rochford Hall. Experience the peaceful and hilly countryside scenery of Kellevie, just a 40-minute drive from Hobart’s CBD and to the Port Arthur Historic Site, with only 10 minutes to the untouched and expansive coastline at Marion Bay.

The spacious Villa is suitable for up to five guests and is a perfect base for exploring the iconic East Coast and the Tasman Peninsula.
neighborhood_overview:
The expansive coastline of Marion Bay is only a 10-minute drive. The beach is perfect for a long stroll or a refreshing dip. Located in Marion Bay is Van Bone, a fine dining restaurant that uses produce from its market garden and orchards, the surrounding land (including our olive oil!) and sea. We recommend booking in advance. The recently opened Break Creek Vineyard Cellar Door is also in this area.

There are many other vineyards within 15 minutes, including Bangor Vineyard Shed and Cape Bernier Vineyard.

We highly recommend Hellfire Bluff Distillery, the oysters at Boomer Bay and The Cannery for lunch and dinner in Dunalley, which are all within 15 minutes’ drive.

Eaglehawk Neck is only a 30-minute drive, which boasts the famed Tessellated Pavement, as well as The Blowhole and Devil’s Kitchen.

Our favourite day walks on the Tasman Peninsula are Cape Hauy, Waterfall Bay, Remarkable Caves, Crescent Bay, Cape Raol and Shipsterns.

The area is studded with alpine tarns formed by glacial action between 8,000 and 20,000 years ago. Lunettes (alpine sand dunes) near Lake Augusta formed after the last glacial period. These are the only alpine lunettes in Australia!

Deer, wombats, spotted-tail quolls, wallabies, ringtail possums and long-nosed potoroos can be seen by careful observers in the evening but during day there is plenty of birdlife including raucous yellow-tailed black cockatoos and majestic Tasmanian wedge-tailed eagles.

host_about:
Hi. We have been married for over 40 years and have a shared passion for travel, which we have passed on to our children. It has also helped that Glenn shares an Austrian heritage, and Gina a Greek heritage through respective fathers. We have travelled extensively to visit family and friends and discover new and wonderful places and can't wait to hear your stories of travel.

We have lived here all our lives and are very excited with the direction Tasmania is heading - especially as we also share a passion for great food and fine wines! We now have some of the finest foods and drinks in the world with an internationally renowned museum, festivals and marvellous natural rugged landscapes.

LEBRENA (South Hobart)
Glenn fell in love with the beautiful grand old Lebrena, a Henry Hunter designed 1876 sandstone mansion. For those of you who choose to stay at Lebrena, we share with you now as an AirBnB experience while we begin the long journey to return it to its former glory. We hope you will stop here a while and enjoy all that there is from our humble beginnings of something that hopefully will turn into a majestic and grand project.

GRANDVIEW (Battery Point)
Those who stay with us at Grandview, it is hard to reconcile the house dated 1885 you now see compared to the dilapidated frame we started with. From the underpinning required to get her standing proud (54 holes approx 1.6 metres deep) to the new renovation, fit out and landscaping, we have done it all ourselves over the last three years. We are still finessing the experience for people and appreciate feedback to help us make it a perfect stay for all. We have named the house Grandview after the original street name of St George’s Terrace.

name: Fork it Farmstay
description:
Stargaze beneath a brilliant night sky, breathe in the fresh air, and enjoy delicious produce straight from the farm.

Situated in the heart of the Pipers Brook Wine Region, your itinerary is likely to be teeming with sojorns to cellar doors. Or you could simply put your feet up, laze in the Tasmanian sun, take in the farm and enjoy a simply delicious charcuterie platter.
neighborhood_overview:
Lebrina is small town located about 38 kilometres north-east of Launceston, right in the heart of the Pipers Brook Wine Region. The Lebrina location and climate are comparable to the Champagne region in France and is consequently home to outstanding sparkling wine.

The locality offers easy access to the North East being a short travel distance to a large number of renowned recreational destinations including Launceston, Bridestowe Lavender Farm, Derby mountain bike facilities and the world class golf courses and other attractions around the seaside town of Bridport.
host_about:
In 2017 we said 'fork it' to the stresses of city life, packed up our lives to become ethicurean farmers. 

We are a small-scale family run farm, consisting of 12 Berkshire breeding sows, a small herd of cattle, sheep, ducks, geese and bees. We also grow most of our own herbs and vegetables.

Our goal is to produce ethical, flavourful food for the local market. Over the past 20 months we have developed our all-natural product range (in our on-farm facility), to utilise the whole animal, which has recently expanded to include our pasture raised duck, goose, beef & lamb.  We are also currently developing a range of products which incorporate sustainably sourced Tassie wild game. 

We put a lot of love into everything we do at Fork it Farm and we love sharing our farm.

Harrington Lane sits right in the heart of inner-city Hobart, surrounded by a mix of historic charm, vibrant culture, and modern comforts. The area is an ideal base for exploring Hobart’s highlights, all within a short stroll. Salamanca Place, with its lively market on Saturdays, boutique shops, and art galleries, is just minutes away. neighborhood_overview:
One of Tasmania’s historic towns, the picturesque Evandale sits on the banks of the South Esk River, 18 kilometres south of Launceston. Named after early colonial explorer and Surveyor-General George Evans, the town is famous for its late-Georgian and early Victorian buildings with relatively untouched streetscape. It also hosts a popular Sunday market and is the annual World Penny Farthing Championships, along with the Glover Prize, named after the father of Australian landscape painting, John Glover.

Many attractions, amenities and eateries are right at your doorstep! The Clarendon Arms hotel serves up British Pub style meals. This hotel arguably has one of the best beer gardens in northern Tasmania. Additional noteworthy eateries include, No.10, the Evandale Cafe, and the Prince of Wales Hotel. The cottage is also within walking distance to a small convenient store, newsagent, post office and right near the Anteiku antique store.

name: RiversEdge_Queenstown Western Tasmanian Wilderness
description:
This home has been set up for families and or friends with fun and comfort in mind. Western wilds of Tasmania is a destination filled with adventure. Whether trekking through National Parks, mountain biking the mammoth Mt Owen or the Silver City trails or exploring all the disappearing towns to riding river rapids, there is an experience for everyone in Tasmania’s west.

A fully renovated 1940’s cottage, we have added every comfort to ensure that you have a wonderful stay.
neighborhood_overview:
Austin Street is a quiet street, walking distance to the town centre. Just around the corner from the town’s public swimming pool & skate ramp park.

The house faces north and receives all day sun. That is when the town built amongst a rainforest enjoys sunshine. 😃

The train tracks that the popular tourist train, West Coast Wilderness Railway, runs on is also on the way to town. Both little and big kids enjoy watching the train pull out of the station.

The Queen River runs along our back yard and makes for a nice little stroll.

The orange colour of the Queen River is the result of the towns mine, the longest running copper mine in the world. With their poor environmental past practices, the trainings used to be flushed into the river, but in the early 1920’s, we’re diverted into a tailings dam. Even more than 100 years on the Queen River is still a dead zone. The locals lie in hope that nature will persist and fix past damage done.
host_about: We love living in Lutruwita (Tasmania,) with its pristine landscapes and incredible produce.  Our family enjoy mountain bike riding, anything water wise and relish new adventures and experiences, it’s all about the destination when we travel.  However, we certainly enjoy beautiful welcoming accommodation and appreciate stunning local cuisine and wine.

neighborhood_overview:

And that is probably coming soon. Mmmm, krill.

The prettiest post-office, the ugliest laundromat and the second best boutique cinema in Australia IMHO (sorry, Govindas in Sydney wins). All 15 minutes stroll from the CBD and 23 minutes walk to Salamanca.

neighborhood_overview:
One of Tasmania's historic towns, the picturesque Evandale sits on the banks of the South Esk River, 18 kilometres south of Launceston. Named after early colonial explorer and Surveyor-General George Evans, the town is famous for its late-Georgian and early Victorian buildings with relatively untouched streetscape. It also hosts a popular Sunday market and is the annual World Penny Farthing Championships, along with the Glover Prize, named after the father of Australian landscape painting, John Glover.

The beloved Evandale market is not to be missed, with unique creations and hidden gems every Sunday, located on Logan Road. The market holds a lovely country charm, providing a great range of fresh local produce, tasty food vans and stalls with local crafts, bric-a-brac, and even pony rides! neighborhood_overview:

The area is popular with people looking for adventure while also quietly immersing themselves in the wildness of the Tasmanian west coast. You'll find challenging landscapes and surf breaks if you're into outdoor activities. If it's peace and quiet you're looking for you'll find wide open stretches of beach, a tranquil river and dramatic rainforest. There's also a very healthy population of protected Tassie Devils, you may get lucky and see one.

We share the reserve with an abundance of wildlife. Drive slow after dark!!

neighborhood_overview:
Sorell is one of Tasmania's oldest farming towns and today is a busy regional center and the last major town on the way to the Tasman Peninsula and the East Coast.

Surrounded by farmland, fields, and a growing suburban commuter community, Sorell's idyllic location and closeness to Hobart attract residents and visitors alike.

A walk around town reveals pieces of history on and off the main street, with impressive historic churches like St George's and Sorell's oldest building, our very own Sorell Barracks, now colonial accommodation.

A visit to a local antique and vintage store will reveal even more treasures from the past.

Sorell is rich in produce too. At the Sorell Fruit Farm, you can pick all kinds of stone and berry fruits, including rare heritage varieties.

Just west of Sorell is the Orielton Lagoon, a nature reserve with locally significant flora and fauna and migratory shorebirds that rest here on their international journey

name: The Lake House-“Luxury in the Wilderness”
description:
An elegant spacious retreat for up to 4 adults offering luxury self catering accommodation.

Situated in a beautiful lake and garden setting in the Central Highlands Wilderness surrounded by many trout fishing lagoons and National Parks.

Fish, walk, sit or use it as a base.

Enjoy the birdlife or maybe you will be lucky enough to see the local wombats, wallabies or platypus. If it all gets too much it's fully internet connected.

It is a truly mood altering experience in all its seasons.
neighborhood_overview:
Bradys lake is a small shack community in the Tasmanian wilderness.

Situated nearly in the geographic centre of Tasmania it is surrounded by forest and trout filled lakes between the Mt Field and Lake St Clair National Parks enroute to the Western Wilds.

This makes it an ideal base for soaking up the wilderness, local exploration or as a central stopping off point whilst touring or a specific spot particularly for fishing.

The original homes are from the 1950s era and many remain as colorful classic holiday shacks along the lake edge.

The nearest small store is at 381 Marlborough Rd Bronte Park on the B11 about 10mins drive away towards Miena. It has diesel but not petrol.

The bigger townships of Deloraine and Miena to the north and Ouse to the southeast are 30-40 mins drive so its best to stock up and get fuel and supplies on the way in.

As it is in the Highland Lakes area it regularly snows in winter

neighborhood_overview:
There are few places as special as Maria Island. This extraordinary national park, located a short distance off the coast of Triabunna, is a blend of World-Heritage-listed, convict-era architecture, early 20th century industrial heritage, diverse and beautiful natural landscapes and abundant, protected wildlife.

The township of Triabunna is the departure point for the ferry to Maria Island and is a short 15-20 minute drive from Twamley Farm.

When you step onto Maria Island a sense of freedom washes over you and the “unplugged” magic of the Island becomes immediately apparent. The Island creates a childlike desire to just wander and explore what is a natural playground filled with wonders to discover. There are no shops or vehicles on the Island.
host_about: Our family has lived and farmed in the Buckland area on the East Coast of Tasmania since the 1840s. We're also very excited about where our food and wine culture is going in Tasmania and so aim to bring you some of the best of Tasmanian products in your experience. We hope you truly enjoy your stay and discover something a little unique beyond the usual holiday houses and B&B's along our beautiful East Coast of Tasmania.

name: picture this - Cherry Tree Hill
description:
Picture this… Located in the heart of a serene Tasmanian bush setting along the scenic Great Eastern Drive, Cherry Tree Hill invites you to experience true tranquility and immerse yourself in the beauty of nature.

Choose to soak in a bath under the stars or unwind in the sauna, luxurious amenities await to help you unwind and rejuvenate. Here, you can truly unplug from the stresses of everyday life and immerse yourself in a bush escape unlike any other.

To the east and north we are bordered by two vineyards: Devil's Corner (just a 2-minute drive and offering cellar door wine sales and restaurant) and Freycinet Winery. (just a 5-minute drive and offering cellar door wine sales). Delightful, yes!

To the west is crown and private land, all large and rural. Getting away from it all is what Cherry Tree Hill offers, as well as plenty of exploring in the bush. It is possible to lose one's bearings so do take care!

Friendly Beaches is the nearest beach and is absolutely stunning. It's on the way to the spectacular Freycinet Peninsula, where a day trip or three is a must. Picturesque Bicheno is a 20 km drive north where there are many glorious beaches, penguin tours, sightseeing, bush walking and cafes. This is also a great place to replenish supplies. Sweet Swansea is 23 kms south, offering incredible views of the Great Oyster Bay and a chance to pick up those last-minute supplies on your way through from Hobart or Lau

name: Wombat Hollow
description:
Wombat Hollow is situated in the beautiful mural town of Sheffield within driving distance to all the local facilities, shops, and cafes. This property offers a gorgeous three-bedroom country retreat with a private garden.

Wombat Hollow is fully self-contained and accommodates 1-6 people . Also it is a pet friendly.

It is ideal for a couple, a family or a group of friends. Central to many tourist attractions including Lake Barrington, Mount Roland, Mole Creek Caves and Cradle Mountain.
host_about:
The Hut@The Good place and Tiny Cradle @ The Good Place where is the place you can be yourself and don't give a damn about what is happening in the world. Searching for your own-self, in touch with your inner-self and connecting with the mother nature and  be peaceful.

We are friendly, easy-going couple.  We have three young children. We live in our hobby farm. We have three cats - their names are Silvester, Trubble and Captain Raymond Holt. We have two goats  - their names are Heidi and Helga. Along with chickens - I think the kids name them but I can't remember lol.  Finally we have 27 sheeps,  don't ask us all their names, lol sorry about that. One clingy member in the family is - Jake the dog.  Our farm is never ending  with animals around.  All the animals are friendly except the sheep and chicken.  Otherwise, all our guests are most welcome to visit them and pat them. 

We try to make everything at home.  We enjoy cooking, good company and a glass of wine or beer and local produces.  We can take you to Mount Roland hiking and bush walking down at the back of our property if the weather allowed.  If you enjoy nature and farm life.  We would love to accommodate you. 

It is only 45-50 mins travel to Cradle Mountain, 40 mins drive to Devonport, short distance drive to Mole Creek and Deloraine, 5 mins drive down the road to Tasmazia and Lake Barrington Rowing Course and also it is only 15 mins drive to the Mural town of Sheffield. Our property is surrounded by stunning mountains, valley and forest.  You can get in touch with your inner self and spiritual side with nature. We like to share our travel experience and tales with you.  

We respect our guest privacy.
Communication is important to us.
We do our best to accommodate our guest request. 
We might not be the 5 star hotel but we love to give our guest the best of our hospitality.  Guests treat us with respect and vice verse.  
We are easy going, fun loving and lay back family.  We love a good story telling and adventure to share. 


We can also be contacted from WHAT S APP, WE CHAT, LINE App.

name: Gatekeepers Lodge - A Historic Hobart Experience
description:
Gatekeeper’s Lodge is your escape to a simpler time. A place of iconic Tasmanian history where the plastered walls tell stories of days gone by. Be pampered in the luxe walk-in shower big enough for 2 or keep the clawfoot bath all to yourself. Chase the dappled light around the beautifully styled yet humble interior or watch the sunset over the sprawling cottage gardens.

Welcome to the smell of fresh stoneground sourdough and locally sourced breakfast provisions.

Find us @gatekeepers_lodge
neighborhood_overview:
Lenah Valley is situated in the foothills of Mount Wellington, just north of Hobart CBD, walking distance to the culinary delights of north hobart but out of the hustle and bustle where you'll find a more peacefull side of Hobart life . With a bus stop 20 metres from our front door, you can get around town with ease

A beautiful quiet northern suburb, close to all the amenities you could require. Only a short trip into the city, or 10 minutes north to MONA.

Lenah Valley was originally known as Kangaroo Bottom, later Kangaroo Valley and Sassafras Valley.
host_about: My partner Arianne and I moved to Tasmania from the mainland in 2021 in search of the good life. Boy did we find it! We became the custodians of the heritage Gatekeepers Lodge in 2022. With a love for all things old and unique, we set out to provide an experience. Not just a roof over your heads. We poured our souls into the Lodge to create something special that we can share with you all.

name: Stapleton Beach House at Spring Beach
description:
Relax in this beautifully appointed beach house overlooking Maria Island at Spring Beach, Tasmania. Nestled between Spring and Stapleton beaches- just a short 5-7 minute walk to each, the house has four bedrooms spread over two levels. Upstairs an open plan living/dining room adjoins the kitchen with a deck overlooking the ocean, along with three bedrooms for the family.

Downstairs, escape to the parents retreat or kids rumpus room- with a TV, lounge and a queen bedroom.
neighborhood_overview:
Spring Beach has a scattering of beach houses and shacks on the quiet and pristine east coast of Tasmania, just an hours drive from Hobart.

There are no shops or facilities at the beach, but there are cafes and a supermarket at Orford, a 5 minute drive away.

Neighbouring the Launceston CBD, the suburb of Invermay is a lovely part of Launceston. Built on the mud flats, before the flood levy was built, Invermay was prone to flooding. Many homes still bear the scars of the floodwaters to this day in stained floorboards and plaster. A suburb traditionally known as an industrial suburb, Invermay now enjoys a new and funky lease on life. Although there is still some commerce peppered throughout the suburb, the gorgeous weatherboard cottages are now sought after and are lovingly being restored back to their former glory!

There are numerous eateries, bars and takeaways nearby, as well as a Kmart, a Coles supermarket, newsagency, chemist, bakery and liquor outlet! Nearby restaurants and eateries of note are Me Wah Chinese restaurant and Café Blue. neighborhood_overview:
Montagu Bay is a suburb of Hobart, Tasmania, on the eastern shore of the Derwent River, about four kilometres from the city centre of greater Hobart. It is a small primarily residential suburb located between Rosny, Rose Bay and Lindisfarne and is centred on a small bay of the same name, formerly known as Smelting Works Bay. The bay has a boat ramp and jetty, and is frequently filled with yachts and other vessels at anchor.

Montagu Bay is notable for its views of the Derwent River, Tasman Bridge, and Mount Wellington. It is home to Montagu Bay Primary School and has two large cricket ovals, one next to the school, and another built on landfill in the bay itself. The school is also home to a sculpture of a giant hand carved from pine wood. Another feature is the boat building shed which has existed since the early 1920s. The Eastern shore cycle path travels through Montagu Bay along the shoreline.

A National Trust classified Georgian village, Evandale is popular with tourists for its unspoiled heritage homes, community and business buildings, charming streetscapes, parks, and early graveyards.

Evandale is home to the world-famous annual Glover Art Prize, the National Penny Farthing Championships, and the ever popular Sunday Markets.

It's a great place to shop, eat and play.

There are two pubs, a great little BYO restaurant (No.10), Ingleside Bakery, a well-stocked supermarket and a takeaway.

name: Dorset Hotel in Derby - Queen Room
description: Home of the Blue Derby Mountain Bike Trails. Get back to the basics with good old fashioned country hospitality. Stay in the renown Dorset Hotel, which features 10 newly renovated rooms, brand new shared bathrooms and a breakfast room. We offer bike friendly amenities. The onsite restaurant serves excellent pub grub daily and happy hour is offered every Friday. There is a great outdoor beer garden, public bar with eight ball table.
neighborhood_overview:
The Dorset Hotel, is one of Derby's most convenient accommodation options, located right in the heart of Derby. Our onsite pub offers a fun friendly atmosphere with great food and features some of Tassie's best craft beers, wines and spirits.

The River Trail, which starts from our Beer Garden, takes you along the banks of the Ringarooma river, providing direct access to the suspension bridge (which takes you across the river to the Lake Trail and Wochya-Upta), past the Pump track and on to the Blue Derby Trailhead. At the end of your day, all you have to do is roll down to the pub, rack your bike, enjoy a few bevies in the beer garden while dinner cooks, tell a few lies, then roll up to bed. EAT. RIDE. SLEEP. REPEAT.
host_about:
I love Tassie and have recently been lucky enough to acquire Dorset Hotel in Derby.  I have been running a popular and well established pub and accommodation on Bruny Island for the past 10 plus years and decided to branch out to other wonderful regional parts of Tasmania.

The original Dorset Hotel was a single story weather board building, it was replaced by the current building in 1911 and withstood the flood that destroyed much of the town in 1929. The pub has a photo wall describing the town’s rich tin mining history and the devastating effect of the 1929 flood.

The pub has been extensively renovated. We have put in a beer garden that seats 50 and installed a commercial kitchen. The bar and dining rooms have been painted and refurnished. We began serving meals in May 2018. The pub currently offers 10 newly renovated rooms, brand new shared bathrooms, and a breakfast room. The new roof is on and the pub exterior has now been re-painted.

name: Dorset Hotel in Derby - Twin Room
description: Home of the Blue Derby Mountain Bike Trails. Get back to the basics with good old fashioned country hospitality. Stay in the renown Dorset Hotel, which features 10 newly renovated rooms, brand new shared bathrooms and a breakfast room. We offer bike friendly amenities. The onsite restaurant serves excellent pub grub daily and happy hour is offered every Friday. There is a great outdoor beer garden and public bar.
neighborhood_overview:
The Dorset Hotel, is one of Derby's most convenient accommodation options, located right in the heart of Derby. Our onsite pub offers a fun friendly atmosphere with great food and features some of Tassie's best craft beers, wines and spirits.

The River Trail, which starts from our Beer Garden, takes you along the banks of the Ringarooma river, providing direct access to the suspension bridge (which takes you across the river to the Lake Trail and Wochya-Upta), past the Pump track and on to the Blue Derby Trailhead. At the end of your day, all you have to do is roll down to the pub, rack your bike, enjoy a few bevies in the beer garden while dinner cooks, tell a few lies, then roll up to bed. EAT. RIDE. SLEEP. REPEAT.
host_about:
I love Tassie and have recently been lucky enough to acquire Dorset Hotel in Derby.  I have been running a popular and well established pub and accommodation on Bruny Island for the past 10 plus years and decided to branch out to other wonderful regional parts of Tasmania.

The original Dorset Hotel was a single story weather board building, it was replaced by the current building in 1911 and withstood the flood that destroyed much of the town in 1929. The pub has a photo wall describing the town’s rich tin mining history and the devastating effect of the 1929 flood.

The pub has been extensively renovated. We have put in a beer garden that seats 50 and installed a commercial kitchen. The bar and dining rooms have been painted and refurnished. We began serving meals in May 2018. The pub currently offers 10 newly renovated rooms, brand new shared bathrooms, and a breakfast room. The new roof is on and the pub exterior has now been re-painted.

At 'Just Relax' you are right on the beach! You overlook your own patch of paradise from the deck chair, open plan living space, bedrooms and kitchen! Swoon over the vintage car collection and get your bearings before a trip west to Stanley. You’ll see the Nut as a spectacular land mass on the horizon before you climb it. At the base, wander along the main street from gallery to boutique and feel like you’ve stepped back in time.

Be guided by the visitor experts into the spectacular Tarkine. There are walk trails that take you into Australia’s largest tract of temperate rainforest and coast

name: @sea 2escape designer built house with 360 views
description: Nestled between the bush and the beach, at the end of a quiet cul-de-sac, @sea 2escape is a self contained, brand new build, uniquely designed, one bedroom, one bathroom and full kitchen/living room house with 360 degree views of the seashore, a short walk to Bicheno centre. Sink into a Houn Pine King size bed with a quality mattress, a choice of pillows and views of the sea from your bed. Enjoy the open plan living room/gourmet fully equipped kitchen or the panoramic views from the verandah.
neighborhood_overview: @sea 2escape is set against the lush grove of Eucalypts which surround Bicheno, in the Seascape subdivision, at the end of a quiet cul-de-sac. Expansive views of the East Coast coastline and Bicheno township stretch out before you. Watch the local eagle pair soar through the treetops riding the thermals or enjoy the magpies teaching their babies how to be the best magpie they can be. It's a short walk to Red Bill Beach where at low tide you can walk across to Diamond Island or come back at dusk, join a penguin tour and wait patiently for the elusive local penguins to creep up the beach to their waiting chicks. Join the locals in town for a morning coffee, an amazing pastry and chat at Governors, Little Bay Patisserie, or something a little different at Sandbar. The Bicheno Bakery has excellent coffee and award winning pies and get the cool barista vibe next door at Darks. Enjoy a relaxed swim at Waubs Bay and mix it with the local regulars who swim around the bay or out to Diamond Isla
host_about: We have been coming to Bicheno for holidays for almost 30 years and have always loved it here. Bicheno is a favourite holiday destination for Tasmanians because of the clear blue water, blinding white sand and striking granite rocks and the peaceful environment. In 2019 we made the decision to close up our allied health practice in Hobart and retire up here. We love it so much here we wanted to share the beauty of our place with visitors by building a brand new, purpose built accomodation house on our half acre property which takes advantage of the expansive views of the East Coast seashore and Bicheno township, set against the lush grove of Eucalypt forest behind us. We designed the accomodation house to be architecturally striking, it's a rectangular box, which looks like it's floating on a pedestal of pure white blocks, with as much glass as possible facing East to maximise the water views. We have used Porters paints to reflect the soft hues of the sea and sand. neighborhood_overview:
The most distinctive landmark in Stanley is “The Nut”, an old volcanic plug discovered by the explorers Bass and Flinders in 1798, who officially named it Circular Head. It has steep sides and rises to 143 metres with a flat top. It is possible to walk to the top of “The Nut” via a steep track, but most visitors choose to ride the chairlift.

Stanley is the main fishing port on the northwest coast of Tasmania and was named after Lord Stanley, a British Secretary of State for the Colonies in the 1840s. A port was opened in 1827 and the first school opened in 1841. In 1880 the first coach service between Stanley and Burnie was established.

name: Quirindi Cabin by Tiny Away
description:
Welcome to Quirindi Cabin! The ideal tiny homes Tasmania getaway, nestled in an 8-acre property that has been with the family for three generations beginning with the land host's grandfather and was later rebuilt by his son in 2013. Surrounded by bushland and grassland with abundant wildlife to keep you company.

Perfect for coastal adventures near stunning beaches, crustacean delights, and all that Dunalley has to offer.
neighborhood_overview:
Quirindi Cabin by Tiny Away is located in a fishing village in Dunalley, 47 min drive from Hobart via Tasman Hwy. Located in one of Australia's best fishing and bay-side destinations, with endless things for you to choose from. Nearby Marion Bay Tavern, Primrose Sands Beach, and Hobart just 55 kilometres away.

Our local recommendation:

- Tessellated Pavement is a natural marvel near Hobart. Its rock formations resembling tiles draw photographers and nature enthusiasts. Explore the intricate crevices housing Tasmanian crabs that adds allure to this wilderness gem.
- Tasman's Arch is a majestic natural bridge sculpted by the Tasman Sea along the Tasman Peninsula's sea cliffs. It offers breathtaking views from an observation platform. Explore this stunning geological wonder near Eaglehawk Neck.
- Dunalley Bakery is a popular place that bakes delicious pastries and pies that tourists often visit.
- Bangor Wine & Oyster Shed is an award-winning vineyard
host_about: Escape the noise and reconnect with what truly matters. Tiny Away offers eco-conscious, design-led tiny houses in thoughtfully curated settings. Each stay is a chance to slow down, unplug, and recharge, whether you're looking for solitude, stillness, or a meaningful moment with someone you love.

neighborhood_overview:
The region is best known for creating cool-climate wines from the brisk wind blowing in from the southern ocean and down from the surrounding Meehan Ranges. Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Riesling are the most popular grape varieties in the Coal River Valley wine region; working well with the crisp, fresh attributes of a cool-climate wine.

The Coal River Valley wine region is still quite young with the first winery popping up in the 1970s, since then a handful of boutique cellar doors have opened up, each showcasing the great flavours of Tasmania.

The weather conditions can be harsh in Tasmania, especially in the winter, but the surrounding hills of the Valley provide shelter from the westerly winds. Though winter brings its own aspects of beauty, the best time to visit the Coal River Valley is around January to March. The valley takes on a stunning summery vibe, and the energy is infectious.

neighborhood_overview: Uchi is ideally located, just a few minutes walk to the southern end of Redbill Beach, one of Tasmania's best surfing beaches. Waubs Bay, also known as Safety Beach, is just a kilometer away and is best for small children. The walk to the centre of the village from Uchi is very picturesque. You can also do the full coastal walk from Uchi to the Blowhole and back and stop in at a cafe for a great coffee on the way back. It's a nice way to spend a morning. You will pass the Gulch where you might see seals or dolphins. There are also many penguin burrows around and you can peek inside and occasionally find a baby waiting for dinner. At low tide you can start a different walk from Uchi and head to Diamond Island by walking along Redbill Beach - the entrance is only a few minutes away. Be sure to return to the beach before the tide comes in! Diamond Island is home to many little penguins to you need to be careful where you walk. The far side of the island is very beautiful.

Discover why guests say we’re the best Airbnb they’ve stayed at. Guests love the thoughtful touches that immediately make them feel at home. They rave about our breakfast hamper, sourdough bread and comfy mattresses and pillows.

Local bird life often appear near the cottage, which we have lovingly named ‘Cacatua’ after our white and black cockatoos.

————————————————
neighborhood_overview:
The White Gum trees in our area are home to the beautiful but endangered Forty Spotted Pardalote birds.

As we are located in a bush setting, you will no doubt experience the beauty of nature. During the day we will often see white cockatoos, black cockatoos, kookaburras and a local echidna who sometimes wanders through.

You may be lucky to spot some of our nocturnal wildlife including owls, small bats, possums, pademelons, bandicoots and wallabies - and you will likely hear the frogs on dusk.

At times, nature may bring along visitors who are less cute and cuddly, for example mosquitos, flies, spiders, ants, jack jumpers and very rarely a snake. The cottage is fumigated and we recommend closing the fly screens when the sliding doors are open. We have mosquito repellent and fly spray in the cottage for you should it be needed.

While at the cottage, you may hear birds chirping, the neighbouring sheep or cow in the distance, children or dogs

host_about:
Hi. We have been married for over 40 years and have a shared passion for travel, which we have passed on to our children. It has also helped that Glenn shares an Austrian heritage, and Gina a Greek heritage through respective fathers. We have travelled extensively to visit family and friends and discover new and wonderful places and can't wait to hear your stories of travel.

We have lived here all our lives and are very excited with the direction Tasmania is heading - especially as we also share a passion for great food and fine wines! We now have some of the finest foods and drinks in the world with an internationally renowned museum, festivals and marvellous natural rugged landscapes.

LEBRENA (South Hobart)
Glenn fell in love with the beautiful grand old Lebrena, a Henry Hunter designed 1876 sandstone mansion. For those of you who choose to stay at Lebrena, we share with you now as an AirBnB experience while we begin the long journey to return it to its former glory. We hope you will stop here a while and enjoy all that there is from our humble beginnings of something that hopefully will turn into a majestic and grand project.

GRANDVIEW (Battery Point)
Those who stay with us at Grandview, it is hard to reconcile the house dated 1885 you now see compared to the dilapidated frame we started with. From the underpinning required to get her standing proud (54 holes approx 1.6 metres deep) to the new renovation, fit out and landscaping, we have done it all ourselves over the last three years. We are still finessing the experience for people and appreciate feedback to help us make it a perfect stay for all. We have named the house Grandview after the original street name of St George’s Terrace.

description: Escape the crowd and traffic this summer in Turners Beach. Our house has been stunningly designed and renovated to ensure comfort no matter what the weather in Tasmania. This relaxing self-contained home is suited to couples, group or families. A great NW base. 150m flat stroll to the beach and 300m to the local Berry Patch Cafe. neighborhood_overview:
Turners Beach is a small village. We have two shops: the local service station/take away shop over the bridge and the Turners Beach Berry Patch. People tend to enjoy the small town community feel. It is a place to unwind. There are two park/plays areas, little bush tracks to explore, a free outdoor tennis court and a bowls club. Locals enjoy walking the 2km beach, braving the cold for a swim or surf and having a fish down at the river. There is also a boat ramp. Our beach is lined with beach rocks that change formation with the tide. There is also a cycling/walking track that goes from Turners Beach to the local town of Ulverstone.

The nearest town of Ulverstone is a quick 5min drive west and the city of Devonport is a 10min drive east. This is where you will find major supermarkets, retail shops, restaurants, cafes, doctors, chemists and pubs.

There are plenty of beautiful places to visit in the north west. The iconic Cradle Mountain makes for a good day trip.

Jess and Andrew:)

name: Luxury yurt glamping at Littlegrove
description:
Nestled in an olive grove with views over Bruny Island’s famous Fluted Cape, our yurts offer the ultimate romantic glamping experience, with private bathroom and cooking facilities and an outdoor bath and fire pit for star gazing.

Each yurt is furnished with vintage wares collected from all over the world, an internal wood fire, timber floors, and wool lined walls for cosy nights.

Double glazed windows look out over the grove and surrounding forest which wraps 360 degrees around our farm.
neighborhood_overview:
Littlegrove is located in Adventure Bay, Bruny Island - voted the fifth most beautiful beach in Australia in 2023. There is a well-stocked local shop, ATM, and petrol pump in Adventure Bay, as well as somewhere you can purchase alcohol.

Enjoy the water sports of your choice, including surfing, snorkelling, swimming, or fishing - you can launch a boat from the ramp in Adventure Bay into some of the world's cleanest and most pristine waters.

There are some great local hikes nearby, including the Fluted Cape, Mavista Falls, and Mount Mangana, which are all under a 10 minute drive from our farm. Wildlife enthusiasts will enjoy the prolific birdlife, local sealife (including migrating whales in the right season), and native Australian animals, including Bruny Island's famed white wallaby.

Just a few minutes drive from Littlegrove, you'll find tourist attractions including Pennicott's Wildlife Cruise, Bruny Island Chocolate Factory, and Bruny Island Raspbe
host_about: We had a wild idea in 2017 to move our family from the other side of the world to a little olive grove on an island, off an island, off an island at the bottom of the world. We love sharing our little slice of paradise with guests - you can usually find us working in the garden, renovating our ramshackle farm house, or tending to our menagerie of animals.

description: Coastal retreat - three hectares of grounds nestled between foothills and sea, with access to private coves, rock pools and costal paths. neighborhood_overview:
We are on a separate private ocean front property that is a 5 minute drive to pristine Four Mile Beach and on the Great Eastern Drive.

The closest shops are in the beach town of Scamander- 15 minutes away, so grab groceries on the way in - our house is a cooks dream but some recommendations for eating out:
Breakfast - Life Bouy Cafe, St Helens; Swims East Coast Coffee, Scamander
Lunch - Lobster Shack, Bicheno; Iron House Brewery, Four Mile Creek
Dinner - Wharf Bar & Kitchen, St Helens; Raida, St Helens; St Mary’s Pub (more casual)

neighborhood_overview:
This house is located in Sandy Bay, Tasmania, Australia.

Sandy Bay is well regarded as one of Tasmania's most premiere suburbs with easy access to Hobart's CBD and world-famous Salamanca, it is home to Nutgrove Beach, Wrest Point Casino and great local shopping, trendy cafes and excellent schools.

Sandy Bay follows the Derwent river, from the outskirts of Hobart city, South, as far South as Taroona (made famous by Princess Mary of Denmark). Sandy Bay is the home of the University of Tasmania and Wrest Point Casino and is only a few minutes drive from Hobart CBD. Properties in this area often have magnificent views of the Derwent river.

The suburb has its own shopping village where you will find a Coles and Woolworths as well as a selection of smaller shops, including a great butcher and bakery. All the major banks have branches in the village and there is also a post office. There are a selection of excellent cafes, bars and restaurants to choose from.

description:
A Tiny Home in the leafy surrounds of Leslie Vale, just 20-minutes south of Hobart, the city capital of Tasmania.

neighborhood_overview:
Alonnah is a rural locality on Bruny Island in the local government area (LGA) of Kingborough in the Hobart LGA region of Tasmania. The locality is about 60 kilometres (37 mi) south (by ferry) of the town of Kingston. The 2021 census recorded a population of 164 for Alonnah.[1]

It is a small township on the western side of Bruny Island, facing the D'Entrecasteaux Channel.

Alonnah is the main location in Bruny Island for government facilities, including post office, police station, primary school, internet centre, community library, pharmacy, and health centre with nurses, a visiting doctor, physiotherapist, and other health practitioners. There is also a museum located in the court house, Bruny Hotel, and a small general store.

The Alonnah Dray track (also known as Sheepwash track) is an easy walking track of historical value, beginning at Alonnah jetty.

description: Home of the Blue Derby Mountain Bike Trails. Get back to the basics with good old fashioned country hospitality. neighborhood_overview:
The Dorset Hotel, is one of Derby's most convenient accommodation options, located right in the heart of Derby. Our onsite pub offers a fun friendly atmosphere with great food and features some of Tassie's best craft beers, wines and spirits.

The River Trail, which starts from our Beer Garden, takes you along the banks of the Ringarooma river, providing direct access to the suspension bridge (which takes you across the river to the Lake Trail and Wochya-Upta), past the Pump track and on to the Blue Derby Trailhead. host_about:
I love Tassie and have recently been lucky enough to acquire Dorset Hotel in Derby.  I have been running a popular and well established pub and accommodation on Bruny Island for the past 10 plus years and decided to branch out to other wonderful regional parts of Tasmania.

The original Dorset Hotel was a single story weather board building, it was replaced by the current building in 1911 and withstood the flood that destroyed much of the town in 1929. The pub has a photo wall describing the town’s rich tin mining history and the devastating effect of the 1929 flood.

The pub has been extensively renovated. We have put in a beer garden that seats 50 and installed a commercial kitchen. The bar and dining rooms have been painted and refurnished. We began serving meals in May 2018. The pub currently offers 10 newly renovated rooms, brand new shared bathrooms, and a breakfast room. The new roof is on and the pub exterior has now been re-painted.

Walk a short distance down Ardyn st to Lake Rosebery; Look up to the summit of Mt Murchison, immerse yourself at the lakes edge . Admire the Beech, Myrtle and Eucalypt forest or the flowers of the Trigger plant or Flax Lilly. Look out for fish, Platypus, Echidnas, Wallabies and bird life.

The 1924 Wee Georgie Wood steam engine will be running past Tullah TrackSide on scheduled weekends, taking you back to a bygone era.

Don't forget out and explore more of the Tarkine takayna region on Tullah's doorstep!
host_about:
Hi I'm Darren!  

I enjoy spending time on the West Coast and in particular the  takayna/Tarkine Wilderness area of Tasmania.   

It is here I am privileged to host ‘Tullah HideAway & Tullah TrackSide’ holiday accommodation.   

I believe long term industries including tourism, which nurture this unique environment should be cherished.  Traditional industries including mining and forestry are essential but need to adapt to modern sustainable practices which preserve the west coasts natural assets.  We cannot forget nor degrade the value of the natural environment.  The takayna/Tarkine wilderness area exemplifies this natural asset.  It inherently maintains biodiversity, clean air & water, while helping to mitigate climate change and harbours as yet undiscovered pharmaceuticals.  Takayna/Tarkine provides a wealth of opportunity for tourism and sporting pursuits supporting long term sustainable employment....it is these things for which we are guardians for future generations.

I Cherish time with my family, children & friends.

Recreational pursuits include paddle boarding, kayaking, bushwalking, trail running, politics, vegetable gardening and bush regeneration.  

I'm committed to living sustainably.  Including how and where I source food (preferably home grown or local), manufactured products,  transport, housing & energy choices.   Philanthropic & political choices are essential to these choices.

I work in health care where I believe all should have equal access to care independent of their financial means, faith or social standing.

neighborhood_overview:

Just 6km from the CBD, it is a short drive or ferry ride across the river. Bellerive has a major shopping centre within 2km, as well as restaurants, cafes and take aways.

name: 1 Seaview
description: Sun filled home with beautiful views of Southport Bay, Bruny Island and bush land.  One, two or three bedroom access depending on beds required, number of people booked.  A second bathroom is available when booked for two or more couples.  Located at the end of a quiet street and just a short walk to the beach, The town of Southport is a great base to explore Hastings Caves and thermal pool,  Cockle Creek, Ida Bay and Roaring Beach.  It’s also a popular spot for fishing, boating and kayaking!
neighborhood_overview:
Our house is located on a hill, two blocks back from the beach and at the end of a quiet street with lovely water views.
Beside our house is bush land and you will find lots of native wildlife hopping around the lawn during dusk and dawn.
Southport is a small community with local residents, we ask that you respect our neighbours please.
There are some great surf beaches, hiking trails, jetty fishing and Hastings Caves nearby.
Phone reception is limited, Optus tends to give best reception. There is wifi available at the property.
Shopping is limited to the Southport shop, offering only basic items, therefore it’s best to bring your own supplies. The closest supermarket is an IGA in Dover, a small town you pass through. The Southport Tavern serve a classic pub meal of an evening if you would like to dine out.
host_about: We built our holiday home in 2009 and our family have enjoyed many a weekend and school holidays spent in Southport, swimming, fishing and kayaking in the bay.  Tasmania really is one of the most beautiful places in the world!  My day job is a ‘Travel Advisor’ so we of course love to explore new places too, this means we can share our little slice of paradise with others and we hope you enjoy it as much as we do!

The cottage comfortably accommodates four guests with a master bedroom and a loft, (accessed by a steep ladder). Located in South Hobart, it’s a short walk to local shops and a scenic stroll along the Rivulet Track takes you to the CBD. neighborhood_overview:
Alonnah is a rural locality on Bruny Island in the local government area (LGA) of Kingborough in the Hobart LGA region of Tasmania. The locality is about 60 kilometres (37 mi) south (by ferry) of the town of Kingston. The 2021 census recorded a population of 164 for Alonnah.[1]

It is a small township on the western side of Bruny Island, facing the D'Entrecasteaux Channel.

Alonnah is the main location in Bruny Island for government facilities, including post office, police station, primary school, internet centre, community library, pharmacy, and health centre with nurses, a visiting doctor, physiotherapist, and other health practitioners. There is also a museum located in the court house, Bruny Hotel, and a small general store.

The Alonnah Dray track (also known as Sheepwash track) is an easy walking track of historical value, beginning at Alonnah jetty.

A suburb traditionally known as an industrial suburb, Invermay now enjoys a new and funky lease on life. Although there is still some commerce peppered throughout the suburb, the gorgeous weatherboard cottages are now sought after and are lovingly being restored back to their former glory!

There are numerous eateries, bars and takeaways nearby, as well as a Kmart, a Coles supermarket, newsagency, chemist, bakery and liquor outlet! Nearby restaurants and eateries of note are Me Wah Chinese restaurant and Café Blue. Falmouth is a small township on a headland on the East Coast of Tasmania. There are no shops, the closest store is 10km away. Approximately half way between St Helens and Bicheno, Falmouth is an ideal location for exploring the surrounding East Coast, or just kicking back and relaxing.
There is a beautiful beach of white sand that stretches for 10km and a tidal lagoon. At the top end of the lagoon you will find the Winifred Curtis Reserve which has an abundance of bird life.
The fishing is great in the area, plus there are lots of choices for swimming, surfing, wind surfing, kayaking or beach combing!
Not far away is the Douglas Apsley National Park, Freycinet National Park, Bay of Fires, Binalong Bay and the Blue Tiers, or head up the St Marys Pass to St Patrick's Head and the South Sister for a great climb!

- Lake Gordon and Lake Pedder are one of the best and most stunning attractions, great for short walks beside the lake.
- Lake Meadowbank is a popular fishing spot managed by the Inland Fisheries Service with brown trout, rainbow trout, and many more.
- Mount Field National Park often known as "the park for of all seasons" is a stunning natural flora that offers an ever-changing view as you climb to higher altitudes
- Styx Tall Trees, or giant ash trees, are a conservation area measuring over 90 meters in height, with girths that make them among the world's largest and tallest trees.
- Possum Shed Cafe, Waterfalls Cafe and Gallery, The Agrarian Kitchen, and Ouse Roadhouse are just of the nearby

neighborhood_overview: Low Head  is a beautiful coastal area of Tasmania where the Tamar River enters the ocean, only 40 minutes from Launceston.  Popular as a holiday destination since the 1870s, it is a quiet beachside community that offers several sheltered sandy beaches and a long expanse of ocean beach. The Low Head lighthouse, the convict built historic Pilot Station, and maritime museum are in walking distance. The area has over 70km of bike trails (Mt George and Tippogore Hills), and is surrounded by vineyards, orchards and berry farms. For those interested in diving, the waters feature abundant marine life including soft corals and sea horses. The depth in the Tamar Estuary is up to 45 metres and wreck diving is available.

neighborhood_overview:
The stunning coastal town of Devonport is like the welcoming gateway to the beautiful northwest region of Tasmania. Tucked between rolling hills and the crystal-clear waters of Bass Strait, it's a top spot for explorers. The town's got that warm and inviting feel, and there's a lot to see and do.

You can't miss the breathtaking coastline with its jaw-dropping ocean views. Take a leisurely stroll, have a picnic, or dive into some water-based fun at iconic spots like Coles Beach and the picturesque Bluff Beach. Don't forget to snap a pic with the eye-catching Mersey Bluff Lighthouse – it's a real local favourite. Check out the iconic ‘Spirit of the Sea Statue’ while on your journey.

Devonport's got a deep maritime history, and its port is a big deal for Tassie's trade and commerce. If you're into all things maritime, the Bass Strait Maritime Centre is a must-visit. You'll find a treasure trove of maritime goodies, from old artefacts to interactive exhibits.

It is only a 400metre walk to the town centre where you will enjoy the cafes, restaurants, shops, cinemas, clubs and pubs. The cottage has 3 bedrooms, 2 bathrooms, full kitchen, dining, two living areas, laundry, two verandas to capture the views and courtyard with a large picnic table setting to relax.
neighborhood_overview:
Centrally located in the CBD of Devonport. Mersey River Cottage is 400metres to the shops, cafe and restaurants. It has panoramic views of the ocean and and the working Harbour. You will enoy sitting on one of the two decks to watch the Spirit of Tasmania dock and turn right in front of the cottage!!

In the Mall which is only two streets away contains many shops and boutique clothing stores plus there is a Cinema for entertainment.

It is walking distance to the foreshore which has a new play area for children and suspended walkway over the harbour to capture the views.

The Harbour Master Cafe which has just recently reopened and is a lovely spot to enjoy a relaxing breakfast or lunch...or just a coffee.

The Antique Emporium which is on Formby road is a must if you want to find a treasure or something to take home.

name: Mountain Explorer - perfect base for exploring
description:
The perfect base to explore the mountain regions of the Great Western Tiers and the Central Plateau of Tasmania, in the quiet town of Deloraine - Mountain Explorer will not disappoint.

Located a short 5 minute walking distance to the vibrant artisan town centre of Deloraine with and abundance of galleries, cafes, bakeries, restaurants and pubs.

This region is full of mountain walks, waterfalls, lakes and is perfectly located for an easy drive to the renowned Cradle Mountain National Park.
neighborhood_overview:
When it’s not in the grip of crafting, Deloraine is perfect for a spot of window shopping - its streets are lined with Georgian and Victorian shopfronts full of art, antiques and crafts.

Set out on foot along the Great Western Tiers Sculpture Trail around the town and along the river to see the works of Tasmanian artists, while the short kooparoona niara cultural trail unveils native plantings, bush tucker and artworks inspired by Tasmanian Aboriginal culture.

Deloraine is surrounded by some of Tasmania’s most productive farmland, and it's less a 10min drive from Deloraine to the little town of Elizabeth Town, which satisfies even big appetites. Find a feast of Tasmanian fare at the Ashgrove Cheese Dairy Door, Christmas Hills Raspberry Farm Café and Van Diemens Land Creamery.

Set beneath the escarpment of the Great Western Tiers, Deloraine is a good base from which to explore Cradle Mountain, Mole Creek, Liffey Falls and the Central Highlands.

neighborhood_overview:
Bridport is a one-hour (85km) scenic drive northeast of Launceston. You will love this well-serviced coastal village, surrounded by bushland reserves with its 11km circuit of scenic walking tracks. It's a popular seaside holiday haven with sun, sand and amazing skies, protected family-friendly beaches and a surf beach nearby. You'll appreciate the ever-changing landscape from the picture windows of your accommodation, as the fishing boats and ferry come and go while the tide ebbs and flows.

There are several attractive beaches, waterfront parks, walkways, cafes, hotels, a gin distillery in Bridport. The Bridport region also has many attractions from world-class Golf courses, the highly popular Blue Derby Mountain Bike Trails, the Bridestowe Lavender Farm, several fine vineyards. Historic towns of Legerwood, Scottsdale and Branxholme are also worth visiting while you're in the region. (See also Getting Around)

description:
Bespoke built wooden cottage with its quirky sliding iron roof is a true gem that promises an unforgettable stay.

The rustic interior, with old brick inglenook fireplace immediately catching your eye. Weathered bricks and rough saw timber walls create an atmosphere of warmth and intimacy.

An inulgent experience, a copper bath, mounted on rails, moves across the secluded deck, a memorable experience and stay in Hobart.
host_about:
I am Australian and have lived in the UK and Japan. My husband, Dermot, grew up in Ireland and has lived in the Ireland, UK and now Australia. We love meeting people, having a laugh, fresh air, walking and cycling, beautiful scenery and great food and wine --- Tasmania! We are both involved in running our Airbnb apartments, having expanded since our initial listing in 2012. 

My career has been in healthcare (mainly midwifery) and my husband's in finance. We are keen travellers, especially if it involves sailing. We have four children keeping us busy, so we are also good at keeping ourselves to ourselves, as appropriate.

We have taken on the challenge of looking after this 19th century house and property, the Anglican Bishop's residence from the 1840s till recently, and spend a lot of time restoring and maintaining it. I am particularly fond of searching for interesting pieces of forgotten furniture, making/growing things and preserving and baking. Dermot is particularly mad about introducing technology to everyday activities such as mowing the lawn - watch out for Monty our robotic lawnmower dodging the local wildlife of rabbits, pademelons & kookaburras.

We were drawn to Airbnb as we get to know a little about our house guests and vice versa. Also, we find that it connects us with people who are considerate and pleasant which is important!

name: Bruny Shearers Quarters
description: Stay at the award-winning, John Wardle designed Shearers Quarters. Available for exclusive stays, allow nature to soothe your body and soul without sacrificing creature comforts. Gaze out over Storm Bay on pristine North Bruny Island, Tasmania, The land of the Nuenonne People, the traditional custodians of this land. neighborhood_overview:

Additionally, the owners have shown their commitment to sustainable farming by placing over a third of the property in reserve through a conservation covenant.

The native wildlife is abundant with frequent sightings of
Forty-spotted pardalote (Tasmania’s rarest bird)
Swift parrot (very rare)
Oyster catchers
Echidnas
Quolls
Sea Eagles
Wedgetail Eagles
Wallabies
And many more!

description: A scenic 1hr drive from Hobart, The Chalet (featured in Australian Traveller magazine 2024) is perched above a tennis court with a traditional Finnish sauna with cold shower on a private 5-acre property overlooking the rolling hills of Spring Beach. Spring Beach is a 5 min drive from the coastal township of Orford where you find a number of cafes, an IGA, pub with bottle shop, post office, newsagent golf club, bowls club, library, beaches and parks.

Spring Beach is a scenic 1 hour drive from Hobart, 40 min drive from historic Richmond, 40 min drive from Sorell, 45 mins to Swansea and 1.5 hours to Freycinet National Park/Wineglass Bay. The Maria Island ferry terminal in Triabunna is only a 10 min drive from the property.

name: First Light Tasmania (Cabin)
description: First Light Tasmania (Cabin) is a newly renovate modern self- contained timber & rammed earth cabin perched on a headland overlooking the Tasman Sea. Enjoy the panoramic, ever-changing views of the ocean, local wildlife, resident sea eagles & whales from your hot jacuzzi while enjoying the secluded in the privacy of 5 acres of beautiful coastal heathland. Beautiful starry night skies & amazing sunrises make it a special piece of paradise.
neighborhood_overview:
Guests have access to Templestowe Beach via a short 200 metre walk through the national park. Or a 2 min drive to the south side will take you to magnificent Denison beach which goes all the way to Bicheno. (11 km for the energetic). This is where our local penguins come in on sunset each evening.
Easy rock walks are available from the edge of the property for you to enjoy the rock pools and lichen covered rocks or just relax on.
North beach is dogs on lead and south beach is dogs off lead.

If you can drag yourself away from FIRST LIGHT, one of Tasmania’s most plentiful regions is on your doorstep. Take your pick of picturesque vineyards serving world-class cool climate wines; excellent bush walks and delicious local fresh seafood.

Our closest township Bicheno is a special little seaside town worth wandering, with its blowhole, lookout, cafes and fascinating history, not to mention those entertaining resident penguins.

neighborhood_overview:
Bellerive is a suburb of the City of Clarence, part of the greater Hobart area, Tasmania, Australia. It stretches from Kangaroo Bay where it borders Rosny Park, around the curved shoreline of Bellerive Esplanade to Kangaroo Bluff, then down to Bellerive Beach and east to Second Bluff, where Bellerive borders Howrah. To the north Bellerive is bordered by the small foothills of Waverly Flora Park.

The area around Bellerive Quay and the boardwalk has a quaint village feel, with many historical homes and buildings in the area, some of which date from the early 19th century. The old Bellerive Post Office, which was built in 1897, now houses both the Sound Preservation Museum and the Genealogical Society of Tasmania. At the point of Kangaroo Bluff is the 19th century British fortress known as Kangaroo Battery (built 1885) which is now a public park.

neighborhood_overview: Situated on Tasmania’s north coast where the Mersey River meets Bass Strait, the city of  Devonport has much to offer visitors, both culturally and historically. Visit The Bass Strait Maritime Centre to learn more about the intriguing maritime history of the city through an extensive collection of objects, models, photographs and exhibits which retell the exciting adventures of early explorers and shipwrecks. Art lovers can immerse themselves in Tasmanian art at the Devonport Regional Gallery, offering a collection of fine and decorative art and crafts, with a predominant focus on 20th-century glass, ceramics and woodcraft.  Or learn about the traditional lifestyle of Tasmanian Aboriginal people at the Tiagarra Aboriginal Culture Centre and Museum, which displays petroglyphs and designs in rock. For those who enjoy getting active, there are numerous walking and cycling tracks in the city, with water sports such as sailing, kayaking, rowing and fishing also popular pursuits. Alternative

name: Beautiful country home in the Derwent Valley
description: Indulge in country living in this idyllic four-bedroom home in picturesque New Norfolk, just a 35 minute drive north-west of Hobart. neighborhood_overview:
Located in a quiet residential street, the home is close to Tynwald Park and the beautiful Derwent Cliffs Walk.

New Norfolk is a historical town with vast history to discover. Tasmania’s third oldest settlement, the town is home to Australia’s oldest Anglican Church, St Matthews, and one of the country’s oldest pubs, The Bush Inn which has been licensed since 1825. Visit Willow Court, a former Military Hospital that became Australia’s oldest institution for people with mental illness.

For antique enthusiasts, New Norfolk is known for its eclectic antique stores, and enjoy the delicious fresh local produce like fresh trout locally grown and produced at the Salmon Ponds from cafes and restaurants.

In 2013 I became a Super Host. I pride myself in providing amazing accomodation!

It's warm and inviting, has individual ecclectic style whilst also having all the basics, dishwasher, heat pump, record player, full kitchen and a pantry of staples! There is a full laundry.

A five minute drive and you can be enjoying the beauty of East Beach or the more sheltered Lagoon Beach.

Lots of fabulous mountain bike tracks to explore! When you finish you can visit one or many wineries on either side of the Tamar River.

name: South Hobart Haven
description:
Recover and rest in this secluded Tasmanian haven. Immerse yourself in the gaze of the forested foothills of Hobart's mountain - kunanyi.

And being only 11 minutes drive from Hobart, make this your getaway base camp.

Experience the sense of a bush escape close to the city and it's stories.

Settled in it's native habitat, South Hobart Haven is self-contained, offering privacy and sunny, step-free access.

We look forward to welcoming you for this part of your Tasmanian adventure.
neighborhood_overview:
Where to start? South Hobart is probably best known for the Cascade Brewery - Australia's oldest surviving brewery. You may wish to take a brewery tour or enjoy the visitors centre's food and drink offerings.

There's also the 'Female Factory' whose ruins have been transformed into an interpretive visitor experience exploring the sobering reality of life for females in the formative years of the colony of Hobart.

Beyond this, South Hobart offers a tranquil and well utilised walking/cycling trail along the Hobart Rivulet. Access to this trail begins at Cascade Gardens immediately next to the brewery.

Turning back towards the mountain, let's just say there's plenty of options for walking and mountain biking. A nearby formalised walking trail is called the Cascade Walking Track and is a good introduction to the scope of landform and vegetaion making up the foothills of kunanyi/ Mt Wellington. It's about a 45 minute walk. Give it a go!

For the mou

name: Riverside Retreat in Orford
description:
Slow down on Tasmania’s East Coast in family friendly Orford, on the mouth of the Prosser River.

Sleeping up to 9 people, the 3 bedroom, 2 bathroom home has been renovated with comfort and connection in mind, featuring light, open spaces, and large bedrooms.

With views of the Prosser River, the home, just an hour’s drive from Hobart, is perfect for a large family or group to share.

Walking distance to beaches to swim, surf, and explore all around Tassie’s beautiful, rugged East Coast.
neighborhood_overview:
Hobart is an easy and scenic one-hour drive from Orford. The seaside village has lots of conveniences: an IGA supermarket, cafes such as Wattlebanks and Elly’s, a pizzeria, a bottle shop, and pubs.

Enjoy the 2km cliff-side walking track to Shelly Beach, offering beautiful coastal views of Spring Bay, Mercury Passage, and Maria Island National Park.

Take a short ferry to Maria Island National Park from Triabunna, just a 10 minute drive from the property.

Abundant bird and wildlife, there are cycling tracks and hiking trails nearby for all levels, and you may be lucky to see dolphins and whales.

Lots of historical experiences, such as a visit to the old sandstone quarry and the Convict Trail.

By car, explore areas of Swansea, Coles Bay, and the Freycinet Peninsula, and discover wineries, distilleries, and home-grown produce from the East Coast regions.
