name: The Lookout House at Pirates Bay
description:
Find yourself in one of Tasmania’s most pristine and naturally beautiful regions, just
one hour’s drive from Hobart.

With elevated views of the stunning Pirates Bay, Lookout House in Eaglehawk Neck offers seclusion, comfort, and expansive views in a modern eco-home nestled into the bush. Travellers can walk to the beach or easily access local attractions including Port Arthur, Tessellated Pavement, Devil’s Kitchen and Tasman Arch.
neighborhood_overview:
Eaglehawk Neck is a small coastal town in southeast Tasmania, just one hour’s drive from the capital, Hobart. Built around a narrow bar of land, Eaglehawk Neck connects Tasman Peninsula and Forestier Peninsula.

Discover history and nature with a trip to the historical site of Port Arthur, access the 3 Capes Track in Tasman National Park, explore the geological feature, Tessellated Pavements, the Blowhole, Devil’s Kitchen, famous surfing beaches, scenic walking trails and incredible restaurants, wineries and produce.

Some favourites to try are McHenry’s Distillery and Brewery, Bangor Vineyard Shed and Hellfire Distillery. For produce try the Raspberry Farm in Koonya for farm-to-table jams or Eaglehawk Neck & Bream Creek Markets for artisan products. Cubed Espresso at Pirate Bay lookout also makes great coffee and banana bread!

Keep an eye out for the abundance of wildlife in the region including Pademelons, Echidnas, Wombats, Penguins and birdlife.

neighborhood_overview:
The stunning coastal town of Devonport is like the welcoming gateway to the beautiful northwest region of Tasmania. Tucked between rolling hills and the crystal-clear waters of Bass Strait, it's a top spot for explorers. The town's got that warm and inviting feel, and there's a lot to see and do.

You can't miss the breathtaking coastline with its jaw-dropping ocean views. Take a leisurely stroll, have a picnic, or dive into some water-based fun at iconic spots like Coles Beach and the picturesque Bluff Beach. Don't forget to snap a pic with the eye-catching Mersey Bluff Lighthouse – it's a real local favourite. Check out the iconic ‘Spirit of the Sea Statue’ while on your journey.

Devonport's got a deep maritime history, and its port is a big deal for Tassie's trade and commerce. If you're into all things maritime, the Bass Strait Maritime Centre is a must-visit. You'll find a treasure trove of maritime goodies, from old artefacts to interactive exhibits.

Enjoy a short stroll to Sandy Bay beach, the yacht club, and the vibrant shopping strip near the University. Return to a warm, welcoming house featuring a private courtyard and sunny native gardens. Karkalla Terrace offers a convenient base for couples, families, or small groups, making it the perfect home away from home.

Nearby, you can enjoy a leisurely stroll to Sandy Bay shops, beaches, yacht club, casino, and through Battery Point to Salamanca and Hobart City Centre. For a taste of history, wander through Battery Point’s streets or take on the challenge of Nanny Goat or Billy Goat Lanes, immersing yourself in the area's rich heritage with its beautiful churches, gardens, and picturesque views.

name: The Clocktower—Serene Stay at Herons Rise Vineyard
description: Nestled amid 12 acres of picturesque gardens within the Heron’s Wine vineyard estate, 'The Clocktower' combines country-style comfort with rural tranquillity and proximity to a host of attractions. Surrounded by manicured gardens, this cottage accommodates up to four guests and features light-filled living and dining rooms, ocean views, and a cosy fireplace. Just 30 minutes from Hobart, it’s only two minutes from the dreamy seaside village of Kettering and the Bruny Island Ferry.
neighborhood_overview:
Just 30 minutes from Hobart and a world away from stress, Herons Vineyard is located a mere 1.5 km from the enchanting seaside village of Kettering. Not only does Kettering offer the only ferry service to Bruny Island, but it’s also a delightful destination in itself.

Enjoy alfresco dining with stunning views of the Kettering Marina at Seawall Cafe and The Oyster Cove Inn. For a fabulous brew, head to the Bruny Island Gateway Cafe at the end of Ferry Road, which transforms into an Asian Fusion haven from 4-9 pm. Don’t miss the roving pizza van on Friday and Saturday nights!

Indulge in exquisite chocolates from a local chocolatier at Nutpatch Chocolate Shop, and savour a cup of coffee at the boutique Steamhouse Coffee Shop, a favourite among locals.

The Bruny Island ferry departs regularly and takes about 20 minutes. Bruny Island is famous for its cheeses, wine, whiskey, seafood, stunning scenery, coastline, walks, and native wildlife, including wallabie

description: Alfred Basil Crisp, one of Alfred’s sons, was a keen amateur cyclist in the Golden Age of the bicycle. name: Explore South Hobart Village from an 1855 Cottage
description: Channel the ambience of Hobart’s colonial past while living in comfort at this reimagined c1855 heritage cottage with shops, buses and humming eateries on your doorstep, and Hobart’s CBD attractions all within walking distance. Small but thoughtfully appointed, it features an open-plan living and dining space warmed by a cosy wood fireplace, a well-equipped kitchen, private covered terrace and rear lawn with views to Mount Wellington.
neighborhood_overview:
Set between the Hobart CBD and the Cascade Brewery and historic Cascade Female Factory, this idyllic location is an entity in itself where you can pop next door to the famous Hill Street Grocers and sample or take home some of Tasmania’s finest fresh produce, step across the road to the trendy Bear With Me Café or stroll to shopping, city buses and humming eateries within a couple of minutes.

The popular Rivulet Track is only a two minute stroll away where you can walk through parkland by the water (keep an eye out for the native Paddymelons) to Cascade Gardens, Cascade Brewery and the historic Cascade Female Factory as well as the attractions in the Hobart CBD within 20 minutes in either direction. If you’re not up for a walk, buses stop just metres from the doorstep running regularly to both destinations and it’s only a few minutes’ drive either way by car.

name: The Outlook on Mount Louis - 1 Bedroom
description:
The Outlook on Mount Louis - a haven and home for nature lovers, aurora chasers and appreciators of a quieter place.

This luxurious 1-bedroom modernist inspired architecturally designed building, sits beautifully on Mount Louis in the Tinderbox Hills. Overlooking a canopy of tall eucalyptus trees are the magical views of the Derwent and South Arm Peninsula to Iron Pot Lighthouse and beyond. This is where you can have a bird’s eye view of the exciting finish to the Sydney- Hobart yacht race!
neighborhood_overview:
Blackmans Bay is about 10 minutes’ drive and is the closest town for essential services and eateries. Here, you will find beach front restaurants including pizza, curries and classic fish and chips. The secluded white sandy beach is a quiet place to relax and enjoy a picnic or just chill for a while.

Bayview Market in Opel drive is a crescent of shops that has a bakery, pharmacy, post office, bottle shop, Hill Street Grocer supermarket, hairdresser, and a medical practice.

Kingston Beach has several waterfront cafes and restaurants. Check out Ebb+Flo and Robbie Browns and The Salty Dog Pub across the road. The bustling beach activity is shared with dog walkers and joggers, while kayakers, swimmers and stand-up paddle boarders share the waves. Alum Cliffs Track starts at the northern end of the beach through a beautiful coastal trail that winds all the way to the Taroona foreshore. It’s a moderately difficult 8km return track.

host_about:
Hello 
I am Stefan.  I have travelled the world as a scientist studying glaciers and climate change in Antarctica and other cool places. I am currently a science consultant at Glaciology Tasmania.

Over the past 5 years I have settled in beautiful Hobart, Tasmania. I still have dreams one of them is to build a sustainable living place in the centre of Hobart. A proof of concept and a kind of demonstrating that city living can be sustainable, possibly off-grid. I do hope over the next years to complete the first stage - a studio in the back of my property with an aquaponic system doubling as biotope and swimming pool. The second stage then will enlarge the current main house and hopefully includes a large garage underneath the house. The concept is to utilize BIPV - Building Integrated PhotoVoltaic (Solar) to generate my own electricity for battery storage (saltwater batteries) as well as for heat generation/storage for hydronic heating as well as hot water.

Your Stay at Villa Kunterbunt will help make this sustainable living in the centre of Hobart become reality and I look forward to answering any question you may have. I am also always keen to hear about ideas of others.

If I am not designing/building my own house I am a single full-time dad, exploring the great outdoors of Tasmania with my son and friends. I also still do some science work and lots of science outreach activities.

host_about:
Hi I'm Darren!  

I enjoy spending time on the West Coast and in particular the  takayna/Tarkine Wilderness area of Tasmania.   

It is here I am privileged to host ‘Tullah HideAway & Tullah TrackSide’ holiday accommodation.   

I believe long term industries including tourism, which nurture this unique environment should be cherished.  Traditional industries including mining and forestry are essential but need to adapt to modern sustainable practices which preserve the west coasts natural assets.  We cannot forget nor degrade the value of the natural environment.  The takayna/Tarkine wilderness area exemplifies this natural asset.  It inherently maintains biodiversity, clean air & water, while helping to mitigate climate change and harbours as yet undiscovered pharmaceuticals.  Takayna/Tarkine provides a wealth of opportunity for tourism and sporting pursuits supporting long term sustainable employment....it is these things for which we are guardians for future generations.

I Cherish time with my family, children & friends.

Recreational pursuits include paddle boarding, kayaking, bushwalking, trail running, politics, vegetable gardening and bush regeneration.  

I'm committed to living sustainably.  Including how and where I source food (preferably home grown or local), manufactured products,  transport, housing & energy choices.   Philanthropic & political choices are essential to these choices.

I work in health care where I believe all should have equal access to care independent of their financial means, faith or social standing.

name: Pod House at Pirates Bay
description:
Escape to one of Tasmania’s most breathtaking regions, just an hour from Hobart. With elevated views of the stunning Pirates Bay, Pod House in Eaglehawk Neck offers seclusion, star gazing, expansive sea views all in a spacious and modern home featuring three bedrooms and sleeping up to five guests.

Located in easy access to local attractions including Port Arthur, Tessellated Pavement, Devil’s Kitchen and Tasman National Park this is the perfect getaway for friends and family alike.
neighborhood_overview:
Located on Tasmania’s stunning Tasman Peninsula a little over an hour away from Hobart’s CBD, Eaglehawk Neck is a breathtaking coastal retreat known for its rugged beauty, rich history, and incredible natural wonders. This peaceful seaside community is the perfect getaway for nature lovers, adventure seekers, and history buffs.

Just minutes from your stay, you’ll find some of Tasmania’s most iconic geological formations such as the Tessellated Pavement – Best viewed at sunrise or sunset! Tasman Arch & Devil’s Kitchen – only a 5 minute drive away and the Blowhole.

Steeped in history and character, this beautifully preserved Georgian town offers a unique glimpse into colonial Australia — with cobbled laneways, convict-built architecture, and a relaxed village atmosphere.
